### Preface

The Maintenance Manual is mainly designed for the development of "Tang EV" series vehicles, which collects the main technical data of "Tang EV" vehicles, such as new energy, chassis, vehicle body and low-voltage electrical equipment, and includes removal and installation, disassembly and assembly, adjustment, overhaul and fault diagnosis. Careful reading and strict implementation of the regulations can help you master the methods of fault diagnosis, troubleshooting, maintenance and repair of this model, so as to ensure that the repaired vehicle is in the best working condition and achieves ideal power, economy and comfort.

### 1.1.1.1 Description

1. The maintenance process consists of the following:

a. Diagnosis.
b. Removal/installation, replacement, disassembly/assembly, inspection and adjustment.
c. Final inspection.

2. Although the following are omitted in this manual, they must be performed:

a. The vehicle should be lifted up with a jack or lift only.
b. All removed parts need to be cleaned.
c. Visual inspection is required before and after any work.
d. Inspection and road test should be conducted upon completion of maintenance.

### 1.1.1.2 Terms and definitions

1. Tightening torque (unit: N•m) the standard value range of which is the standard values of tightening torques to be applied for installing some fasteners, such as bolts and nuts
2. Standard value the criterion for parts quality judgment or assembly inspection, or the correction and adjustment value of related parts or assembly, expressed in the form of a range
3. Limit value the criterion for parts quality judgment or assembly inspection, which also indicates the maximum or minimum value of any parts or assembly that meets the functional or strength requirements

### 1.1.1.3 Unit

1. The international system of units (SI) is adopted in this manual. For example: Tightening torque: 9±1N•m

2. List of common units:

### 1.1.1.4 Maintenance procedure

1. This manual provides illustrations for key steps and operations in the maintenance procedure, describes them in detail, and lists the operation methods, reference data and precautions.

2. The procedure instructions are described in the following order:

a. Illustrations indicate "what to do" and "where to do".
b. Titles of operation steps indicate "what to do".
c. Contents of operation steps explain "how to complete the task" and provide help information such as "WARNING", "CAUTION" and "REMINDER".

### 1.2.1.1 Warnings, notices and tips

1. WARNING: Reminds you of potential personal injuries to yourself or others.
2. CAUTION: Reminds you of potential damage to the parts or vehicle under maintenance.
3. Tips: Reminds you of auxiliary information that may be helpful to maintenance operations.

### 1.2.2.1 Safety instructions for maintenance of electric vehicle

1. Electrical appliances on the electric vehicle are divided into low-voltage and high-voltage electrical appliances. The low-voltage electrical appliance system includes audio & entertainment, lighting, power windows, wiper and washer system, instrument cluster, sunroof, centre control system, power seats, airbags, horns and on-board power supply, while the high-voltage electrical appliance system includes high voltage battery, charging and distribution assembly, front drive electric powertrain, rear drive electric powertrain, electric compressor assembly, front PTC driver assembly, PTC heater core, integrated AC/DC charging vehicle socket sub-assembly and high-voltage wiring harnesses.

A Warning:
• All high-voltage wiring harnesses and connectors are in orange color, and warning labels are provided on all high-voltage components. Never touch these wiring harnesses and components at will. To avoid electric shock, do not touch any exposed or damaged cable on the vehicle before disconnecting the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and disabling the high voltage power.

### 1.2.2.2 Safety measures for maintenance of electric vehicle

1. Insulating protective articles

a. Insulating protective clothing b. Insulated shoes.
c. Safety goggles
d. Insulated gloves.
e. Protective mask.

A Warning: Maintenance personnel must wear insulating protective articles before operation.

2. Insulating tools a. Insulating foot pad b. Insulating tool kit

A Warning: Maintenance personnel must wear insulating protective articles before operation.

3. Maintenance site

a. High-voltage warning sign
b. Carbon dioxide fire extinguisher
c. Warning line
d. Special ground wire for maintenance station

！ Warning:

Take isolation measures prior to maintenance, adopt warning lines for isolation, and set up high-voltage warning signs to warn irrelevant personnel to stay away from the maintenance area and avoid safety accidents.
Before repairing any high-voltage equipment, connect the ground wire for the vehicle body to the ground wire of the special maintenance station for electric vehicles.
Keep the working environment clean, well-ventilated and away from liquids and inflammables.

### 1.2.2.3 Important warnings for disconnecting cathode of 12V battery (starter Fe battery)

A Warning: Unless otherwise stated in the operating procedures, make sure that the vehicle is in the "OFF" state and all electrical loads are turned off before starting the maintenance of any electrical component. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) if the tool or equipment is easy to touch any exposed live electrical terminal during operation. Violation against the above safety instructions may result in personal injury and/or vehicle damage.

### i Caution:

The operators must obtain High Voltage operation certificate from local authority before any operation to High volt Voltage parts and components, and technical certification from BYD AUTO shall only serves as a training qualified record.
Maintenance technicians must have received professional training before conducting maintenance and inspection of the high-voltage system.
All high-voltage wiring harnesses and connectors are in orange color, and warning labels are provided on all high-voltage components. Never touch these wiring harnesses and components at will.
Before conducting maintenance and inspection of the high-voltage system, be sure to take all safety measures, such as wearing insulating gloves to avoid electric shock.
Before using insulating gloves, be sure to check them for breakage, wear or other types of damage.
Before touching any exposed high-voltage terminal, be sure to wear insulating gloves and use testing equipment to confirm that the voltage of the terminal is 0 V.
Do not try to repair any failed wiring harness or connector of the high-voltage circuit, but replace the damaged high-voltage wiring harness or connector.
Do not carry metal objects such as scale when repairing the vehicle; otherwise, these objects may accidentally drop and cause a short circuit.
Wrap any high-voltage connector with insulating tape immediately after disconnecting or exposing it.
Tighten the bolts and nuts of high-voltage terminals to the specified torques. Insufficient or excessive torque may cause a failure.
Use the sign "WARNING: Do not touch high-voltage system" to inform other maintenance technicians that the high-voltage system is under inspection and/or maintenance.
After maintenance of the high-voltage system, check again to make sure that no parts or tools are left in the system and that high-voltage terminals are fastened and connectors are correctly connected.

### 1.2.2.5 Precautions for inspection and maintenance of front compartment

1. Unless otherwise stated, it is forbidden to start the vehicle during inspection and maintenance of the front compartment.

### i Caution:

When the "OK" indicator on the instrument cluster lights up, it means that the vehicle is powered on. It is necessary to make sure that the high-voltage power of the vehicle is disabled before starting work, in order to prevent causing injury to the maintenance personnel.

### 1.2.2.6 Precautions for inspection and maintenance of SRS

1. The following steps should be observed during airbag component operations (including indirect operations related to airbags):

a. Wait for at least 90s after disconnecting the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and then proceed with subsequent operations.
b. Do not impact or vibrate airbag components (especially the sensor) when removing or installing parts or repairing the sheet metal.
c. Be sure to remove the SRS ECU, airbag modules, clock spring, collision sensor and seat belts with pre-tensioning function in order to avoid heating damage during paint spraying.

### i Caution:

The SRS can also provide sufficient voltage for airbag deployment in a short time after the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) is disconnected. If any component of the SRS is repaired within 90s after the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) is disconnected, the SRS may be started and deployed, resulting in serious accidents.
Ensure that specified special tools and test equipment are used.
Place removed airbag components in a clean and dry area, and place the airbag module on a flat surface, with its front facing upwards. Do not place any objects on it.
Do not repair airbag components (SRS ECU, airbag module and clock spring and collision sensor).
After replacing airbag components, check for normal working of the warning light to ensure the normal function of the system.

### 1.2.2.7 Precautions for vehicle lifting and supporting positions

1. Important precautions for vehicle lifting

i Caution: Make sure that the vehicle is in the no-load state before jacking or lifting it. Do not jack or lift a loaded vehicle. Be careful when jacking and supporting the vehicle, and be sure to jack and support the vehicle at correct positions. The centre of gravity of the vehicle shifts during the removal of the powertrain or heavy components. Place a bracket under the other end of the vehicle for stabilising it.

### 2. Important precautions for using 4-post lift

i Caution:

Follow the safety procedures described in the lift manual.
Be careful not to damage tyres or wheels when driving to the lift position.
Use wheel chock blocks to stop wheels.

3. Important precautions for using 2-post lifts (double-post lift with rocker arm and doublepost gantry lift)

### i Caution:

Follow the safety procedures in the lift manual.
Use rocker arms with additional rubber support blocks.
Make sure that rubber pads or rocker arms do not touch the vehicle body.

4. Important precautions for using jacks and safety bases

### i Caution:

Always use wheel chock blocks when operating on the horizontal ground.
Use a safety base with additional rubber support blocks.
Place the jack and the safety base accurately at the designated positions under the vehicle.
Make sure that wheel chock blocks are placed in front of and behind rear wheels when jacking up front wheels.
Make sure that wheel chock blocks are placed in front of and behind front wheels when jacking up rear wheels.

### 1.2.2.8 Important warnings for road test

A Warning:
• Perform a road test on the vehicle on the premise of ensuring safety and complying with all traffic regulations. Do not try any operation that may endanger the control over the vehicle. Violation against the above safety instructions may result in personal injury and/or vehicle damage.

### 3. Part II: vehicle descriptor section (VDS)

a. The vehicle descriptor section (VDS) consists of vehicle type, vehicle body type, motor type/ vehicle length, drive type and wheelbase/number of axles, vehicle's technical characteristic parameters and check digit.

a. The vehicle identifier section (VIS) is an 8-digit code consisting of year, assembly plant and production sequence number information.

### 1.6.1.1 Acids and alkalis

1. Acids and alkalis are corrosive substances, such as sodium carbonate and sulfuric acid.

2. Acids and alkalis are irritant or erosive to eyes, skin, smell and throat, and they may cause burns to human body and damage ordinary protective clothing.
3. Avoid splashing acids and alkalis into eyes and onto skin and clothes. Wear appropriate protective clothing, gloves and goggles, and avoid inhaling the spray of them.
4. Flushing installations (e.g., eye rinsing bottles and soap) must be provided nearby for timely rescue in case of splashing events.
5. Provide signs indicating danger at eye-striking locations.

### 1.6.1.2 Airbag

1. Airbags are installed in the steering wheel, the dashboard in front of the front passenger seat and at other positions as the auxiliary safety system.
2. The airbag expander contains a high-energy propellant, which will produce extremely hightemperature gas when ignited.
3. This propellant is stored in a sealed airbag module and the gas will fill the entire airbag when the airbag deploys.
4. Avoid triggering the airbag during maintenance; otherwise, it will lead to a danger due to contact with the propellant. Wear full protective clothing when handling spilled substances after identifying a broken gas generator.
5. Wear goggles and gloves during maintenance after the airbag is normally deployed.
6. Deployed airbags should be disposed of in accordance with the relevant local laws and regulations.
7. After direct contact with gas derivatives, be sure to: a. Rinse the contact area thoroughly with clean water. b. Seek medical assistance as appropriate.
8. Operations to be performed during maintenance of airbags (For your safety, please wear protective articles as far as possible before performing the following operations. Be sure to power off the vehicle, disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and wait for 90s before removing the airbag). a. Store the airbag module in an upright state. b. Keep the airbag module dry during storage. c. When handling the airbag module, be careful not to touch the electrodes with your hands and keep the airbag as far away from your body as possible. d. Place the airbag module with its protective cover facing upwards. e. Carefully check whether the airbag module is damaged. f. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), wait for 90s, and stand on the side of the airbag module before installing it. g. Correct and maintain all equipment accurately. h. Be sure to wash hands after handling a deployed airbag.

### 9. Airbags operations to be avoided

a. Do not store flammable materials together with the airbag module and the gas generator.
b. Do not immerse the airbag assembly in water or contact it with other liquids.
c. Do not store the gas generator in an environment with a temperature higher than 80℃ or in a humid environment.
d. Do not store the airbag module upside down.
e Do not attempt to open the casing of the gas generator.
f. Do not expose the gas generator to open flame or heat source.
g. Do not place other items on the protective cover of the airbag module.
h. Do not use damaged airbag modules.
i. Do not touch the airbag module or gas generator within 10 min after the airbag module is deployed.
j. Do not use any electrical probe on the electrical circuit.

### 1.6.1.3 A/C refrigerant

1. Contact between A/C refrigerant and skin may cause frostbite.

2. Wear appropriate goggles and protective gloves.

3. If the skin or eyes come into contact with the refrigerant, rinse the contacted area with water immediately. In addition, rinse eyes with proper rinsing solution, and do not rub them. Seek medical assistance as appropriate.

4. A/C refrigerant - operations to be avoided

a. Do not store refrigerant in places with direct sunlight or heat sources.
b. Do not allow the refrigerant bottle to fall off.
c. Do not directly discharge the refrigerant into the atmosphere under any circumstance.
d. Do not mix refrigerants.

### 1. Important precautions for using adhesives/sealants

a. Before using adhesives/sealants, be sure to clean the surface of the part to be applied with adhesives/sealants and wipe it with special cleaning agent to avoid affecting the bonding effect.
b. When using sealant, do not allow the room-temperature curing sealant to enter the blind threaded hole; otherwise, the fastener will have a hydraulic locking effect during fastening, which will cause damage to the fastener and/or other parts and the fastener's failure in getting the correct clamping force during fastening, and make the sealant's sealing effect worse, thus leading to incorrect fastening of the fastener and loose or separated parts, resulting in serious damage to parts.

### 2. Health and safety

a. Materials adopted for adhesives/sealants contain hazardous substances, and long-term contact with it will cause acute and chronic poisoning, occupational diseases, skin diseases and other diseases.
b. During the application of adhesives/sealants, a ventilation device should be used to keep the workshop ventilated. Protective gloves, masks, protective clothing, etc. should be worn during operation. After work, it is required to wash hands carefully and keep the workshop clean, tidy and sanitary.
c. Wastes contaminated by waste rubber or solvent should be cleared away in time, and longterm accumulation of them is not allowed.
d. Adhesive/sealant products should be stored in a non-smoking area in general and should be kept clean when used. An applicator or container should be used for operation as far as possible.

### 3. Repair of adhesives/sealants

a. In the event of a vehicle failure or accident, it will generally lead to the deformation of vehicle body, cracking of steel plates, disconnection of solder joints, etc. Sometimes, it will also cause local damage to other assembled components such as the front/rear drive electric powertrain and the chassis, resulting in the stripping of and damage to some adhesive/ sealant products. During maintenance of the vehicle, adhesives with the same performance should be selected according to the material and functional requirements of the component concerned. The following table lists the adhesives/sealants that can be used in the process of vehicle maintenance.

b. Adhesives for vehicle body maintenance

![](images/cf3efa9b291bca9e501348f110dab68e32cbbf32573424246b822d2d5eea3c1f.webp)

### 4. Vehicle body maintenance

0 Tip:

The adhesive coated on the vehicle body will strip off or break after interior trimmings and steel plates of the vehicle body are deformed or cracked. Therefore, it is necessary to repair the parts coated with adhesive during maintenance.
a. Remove the adhesive on the surface of the vehicle body with a proper tool, and wipe clean the residual adhesive with alcohol.
b. Wipe the adhesive application part with special cleaning agent to avoid impurities such as residual adhesive remaining on the adhesive application surface.
c. Apply the repair adhesive to the original adhesive application part to achieve the bonding and sealing effect.

### 5. Maintenance of parts and components

a. Repair of bonding and sealing is required after some interior trimmings, front/rear drive electric powertrain and other components are damaged. It is necessary to clean the bonding

surface before applying sealant to prevent the bonding effect from being affected by burrs and cracks.

b. Sealants for maintenance of parts and components

![](images/0160cc4f11e9f7c4963e9a0358b52b2a1d2d11c856eb2e4c0c0abe611b4de856.webp)

### 7. Precautions for construction operation

a. The adhesive/sealant can prevent water and dust from entering the vehicle, and also has an anti-corrosion effect. Original sealed joints are obvious. If these seals are damaged, they should be resealed. Open joints sealed with adhesives/sealants should be filled with high consistency filler. Follow the instructions for the selected material.
b. When spraying adhesive/sealant, precautions must be taken to avoid spraying them into component openings (such as door locks, window lifting slots and seat belt retractors) and any moving or rotating parts. After spraying adhesive/sealant, make sure that all the relief holes of the vehicle body are open.
c. During construction operation, special goggles, gloves and protective clothing should be worn to prevent personal injury.
d. When the vehicle leaves the factory, all metal plates of the vehicle body have been subject to coating treatment. After overhaul and replacement of parts, all exposed metal surfaces must be treated with anti-rust primer for glue spreading.
e. After gluing maintenance, some adhesives/sealants need to be dried and cured, and the baking condition is baking at (70\~80)℃ for 20\~30 min.

### 1.6.1.5 Coolant

1. Coolant is applied to the battery thermal management system and motor cooling system of the vehicle.
2. When the coolant is heated to a high temperature, it may produce steam, the inhaling of which should be avoided as far as possible.
3. After direct contact with the coolant, the dosage of coolant directly absorbed by skin may be toxic or harmful. Anyone who swallows coolant by mistake may be in danger and should be sent to hospital for medical assistance immediately.
4. Such products are forbidden to be processed with ordinary food or connected with the drinking water supply system.

### 1.6.1.6 12V battery (starter Fe battery)

1. When removing the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) terminals, make sure to remove the cathode first. If the anode makes contact with any metal in the surrounding area during removal, there may be sparks and even fire, as well as a high risk of electric shock, resulting in serious or even life threatening injury.
2. Turn off all electrical equipment on the vehicle before turning on the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) again. First connect the positive terminal and then the negative. Do not install the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) in the wrong order, as this may cause fire.
3. The 12V battery (starter Fe battery) should be kept away from heat sources and open flames, and it should be well-ventilated when charged and used. Failure to do so may result in fire or personal injury.
4. Check whether the fixing clips of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) terminal are firm and in good contact.
5. The 12V battery (starter Fe battery) has a built-in power manager. Do not disassemble or repair the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) without authorisation, so as to avoid damage or personal injury.

### 1.6.1.7 Brake fluid

1. Brake fluid must be stored in marked con- tainers and kept out of the reach of children.

2. If the brake fluid comes into contact with skin or eyes, immediately wash the affected area with water and seek medical help at once.

3. Do not spray brake fluid on the paint. If brake fluid splashes on the paint, wash it with water immediately.

4. The use of any non-designated brake fluid may damage the brake system.

### 1.6.1.8 Chemical materials

1. Chemical materials, such as solvents, sealants, adhesives, coatings, resin foam, coolant, brake fluid, lubricating oil and grease, should be carefully used, stored and handled. They may be toxic, harmful, corrosive, irritant or highly flammable, and have highly dangerous odor and dust.

2. Long-term overexposure to such chemical substances may cause immediate or chronic, transient or permanent, cumulative, superficial, life-threatening effects or may affect the life span.

3. Chemical materials operations to be performed

a. Carefully read and abide by all warnings and precautions on raw material containers, and any attached leaflets, posters or other instructions for use. The health and safety data sheets of raw materials may be obtained from relevant manufacturers.
b. After being exposed to chemical materials, remove them from skin and clothes as soon as possible, immediately replace clothes that are heavily contaminated by chemical materials, and thoroughly clean them.
c. Strictly follow the working instructions and wear protective clothing to prevent chemical materials from directly contacting with skin and eyes.
d. Be sure to wash hands before taking a rest, eating, smoking or using toilet facilities during the handling of chemical materials.
e. Keep the working area clean and tidy and do not spill chemical materials.

4. Chemical materials operations to be avoided

a. Do not mix chemical materials at will unless otherwise stated by their manufacturers, because some chemical substances can form other toxic or hazardous chemicals, and they will release other toxic and hazardous gases and may cause explosion and other accidents when mixed.
b. Do not spray chemical materials in an enclosed environment.
c. Do not heat chemical materials unless otherwise stated by their manufacturers, because some chemical materials are highly flammable, while others may release toxic and hazardous gases.
d. Do not keep any chemical container open, because the emitted gas may accumulate to the extent that may cause poisoning, hazard or explosion. In addition, the gases of some chemical materials are heavier than air and will accumulate in the enclosed space.
e. Do not place chemical materials in unmarked containers.
f. Do not use chemical materials to clean hands and clothes. Chemicals, especially solvents and fuels, will dry the skin, which may cause allergies, skin inflammation or direct absorption of toxic and hazardous substances through the skin, thus affecting health.
g. Do not store chemical materials in empty containers at will unless such containers have been cleaned under supervision.
h. Do not sniff or smell chemical materials at will. Short-term exposure to high-concentration gases may still cause the risk of poisoning or injury.

### 1.6.1.9 Dust

1. Powder, dust and particles may be irritant, harmful or toxic. Avoid inhaling powdery chemicals and dust raised by dry friction operation. In case of poor ventilation, wear a protective breathing mask to prevent inhaling dust.

2. Fine dust of combustible substances may cause explosion. Stay away from fire sources to avoid explosion.

### 1.6.1.10 Electric shock

1. Electric shock may be caused by the improper use of any electrical equipment without following instructions or the misuse of any equipment in poor condition.

2. Be sure to maintain the electrical equipment within the specified time and test it frequently. Any faulty equipment should be marked and it is best to move it outside the working area.

3. Never cause wear, twist, cut-off, rupture or other damage to wires, cables, plugs and sockets. Do not contact electrical equipment and wires with water.

4. Make sure that the electrical equipment is protected by the correct fuse.

5. Misuse of electrical equipment is prohibited and no equipment with any hidden danger can be used; otherwise, personal safety may be affected.

6. Make sure that cables of the electrical equipment is not pinched and damaged during moving.

7. It is necessary to provide basic first aid training for specialized electrical operators.

8. In case of an electric shock:

a. Turn off the power supply before touching the victim.
b. If it is unable to turn off the power supply, remove the power that the victim touches using some dry insulating materials.
c. Please give first aid on the spot immediately if you have received special first aid training.
d. Ask for medical assistance.

### 1.6.1.11 Fibre isolation

1. Fibres are used to isolate noise.

2. Fibrous substances and sharp edges on the fibre surface may cause skin allergy. 3. Instructions for operation procedures should be observed and gloves should be worn during operation to avoid excessive skin contact with fibres.

### 1.6.1.12 Fire

1. Many materials related to vehicle maintenance are extremely flammable. Some materials will produce poisonous and harmful gases after burning.
2. Be sure to observe the instructions for fire safety when storing and handling flammable materials or solvents, especially in places close to electrical equipment or locations where welding operations are i n progress.
3. Be sure to confirm that there is no fire hazard before using any electrical and welding equipment.
4. Prepare a suitable fire extinguisher around the working area before performing welding

operations or using the heating equipment.

### 1.6.1.13 First aid

1. First aid should be given in accordance with local laws.

2. It is best to arrange some persons who have received professional first aid training in the workplace.
3. In case of splash into eyes, rinse eyes with clean water for at least 10 min.
4. In case of skin contamination, wash the contaminated area with soap and clean water.
5. In case of frostbite, soak the frostbitten part in ice water or cold water.
6. In case of inhaling toxic gas, immediately transfer the victim to the location with fresh air. If adverse reactions persist, immediately send the victim to the hospital for medical assistance.
7. In case of accidentally swallowing a liquid, inform the doctor of the information marked on the container or label. Do not blindly induce vomiting unless there is an indication on the label.

### 1.6.1.14 Foam polyurethane

1. Cured foam is used as the cushions for seats and trimmings.

2. Follow the manufacturer's instructions.
3. Foam components without chemical action are irritating and they may be harmful to skin and eyes, so gloves and goggles should be worn during operation.
4. People with chronic respiratory diseases, asthma, bronchial problems, or hereditary allergies, should not handle or approach uncured substances.
5. The spares, steam or spray of foam can cause direct irritation and allergic reaction and may be toxic and harmful.
6. Remember not to inhale the steam or spray of foam materials. Such materials must be used with good ventilation and protected breathing. Do not remove the mask immediately after spraying. Wait until the steam and spray are completely dissipated and then remove the mask.
7. Burning of uncured components and cured foam will produce toxic and harmful gases. Smoking and using open flame and electrical equipment are prohibited during foam-related operations unless the steam and spray have been completely removed. Any hot cutting of foam materials or special foam materials should be carried out in a well-ventilated environment.

### 1.6.1.15 General workshop tools and equipment

1. Always keep all tools and equipment in good working conditions, and operate them correctly during use.

2. Remember not to use tools or equipment for purposes contrary to their designed functions.
3. Do not have such equipment as crane, jack, axle and chassis support or sling bear any load exceeding its maximum load limit. The damage caused by overload may not appear immediately, but may result in a serious accident in the next use.
4. Do not use tools or equipment that are damaged or in poor working conditions, especially some high-speed equipment, such as grinding wheels. A damaged grinding wheel will break without warning and cause serious injury.
5. Wear goggles when using grinding wheels, chisels or sand blasting equipment.
6. Be sure to wear an appropriate breathing mask when using sand blasting equipment, handling asbestos-containing materials or using spraying equipment.
7. There must be ventilation equipment that can control the content of dust, spray and smoke in the environment.

### 1.6.1.16 Lubricant and grease

1. Avoid repeated contact with mineral oils for a long time, because all lubricating oils and greases are irritant to eyes and skin.

2. Used gear oil

a. Long-term repeated contact with mineral oils will cause the loss of natural grease on the skin, resulting in dryness, irritation and skin inflammation. In addition, used gear oil probably contains hazardous substances that can cause skin cancer. Be sure to use skin protection equipment and make sure that proper flushing installations are provided. b. Do not use any used gear oil as lubricating oil, or for any other applications that may be in direct contact with skin.

### 3. Safety rules for health protection

a. Avoid long-term and repeated contact with gear oil, especially used gear oil.
b. Wear protective clothing, including impermeable gloves.
c. Do not put the wiping cloth with gear oil in the pocket.
d. Prevent gear oil from contaminating clothes, especially underwear.
e. Do not wear clothes and shoes contaminated by gear oil. Wash work clothes regularly and keep them clean.
f. Deal with open wounds in time.
g. Apply cream on the skin as far as possible before working to avoid direct contact between the skin and gear oil.
h. Wash with soap and water to remove all gear oil. Application of protective agent containing lanolin will help to replace the natural grease removed from the skin.
i. Seek medical assistance immediately if skin lesions occur.
j. Remove the residual grease from components as far as possible before working.
k. Wear goggles, such as chemical goggles or face masks, if there is a possibility of direct contact with eyes. In addition, eye washing installations must be provided.

### 1.6.1.17 Noise

1. Some operations will produce noises of extremely high decibels, which may cause hearing damage. In this case, appropriate hearing protection devices should be worn.

### 1.7.1.1 Use of diagnostics device

1. Use of diagnostics device

a. The vehicle is powered off.

b. Connect VDCI to the diagnostic interface, and connect VDCI and VDS.

The diagnostic interface is located on the right side of the bonnet opening handle.

c. The vehicle is powered on.
d. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.

### 1.7.1.2 Fault diagnosis and troubleshooting

1. Diagnostic basis and troubleshooting method

![](images/0aa57cec6a55a2cd24e4600e38455a7d90ea66f17baef75b32c6d07b44f2ebd1.webp)

### 1.7.1.3 Circuit simulation tests

1. Unscheduled faults and other faults that cannot be detected by road test may be detected by circuit simulation tests, and possible vehicle faults can be effectively determined by simulating the conditions/environments when such faults occur.

0 Tip:

Listening carefully to the customer's description of the fault is very important for simulating the conditions when fault symptoms occur.

2. Simulation tests are generally divided into the following categories:

Vehicle vibration test
Thermal sensitivity test
Freeze test
Leak test
Load test
Pressure drop test

3. Vehicle vibration test: The vehicle may be faulty when it is running on a rough road. In this case, it is necessary to check the vibration-related conditions and the following parts of the vehicle:

a. Connectors and wiring harnesses: Determine which connectors and wiring harnesses may affect the electrical system under inspection. Gently vibrate or swing each connector and wiring harness when the monitoring system displays the fault that the system is trying to simulate. This test may show loose or poor electrical connections.

### 0 Tip:

When a connector is exposed to a humid environment, a corrosive film may form on its terminals. This situation may not be found during the visual inspection with the connector not disconnected. If an intermittent fault occurs, it may be caused by corrosion. It is recommended to check and clean terminals of the relevant connector in the system after disconnecting it.
b. Sensors and relays: Gently vibrate the sensors and relays in the system under inspection. This test may find loose or poorly-installed sensors or relays.
c. There are many reasons for electrical faults arising from vehicle vibration, among which the following need to be checked:

0 Tip:

First make sure that the system is properly grounded, then gently vibrate the wiring harness or parts as per the method introduced above and check whether the connection gets loose, and finally check the continuity of the wiring harness and conduct a voltage drop test according to the circuit diagram. • The connector is not installed in place. • The wiring harness is not long enough and it is stretched due to vibration or shaking. The wiring harness is attached to the bracket or movable parts. The ground wire is loose, dirty or corroded. The wiring harness is too close to high-temperature parts.

d. Locations behind the dashboard

Improper fixing of wiring harnesses may cause them to be twisted together during the installation of accessories. Vehicle vibration can cause excessive wear of wiring harnesses near brackets or mounting screws.
When the vehicle vibrates, loose or unfixed wiring harnesses will get stuck by seat parts (such as sliding guide rails). If any wiring harness passes under the installation position, it is necessary to check whether the wiring harness is damaged or stuck.

### 4. Thermal sensitivity test

a. Some faults may occur after the vehicle is exposed to sunlight in summer or is running for a long time. The reason for this may be related to the high temperature suffered by some parts of the wiring harness/electrical system. In this case, the thermal sensitivity test method should be used.
b. A heating gun or similar tool should be used to heat the faulty system parts and conduct the thermal sensitivity test.

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> Do not heat parts above 60°C (140°F).
> If a fault occurs during the heating test of any parts, the parts should be properly insulated and replaced if necessary.

### 5. Freeze test

a. If a vehicle fault disappears after the vehicle warms up in winter, the reason may be related to icing of some parts of the wiring harness/electrical system. Check whether this situation exists using the following two methods: Method : Leave the vehicle outside all night. Ensure that the temperature is low enough to allow recurrence of the fault, and diagnose the parts that may be affected quickly and thoroughly in the morning. Method II: Put the suspected parts in the refrigerating chamber long enough to freeze, reinstall the parts on the vehicle and check whether the fault recurs. If the fault recurs, repair or replace the parts.

### 6. Leak test

a. Check whether there is a leakage in the cooling system.
b. Check whether there is a leakage in the A/C system.
c. If the fault only occurs in highly-humid or rainy and snowy weather, it may be caused by water entering the electrical parts. In this case, check whether the vehicle body leaks by spraying water on the vehicle (similar to washing the vehicle).

### 7. Load test

a. If a fault occurs only when electrical equipment is turned on, turn on all electrical appliances (including A/C, audio system and fog lights) one by one, determine the relationship between each electrical appliance and the fault, and confirm the fault by a load test.

### 8. Pressure drop test

a. Usually, the voltage drop test is used to find out the reasons that may affect the normal operation of electrical parts or circuits.
b. A digital multimeter is used to check the circuit.
c. The wiring harness or circuit is determined as normal, if the resistance of a single wiring harness measured by a digital multimeter is very small (0 Ω or close to 0 Ω) and the voltage drop test result is normal.

### i Caution:

Turn off all electrical appliances before disconnecting the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).
Before performing electrical operations, power off the vehicle, disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and wait for 2 min to let the backup power supply of the airbag module run out.
Disconnecting the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) may delete the memories of clock, audio system and DTC. Therefore, it is necessary to confirm these memories before disconnecting the cathode cable.
Install genuine parts of the OEM only.
Never reversely connect terminal electrodes of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).

1. Check the input and output of relevant parts and their functions before replacing the control module.

a. When disconnecting parts:

Do not apply too much force when disconnecting a connector. If the connector is installed by fastening bolts, loosen the bolts and then disconnect the connector.
b. When connecting parts: Before installing a connector, make sure that its terminal is not bent or damaged and then connect it correctly. When installing the connector with fastening bolts, tighten the mounting bolts to the specified torques.
c. Do not drop or hit the control module, in order to avoid excessive impact.
d. Pay attention to avoiding condensation of the control module due to rapid temperature change and preventing the control module from contacting with water drops or raindrops. If water is found on the control module, dry the control module completely before installing it on the vehicle.
e. Be careful not to drop any oil/fluid on the control module connector.
f. Avoid cleaning the control module with volatile oil/fluid.
g. When using a digital multimeter, be careful not to allow its test probes to touch each other, thereby causing a short circuit. Avoid damaging the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) due to a short circuit of the power transistor inside the control module.
h. Use the specified test adapter when checking input and output signals of the control module.

### 2. Check the fuse

a. Check and confirm that the wire of the fuse is not disconnected.
b. If the wire of the fuse is disconnected, check whether the circuit is short-circuited.
c. When replacing the fuse, be sure to use a fuse with the same amperage rating.

### 1.7.1.5 How to check connectors

0 Tip:

Many electrical faults may be caused by electrical connection or wiring harness failures, or by stuck of parts or relays. Check the connector for good connection before confirming whether a fault is caused by parts or the wiring harness assembly.

### 1. Check the connector with a digital multimeter

a. Probe detection from the wiring harness side:

If the connector has a back cover, remove the back cover before probing the terminal. • Do not probe a waterproof connector from the wiring harness side; otherwise, the seal between the wiring harness and the connector may be damaged. b. Probe detection from the terminal side: Female terminal: Do not insert any object larger than the male terminal into the cathode connector. Male terminal: Carefully probe the contact surface of each terminal with a T-probe, and do not bend the terminal.

2. Check whether the tension of contact spring plate of the terminal is appropriate

a. Contact spring plate at the terminal may generate intermittent signals in the circuit.
b. If an intermittent open circuit occurs, check the contact spring plate at the open-circuited wiring harness and the female terminal in accordance with the following steps. Use a male terminal that matches the female terminal. Disconnect the suspected faulty connector and fix the terminal side upwards. Try to insert the male terminal into the female terminal when fixing the male terminal wiring harness. Plug and unplug the connector again, and check whether the male terminal can be easily inserted into the female terminal.

### 1. Clothes

a. Please wear clean work clothes that meet the workshop standards.
b. Be sure to wear labor protective articles, and wear a safety helmet when working under the vehicle.

2. Vehicle protection

a. Prepare radiator grille cover, fender cover, seat cover, floor mat, etc. before starting the operation.

### 3. Safe operation

a. When two or more technicians work together, they must check safety for each other.
b. Be sure to wear necessary protective articles and be careful not to hurt yourself or others when working in a high-temperature and high-pressure environment or performing operations on rotating, moving or vibrating parts.
c. When jacking the vehicle with a jack, be sure to support the designated parts with safety brackets.
d. Use appropriate safety equipment to lift the vehicle.

4. Preparation of tools and measuring equipment a. Prepare tool supports, special tools, measuring tools, oil/fluid and parts for replacement before starting the operation.

5. Removal and installation, disassembly and assembly operations

a. Perform diagnosis after fully understanding the correct steps and the problems reported.
b. Check the general condition, deformation and damage of the assembly before removing its parts.
c. In case of a complex assembly structure, make records (e.g., recording the total number of all electrical connectors and bolts, or the total number of removed hoses) and draw fitting marks, so that the assembly can be reassembled to its original state. If necessary, temporarily mark hoses and their joints.
d. If necessary, clean the removed parts, thoroughly inspect and install them.

6. Removed parts

a. Place all removed parts in separate boxes to prevent them from mixing with or contaminating new parts.
b. Replace all removed parts that cannot be reused, such as gaskets, O-rings and self-locking nuts.
c. Keep the removed parts for inspection if required by the customer.

7. Inspection after completion of work

a. Ensure that the parts for replacement are properly installed and fastened.
b. Ensure that the tools and materials used are not left inside the front compartment, vehicle and boot.
c. Check and confirm for no liquid leakage.

### i Caution:

After the completion of work, be sure to carry out the above-mentioned inspections correctly; otherwise, serious accidents or injuries may be caused.

### 8. Pre-coated parts

a. Pre-coated parts refer to bolts and nuts coated with locking sealant in the plant. b. a pre-coated part is retightened, loosened or moved by any means, it must be recoated with the specified locking sealant. c. Before using a pre-coated part again, be sure to remove the old locking sealant, dry the part with compressed air, and apply a proper amount of new locking sealant to the part. d. Some locking sealants cure slowly and may require waiting for a certain time.

9. Pads

a. If necessary, apply sealant to pads to prevent leakage.

10.Bolts, nuts and screws

a. Strictly abide by all torque requirements for fasteners, and always use a torque wrench.
b. Make sure that no foreign matters (burrs, paint, etc.) are deposited under the bolts and nuts when tightening them.
c. Please follow the following basic principles when removing nuts or bolts: diagonally loosen them several times from outside to inside; in case of any special regulations, please operate according to such regulations.
d. Please follow the following basic principles when tightening nuts or bolts: diagonally pretighten them several times from outside to inside; in case of any special regulations, please operate according to such regulations.

11.Fuse

a. For fuse inspection, check and confirm that the wire of the fuse is not blown.
b. For fuse replacement, carry out a short-circuit test first, and then replace the fuse after confirming that there is no short-circuit fault in the line.
c. Fuses with the same rated current must be used.

12.Clip

a. The positions of clips, tree nails, clamps, etc. encountered during disassembly are marked and indicated in illustrations contained in this manual.

0 Tip: Replace damaged clips.

### 1.7.3.1 Workflow

![](images/0cf7e2e447c412641044737ce2ed4111c880f98abec15eb357ffdd36911b250d.webp)

![](images/49050086efe8b87c33cdbb4f85000dea16adf634c6180cb67640fed43c451877.webp)

![](images/58668c8f7a0e8604178be900dabfc11ab4811d65462f8184bf7c5a1b1c244a1d.webp)

### 1. Check the blown fuse line

a. Remove the blown fuse, measure the resistance between the load end of the blown fuse and the ground wire, and disconnect all circuit switches connected to the fuse. In this case, if the measured resistance is about 0Ω, it indicates a short circuit somewhere between the switch and the load. If the measured resistance is displayed as "OL", it indicates no short circuit, but the instantaneous overvoltage of the load may also cause the fuse to blow.

### 0 Tip:

Main causes for short circuit include the following: The outer surface of the wiring harness is damaged due to wear or overheat. Water enters the connector. There is a man-made fault.

b. When replacing a fuse, make sure that the current rating of the new fuse is correct and never use the fuse whose current is over or below the current rating.

### 1.7.3.3 How to deal with intermittent faults

0 Tip:

To determine the status of an intermittent fault, first ask the customer about driving conditions, weather conditions, fault occurrence frequency and fault symptoms of the vehicle, and then try to simulate the fault. Determine whether the circuit under detection is damaged or normal, and confirm and remove the fault. Refer to the symptom list of each system to narrow the range of possible faults.

### 1. Vibration method

a. Gently vibrate the possibly faulty sensor with your fingers, and check whether the fault recurs.
b. Gently shake the connector in the horizontal and vertical directions to see whether the fault recurs.
c. Gently shake the wiring harness and the connector in the horizontal and vertical directions to see whether the fault recurs.

### 2. Heating method

a. Heat the possibly faulty parts with an electric hair dryer or a similar article to see whether the fault recurs.

i Caution: Do not damage the component structure when heating.

### i Caution:

Do not spray water directly on the front compartment and high-voltage and lowvoltage components. Be careful when conducting a water spraying test on the vehicle, because water leakage of the vehicle may cause damage to some electrical components.

### 1.7.3.4 How to deal with historical faults

1. A fault indeed occurs although it is not displayed in the current state. If this happens, the related faults may always exist. In case of a historical fault, the following detection steps should be performed:

a. Check whether the customer has changed the fuse or disconnected the connector. b. If so, clear the DTC and then check whether the DTC has been reset. If the DTC is not reset, complete the diagnosis. c. If the DTC is reset, perform the relevant DTC diagnosis process. After that, check the wiring harness and the connector. See "How to deal with intermittent faults" for details.

### Description

1. This section is provided to assist in the diagnosis, testing and maintenance related to noise, vibration and abnormal sound.

a. Noise is defined as the sound that has nothing to do with the equipment in the cab but cannot be accepted by passengers.
b. Vibration is defined as the pulsation felt by passengers that is not caused by road surface changes.
c. Comfort is a riding quality, with which passengers can clearly feel the reaction from the road.

### Principle of diagnosis

1. Diagnosis is not only based on a series of related steps to solve specific problems. It is a method to check a system that fails to function properly and find out the cause. This method should also help to understand how the system works and whether it works normally. There are some basic rules for diagnosis. If these rules can be observed, the cause of a problem can usually be found out at the first time.

### Understand the system

1. Understand how the parts are assembled.

2. Understand operations and restrictions of the system, and what will happen if the system becomes faulty. 3. Sometimes, it is necessary to check a possibly faulty system against a known good system.

### Understand the history of the system

1. Any clue about the following items can save the diagnosis duration:

a. Is the system new or old?
b. What treatment has been done to the system?
c. Has the system been repaired previously? Is the current situation related to the previous repair?
d. How about the maintenance records?

### Understand the history of the situation

1. Any clue about the following items can save the diagnosis duration:

a. Does the situation occur suddenly or form gradually? b. Is the situation related to other events, such as impact or previous replacement of parts? c. Knowing how the situation was discovered may be an important clue to find out the cause.

### Understand the development possibility of certain situations

1. Pay attention to simple problems instead of complex ones. For example:

a. A circuit problem usually occurs in the connection, not in the part itself. b. Startup failure of the motor is more likely to be caused by loose wires or minor adjustments, rather than mechanical faults.

c. It is necessary to understand the difference between "impossible" and the "unlikely". Faults in some systems, though unlikely, still happen. d. Although parts are new, it does not mean that they must function properly.

### Symptoms eliminated but failed to find fault cause

1. For example, reducing the tyre pressure of a front wheel may solve the vehicle's leaning to one side, but this does not identify the real reason.

### Fault cause identified

1. Confirm the problem found repeatedly and check what causes the wear of components. For example:

a. Looseness of one fixed seat of the powertrain may indicate that other fixed seats also get loose.

### Check

1. Operate the vehicle to allow recurrence of the fault, and confirm the problem described by the customer.

2. Check whether the obvious cause of the fault can be found by visual inspection.

3. If any obvious cause is found by visual inspection or based on the customer's problem description, eliminate the cause before proceeding with the next step (if possible).

4. The road test and the customer's description in detail can provide the relevant information that helps to confirm the problem and the direction for starting the diagnosis correctly.

5. If the problem still exists after inspection, remove it according to the fault symptoms.

### Check

1. Noise and vibration usually occur in the following 4 areas:

a. Tyre. b. Suspension. c. Drive system d. Interior trimmings

2. The locations of problems related to noise, vibration and comfort should be determined as soon as possible. The simplest and fastest way is to conduct a road test, with appropriately approved noise, vibration and comfort diagnostic detectors being used to support the diagnosis and testing procedures.

### 2.1.1.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Operators should wear insulating protective equipment, such as work clothes, insulating gloves, insulating shoes, goggles.

2. Ensure that the workplace is dry and ventilated, tools and instruments are placed neatly, and fire extinguishers are provided if necessary.

3. Check the safety conditions of instruments and equipment, such as lifts and jacks.

4. Check the safe driving operation of the vehicle to ensure the smooth maintenance.

5. When the vehicle enters the repair workshop, please put on the seat cover and steering wheel cover. Avoid dirtying the vehicle during operation.

6. Before driving the vehicle into the lifting frame, make sure that there is enough distance between the bottom and both sides of the vehicle and the lifting frame to avoid scratching.

7. Before lifting the vehicle, ensure that the weight of the vehicle does not exceed the rated load of the lift.

8. Be sure to select the correct lifting point when lifting the vehicle.

9. In the process of lifting the vehicle, it is not allowed to start the vehicle and put it into gear when the driving wheels touch the ground; otherwise it may cause damage to the vehicle or personal injury.

10.Operators must strictly abide by various safety rules and usage rules during maintenance; otherwise it may cause damage to the vehicle or personal injury.

11.When replacing parts and wearing parts, be sure to use original spare parts to ensure the safety and performance of the vehicle.

12.After the maintenance, be sure to carry out a test run inspection and pay special attention to the inspection of the brake system and occupant protection system.

13.The vehicle can only be handed over to the customer after the fault code is cleared.

### Basic safety requirements

1. Signs such as "Danger" and "Warning" marked on the vehicle are safety information. Before maintenance operation or maintenance steps, relevant tips and specified safety operation requirements shall be strictly followed.

"Danger" indicates that serious injury or death will be caused if the specified operating procedures are not followed.

"Warning" indicates that it is a direct danger, and serious personal injury may be caused if the specified operating procedures are not followed.

2. High-voltage components include high-voltage orange wiring harness, high voltage battery system, front drive electric powertrain, rear drive electric powertrain, charging and distribution assembly, charging system, electric compressor, PTC heater, etc.

3. Electrical circuit maintenance personnel must hold a qualification certificate of high voltage practice and strictly abide by the electrician s safety operating procedures.

4. When maintaining high-voltage components, be sure to wear non-destructive insulating protective equipment as required. The maintenance tools for operation must be high-voltage insulating tools.

5. Do not wear accessories, watches, etc. when maintaining the vehicle.

6. It is strictly forbidden for non-professionals to cut or open high-voltage cables and highvoltage components.

7. Do not touch the anode and cathode terminals of high voltage components of the vehicle with both hands at any time.

8. Do not wash the high-voltage components and electrical compartment of the vehicle with water.

9. No artificially destructive behaviour on high-voltage components of the vehicle is permitted.

### Testing safety requirements

1. All levels of maintenance and pre-inspection for battery electric vehicles are in a live and start-up state, and the pre-inspection must be carried out by professionals.

2. Before the vehicle is powered on, be sure to confirm that no other personnel are performing maintenance work, and ensure that parking brake has been applied and the vehicle is in neutral position.

3. After the vehicle is powered on, warning signs such as "No Move" should be hung on the steering wheel.

4. Insulating gloves must be tested for insulation before vehicle testing, diagnosis, and completion inspection. Do not use damaged insulating gloves. The testing instruments can be used only after they are confirmed to be in good working condition, so as to avoid high voltage accidents caused by false values output from faulty instruments.

5. Do not directly touch the orange wiring harness, high-voltage connectors and high-voltage components with bare hands.

6. Do not touch the terminals in the high-voltage cable connectors with fingers, metal ends of small tools or iron bars.

7. Do not touch the probe conductor by hand when measuring the voltage of the high voltage terminal with a multimeter.

### Maintenance safety requirements

1. Before the vehicle construction operation, the vehicle should enter the maintenance operation area, with warning signs of "High Voltage Danger" and "No Entry". Nonmaintenance personnel are prohibited from entering, and the warning signs can only be removed by maintenance personnel.
2. Before the vehicle construction operation, ensure that the vehicle is disconnected from highvoltage electricity.
3. During the vehicle construction operation, it is necessary to record the number of all disassembled parts and place them in the parts tray in a clean and visible area. When assembling, ensure that all parts are installed in place, and there are no spare or missing parts, so as to strictly prevent small parts such as bolts from falling into the high-voltage components.
4. When the vehicle is repaired and maintained, the anode and cathode connectors of the cables of dismantled high-voltage components shall be insulated and protected with special insulating covers or insulating tapes.

### Checking fixing bolts and nuts of chassis

1. Check whether the fixing bolts and nuts of chassis are loose

a. Lift the vehicle, check the matching marks of the chassis fixing bolts and nuts, and check the torque of the bolts or nuts if there is any misalignment.

### Checking brake pedal

1. Check the working condition of brake pedal

a. Check that there should be no jamming and failure to return during the operation of the brake pedal.
b. Check that there should be no abnormal noise in the operation of brake pedal, and apply grease to the friction joint if necessary.

### Checking EPB switch

1. Check the working condition of EPB switch a. When the vehicle is powered on, press the brake pedal. When the vehicle is stationary, pull up the EPB switch. The EPB indicator on the dashboard flashes and then stays on, enabling the electronic parking brake.

![](images/1e4182e757b04fd186e3905937608fcefa23aff33b950a55d279e337b70627a1.webp)

![](images/6c951a2531b63bf410009180b07a07bb93c34fc58143e2c8ef37f7612e6d8a7c.webp)

b. When the vehicle is powered on and is in any gear other than P and EPB has been engaged, press the brake pedal and the EPB switch. The EPB indicator goes out along with a text prompt reading "Parking brake released” on the dashboard, releasing the electronic parking brake.

### Checking brake pad

1. Check the front brake pad a. Check whether the thickness of brake pad friction material meets the requirements (excluding the thickness of steel backing) with a brake pad thickness gauge.

![](images/e2b5de58b2e8ae56c1e597f1a2bfc9e7fa93f782f23e71eeff3dd653997ce710.webp)

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> If the thickness of brake pad friction material is less than the service limit, replace the whole set of brake pad.
>
> Allowable wear thickness of front brake pad: 2.75\~9.85mm (thickness after wear)
>
> 2. Check the rear brake pad a. Check whether the thickness of brake pad friction material meets the requirements (excluding the thickness of steel backing) with a brake pad thickness gauge.
>
> ![](images/7d4641d8be836bb975347e33e5d4e0621fa235a5dbc9c6ff904e14c5f71017f1.webp)

### i Caution:

If the thickness of brake pad friction material is less than the service limit, replace the whole set of brake pad.

Allowable wear thickness of rear brake pad: 3\~11.1mm (thickness after wear)

### Checking brake disc

1. Check the runout and thickness of the front brake disc a. Remove the front wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly b. Remove the 2 fixing bolts and take off the front brake caliper assembly ①.

![](images/4f605685e80b8cf7a07d5ee0b396857d87c2b934aa7c6ff93b61b88c3f06024e.webp)

0 Tip: Hang the front brake caliper assembly aside with a hook.

c. The vehicle is in neutral gear.
d. Thoroughly clean the brake disc and remove all rust corrosion.
e. Check if the surface of the brake disc is subject to damage or cracks, and replace the brake disc if any.
f. Install appropriate flat washers and wheel nuts and tighten them.

![](images/01a965bff8f5106ce654387b6693dee959dd562122def0694c887e23b739b16b.webp)

g. Install the measuring support of brake disc runout. Special tool: measuring support of brake disc runout

![](images/4d5c4377d7a778b12499bca051370e7689ffa533d78622f005f5e024802f2543.webp)

h. Put the dial gauge as shown in the figure, slowly rotate the brake disc, and measure the runout at 10mm from the outer edge of the brake disc.

### 0 Tip:

If the runout of the brake disc exceeds the service limit of 0.08mm, adjust the brake disc with an optical disc drive.
If the thickness of brake disc is less than the adjustment limit, replace it.

### Flatness of front brake disc: 0.08mm

![](images/37960af89dd8b70256ed0168c45d4d650f8274a9ec4c6ab20981d6f22720d187.webp)

i. Use a micrometer to measure the thickness of the brake disc at 8 points 10 mm from the outer edge of the brake disc and at the intervals of about 45°. If the minimum measured value is less than the adjustment limit, replace the brake disc. Allowable wear thickness of front brake disc: ≥32\~34mm (thickness after wear)

![](images/e6b9495a284c7a41450374fb48155841f2290c230cf20511c78c3892cd7fd89e.webp)

k. Remove the wheel nuts and gaskets.

j. Install and tighten the 2 fixing bolts of the front brake caliper assembly Torque: 195±5N•m

l. l. Install the front wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

2. Check the runout and thickness of the rear brake disc a. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly b. Release the EPB.

![](images/e975c66c8cc2eabcc73719097aad1f8a75fb650ef1084a576f6c278ab10bc42d.webp)

c. Disconnect the connector A, remove the 2 fixing bolts B, and remove the rear integrated EPB caliper assembly.

### 0 Tip:

Hang the rear integrated EPB caliper assembly aside with a hook.

d. Thoroughly clean the brake disc and remove all rust corrosion.
e. Check if the surface of the brake disc is subject to damage or cracks, and replace the brake disc if any.
f. Install appropriate flat washers and wheel nuts and tighten them.
g. Install the measuring support of brake disc runout. Special tool: measuring support of brake disc runout

![](images/892dd2b2a6a7cef0e6c926ef4221e20976d100724f581049c35c4af09deaea2e.webp)

h. Put the dial gauge as shown in the figure, slowly rotate the brake disc, and measure the runout at 10mm from the outer edge of the brake disc.

### 0 Tip:

If the runout of the brake disc exceeds the service limit of 0.08mm, adjust the brake disc. If the thickness of brake disc is less than the adjustment limit, replace it.

Flatness of rear brake disc: 0.08mm i. Use a micrometer to measure the thickness of the brake disc at 8 points 10 mm from the outer edge of the brake disc and at the intervals of about 45°. If the minimum measured value is less than the adjustment limit, replace the brake disc. Allowable wear thickness of rear brake disc: 28\~30mm (thickness after wear)

![](images/7ac300e612e3e3fa19052a54b614a97ab295b573234f6e7d834aaa2033b0be9a.webp)

![](images/294225ebd2252847f9b071bef4f423c73c838ffadf1ac81b355b62d5118da2ce.webp)

j. Install and tighten the 2 fixing bolts of the rear integrated EPB caliper assembly, and connect the connector A. Torque: 100±10N•m

k. Use the parking brake. l. Remove the wheel nuts and gaskets. m. Install the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

### 1. Checking brake system pipeline

a. Check whether the brake system pipe is deformed, seriously corroded and cracked, and replace it if so.
b. Check whether the brake system hose is aging and cracked, and replace it if so.
c. Check whether there is oil leakage in the brake system pipeline and joint, and repair or replace it if any.

### Checking brake caliper guide pin

1. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

2. Checking brake caliper guide pin

![](images/1c99aa85e0ba410ab30e0853a18fc88d2e59bbf34c79ccd10af8a77ac870b9f5.webp)

a. Remove the dirt, check whether the dust cover of the brake caliper guide pin is cracked and aging, and replace it if so.
b. Release the EPB, press the brake pedal, check whether there is any jamming or abnormal sound in the brake caliper guide pin, and repair or replace it if any.

3. Install the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

### 1. Checking steering wheel

a. Hold the steering wheel and shake it up and down and left and right, and check that the steering wheel is not swinging or loose.
b. When the vehicle is powered on, check whether the steering wheel rotates heavily, and repair the steering system if so.

2. Check the free clearance of steering wheel

a. Make the front wheels in a straight driving position.
b. Power off the vehicle.
c. Mark the top of the steering wheel.
d. Lean a ruler against the top of the steering wheel.
e. Measure the maximum distance that the steering wheel can turn left under the condition that the front wheels do not rotate.
f. Turn the steering wheel back to its original position.
g. Measure the maximum distance that the steering wheel can turn right under the condition that the front wheels do not rotate.
h. If the sum of the left and right measured values is not more than 30mm, the free stroke of the steering wheel is normal; otherwise, check the steering system.

![](images/f5c9d24159bad3070a3aacc22210c44604631b6af3f3c5ca8991c7937c310916.webp)

### Checking steering tie rod

1. Check the steering tie rods on both sides a. Check whether the steering tie rod is deformed, and replace the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly if so. Refer to: Electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly

![](images/40482c15887352012a49aac78aa600dbbdf4694e34ca0e69c3ee382b854db29a.webp)

### Checking steering tie rod ball pin and dust cover

1. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly

3. Check the dust cover

![](images/c1837fbeedd3d7c5c76ccdf37914869d1b02d525045b8cfbd34a63f804dbe29c.webp)

a. Check that the dust covers of steering tie rods on both sides are free of damage or aging.

![](images/14d9aea2ba6ecb5b5fc76c0a1b527020636f881c2459b68f2ae56c5944ee6de9.webp)

b. Check that the ball pin dust covers of outer steering tie rods on both sides are free of damage or aging.

4. Check the ball pin

![](images/ba8d49a57beaad4ec71660dfd84e56dc8699a1a4fabdf45e85292ffc0ccf17ec.webp)

a. Check that the ball pin of the outer steering tie rod rotates flexibly without jamming and looseness, the nut is tightened, the lock pin is not lost, and the lubrication is good.

5. Install the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly

6. Install the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

### Checking dust cover of the drive half shaft

1. Checking dust cover of the drive half shaft

a. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly

![](images/5885a00d548c9705a4d8954358884d5ce9cf09bf7d093fc4d71b904740ae2155.webp)

b. Check whether the dust covers of all drive half shafts are damaged or aging, and replace the drive half shaft assembly if so. Refer to: Front drive half shaft assembly or Refer to: Rear drive half shaft assembly

### Checking front and rear suspension systems

1. Checking front and rear suspension systems

a. Check that the front and rear suspension system components are free of deformation, cracking and damage.

### 1. Check tyres

a. Check that the tyre is not leaking, and there is no crack or bulge on the surface.
b. Check the tyre for abnormal wear.
c. Check whether the tyre is worn to the wear mark position, and replace it if so.

2. Check inflation pressure

![](images/c970a5f843e8904a6637eebc4e0e891eee6655f36878073ec438e7162a334def.webp)

a. Check the inflation pressure of wheels with a tyre gauge.

### 0 Tip:

The front wheel king pin caster angle and inclination angle and front or rear wheel camber angle are not adjustable. If they are not within the specified values, check the suspension components for bending or damage. If the suspension components are bent or damaged, be sure to replace the damaged parts. Do not try to repair them by tapping and other methods. If the front wheel toe-in is correct, but the steering angle is not within the specified range or the left inner steering angle is different from the right one, check the suspension components for bending or damage. If the suspension components are bent or damaged, be sure to replace the damaged parts. Do not try to repair them by tapping and other methods.

### 1. Check before alignment

i Caution: Do not try to align the parts by straightening, and damaged parts must be replaced.

a. Release the parking brake to avoid incorrect measurement.
b. Make sure that the suspension device is not changed.

![](images/d49ab1d1315f5b4cc3b0450d9024d51794ee71c5ebd9bd462aeef2bbe63b2075.webp)

c. Make sure that the 4 tyres are in the same size and correct, and the tyre pressure is within the specified pressure range.

d. Make sure that there is no people or extra load in the vehicle.
e. Check whether each fixing point of suspension is loose and deformed, and check that the clearance of each ball head of suspension is not too large.
f. Check the vibration of the wheel.
g. Check that the heights of the corresponding positions on both sides of the vehicle should be consistent.
h. When the wheels are in a straight forward position, the steering wheel must be centred.
i. Make the wheel device bounce up and down for several times to stabilise the suspension.

2. Test

0 Tip: Check the wheel alignment according to the operating instructions of the four-wheel aligner.

![](images/f5b91219c673844060cb944a717e6c451db423988c1062d02ba7f7fe876f19ad.webp)

![](images/9941da5a372c014de7dcfba55ff37c7e5c8fb59e063c2a7b56369de37b1f7353.webp)

### 3. Adjust the rear wheel toe-in

![](images/820a32cd2e9651e071ad99c04ea0c0567263084d409c958719119de5e87abc49.webp)

a. Fix the adjusting sleeve ① of the rear control arms on both sides with a wrench, and loosen the lock nuts A and B.
b. Rotate the adjusting sleeve ① of the rear control arms on both sides until the rear wheel toe-in is correct. Rear wheel toe-in (Single side):0° ±0.08° (Required absolute difference between left and right sides<0.03°)
c. After adjustment, fix the adjusting sleeve ① of the rear control arms on both sides and tighten the Torque: 90±5N•m

### 4. Adjust the front wheel toe-in

a. Lock the steering wheel assembly to prevent it from rotating.

![](images/898d39dc456d79ff64a9e8c63674fc0fe08e0c608b2eb65ac29e95c4456ec88f.webp)

b. Loosen the lock nut A and elastic clamp B on the left and right sides of the steering tie rod.
c. Twist the toe-in adjusting rods ① on both sides as required to adjust and measure the toe-in value until it reaches the specified value. Front wheel toe-in (Single side):0°±0.08° (Required absolute difference between left and right sides<0.03°)
d. Tighten the lock nut A and install the sheath elastic clamp B. Torque: 90±5N•m

e. After adjustment of the front wheel toe-in, check whether the steering wheel is in the middle position, and adjust it if not.

f. Perform the steering angle calibration according to the prompt of the diagnostics device. Refer to: Steering angle calibration

### Wheel transposition

1. Wheel transposition adjustment

![](images/4fa6a6409223e50e4592e98af3a750bf038388ef522d30dc05c68ea9b47eb93c.webp)

a. Transpose the wheels in the sequence shown in the figure.

①: Non-directional tyres
②: Directional tyres

### 0 Tip:

In order to make the tyre wear evenly and prolong the service life of the tyre, it is recommended to perform wheel transposition according to the maintenance schedule. However, the most time suitable for wheel transposition depends on the driver's driving habits and road conditions.
After wheel transposition, it is necessary to rematch and learn the tyre pressure monitoring module. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring module matching
Self-learning of tyre pressure monitoring module: After parking for more than 30min and driving for more than 10min when the vehicle speed exceeds 40km/h, self-learning is successful.

### Checking axial clearance of hub bearing

1. Checking axial clearance of hub bearing a. Remove the wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly b. Install appropriate flat washers and wheel nuts and tighten them. Tightening torque: 130N•m

![](images/c55115d633fabbbd7ee56d4c75bd858feddeaaa0812607e2bc38dcadbd9771f3.webp)

c. Put the dial gauge as shown in the figure, shake the brake disc back and forth in the direction of the drive half shaft, and measure the axial clearance of bearing.

Standard value: 0\~0.05mm

### 0 Tip:

The dial gauge probe should be pressed against the hub flange.
Replace the hub bearing unit if the axial clearance of bearing is greater than the standard value.

d. Install the wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

### Checking coolant level in the auxiliary coolant tank

1. Check the coolant level in motor cooling system a. Remove the front right compartment trim panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trim panel assembly

![](images/d59a687582f0514760e9699f6b5df1e2b6765770a016d0f56298c97a31fccb47.webp)

b. Observe the coolant level in the auxiliary coolant tank assembly. Make sure that the coolant level is between the "MIN" and "MAX" marks.
c. If the coolant level is at or below the "MIN" mark, add coolant to the auxiliary coolant tank assembly until coolant reaches "MAX" mark and check if the cooling system is subject to leakage.

d. Install the front right compartment trim panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trim panel assembly

2. Check the level of battery temperature control system coolant a. Remove the engine trim panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trim panel assembly b. Remove the front right compartment trim panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trim panel assembly

![](images/3f404f1fb97e7fb3965f884610196cb005a0dedc784119562f00ce6923ea8380.webp)

c. Observe the coolant level in the battery thermal management auxiliary coolant tank assembly. Make sure that the coolant level is between the "MIN" and "MAX" marks.
d. If the coolant level is at or below the "MIN" mark, add coolant to the battery thermal management auxiliary coolant tank assembly until coolant reaches "MAX" mark and check if the battery temperature control system is subject to leakage.

e. Install the front right compartment trim panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trim panel assembly f. Install the engine trim panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trim panel assembly

a. Remove the engine trim panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trim panel assembly b. Check that the brake fluid level should be between "MAX" mark and "MIN” mark. If the level is below the "MIN” mark or above the "MAX” mark, fill or pump out the brake fluid.

### 1. Preparations

a. Drive the vehicle into the lifting position, activate the parking brake, and power off the vehicle.

2. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly

3. Remove the front right compartment trim panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trim panel assembly

4. Drain the coolant

a. Remove the auxiliary coolant tank cover.

i Caution:

After the drive motor and auxiliary coolant tank are completely cooled, remove the auxiliary coolant tank cover.

0 Tip:

Turn the auxiliary coolant tank cover counterclockwise slowly (do not press it down) until it is removed. Such slow operation can gradually relieve residual pressure in the cooling system.

![](images/8f54683acdcb2bfc2affc115b9ff34e45bf0182904a41472fdcebb7484353042.webp)

b. Remove the elastic clamp, pull out the coolant pipe assembly 51①, and recycle the waste coolant.

i Caution:

Recycle the waste coolant according to local regulations.

c. After the coolant is drained, install the coolant pipe assembly 51① and fix it with elastic clamps.

### 5. Add coolant

Coolant capacity of motor cooling system: 9.3±0.2L Coolant specification of motor cooling system①: -40℃ long-acting organic acid coolant Coolant specification of motor cooling system②: Arteco Havoline XLC50_50

a. Fill in the auxiliary coolant tank with the coolant, until reaching the “MAX” mark.
b. Install the auxiliary coolant tank cover, but do not fasten it.
c. Start the vehicle, and power it off after the coolant pump runs for about 5min.

0 Tip: Fill the auxiliary coolant tank with coolant continuously until the coolant level is between "MIN” mark and "MAX" mark and does not change. d. Start the vehicle again and check the motor cooling system for any leakage. e. Install the auxiliary coolant tank cover and fasten it.

6. Remove spilled coolant

7. Install the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly
8. Install the front right compartment trim panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trim panel assembly
