### 3.6.7.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Rear drive motor controller(BYD)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

![](images/c1fd7d17206e9031ae0b2243dad17059304a27305162803db3fdccc16b0c18d8.webp)

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of the rear drive motor assembly without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Rear drive motor controller(BYD)”

6. Read data flow

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

### Replacing rear drive transmission gear oil

1. Lift the vehicle.
2. Drain the rear drive transmission gear oil

![](images/a5a9d60aea62b046ab709f1d9e5b40cd4d5c8b27553f8b136ef2975425376cd8.webp)

a. Remove the oil drain plug of rear drive transmission.

### 0 Tip:

Collect waste gear oil with the gear oil collection device, and dispose of it according to local laws and regulations.

b. Install and tighten the oil drain plug after discharge. Torque: 50±3N•m c. Clean the gear oil around the oil drain hole.

3. Fill the rear drive transmission gear oil a. Remove the oil filler plug of rear drive transmission.

![](images/1ebfaf2eeecd37618673aa52c56414cd695d7c45255cde6c8b9680c969510bae.webp)

b. Fill the rear drive transmission gear oil with the gear oil filling machine.

Specification of gear oil①: Castrol ON D2 Specification of gear oil②: Castrol BOT384 Specification of gear oil③: Shell S3-ATF-MD3 Filling amount of gear oil: 0.95±0.1L
c. Install and tighten the oil filler plug after filling. Torque: 37±2 N•m
d. Clean the gear oil around the fuel filler cap.
e. Lower the vehicle and move it out of the station.

### Calibration procedures

1. Record the motor zero-position code.

![](images/10e2ec452251a0050a564c794a2fd65c8a5449ce03ec2246920137db6706f530.webp)

a. Record the motor zero-position code on the rear drive motor. After the assembly is completed, use VDS (VDS is updated to the latest version) to perform the motor electronic control zeroposition calibration. The motor zero-position code is as shown in the red box.

2. The vehicle is powered off.
3. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
4. Start the vehicle.
5. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
6. Zero-position calibration

![](images/3b829868f38ca09a72ba439a38b72d9ea32021e1240f1294c6b49250506cb355.webp)

a. Select "VDS2000 Vehicle Diagnosis System".

![](images/a700dec4acbd490028644b3f081526c6a40e95cf6de9d73a597650fff9d68371.webp)

b. Select Passenger car".

![](images/ec023868284ea7662b2aa13ec8255e378201f7b6452a0cf54c7f463bec1b740a.webp)

c. Select "EV series".

![](images/5f32405eb2980f66c1b301ebee4f79b46918300edfbd8f3295d8638062ad6ab4.webp)

d. Select "New Tang EV 2021".

![](images/409ba84213585660b4162f6bc1d987a2f6608cd4ca2e759bf7c0814bf45561d6.webp)

e. Select "New Tang EV 2021 General".

![](images/18397fa3ddd8562686052a16619599066eb4d20842b20983e668965fe2a82da6.webp)

f. Select ECU module".

![](images/d41886002d28f2f964371c2e02319d126736a12d5af1621829234ae03c218b65.webp)

T-4205A49

g. Select the arrow shown in the figure.

![](images/60d076bec15602a7b54bc2f39ffa4a09a439b6a0c8ee30c906d7b9a0f32e8a7e.webp)

h. Select "Data flow".

![](images/2462635328a7ca61d3bf6333020d2c67e3c10e2c6602585e61e59d0c179cfe0b.webp)

i. Click the run button to read the data flow.

![](images/3f8d6d552be99eac6194dc543a8f194e5bf428032c9a8070df77d9fb827a84e7.webp)

j. Check and record the original zero-position code of rear drive motor.

![](images/3e6b85f3c0ea3f3cb3cce7cde2a474c91756f72dc6953071fac3be03262d31fb.webp)

k. Click the stop button to stop reading data flow and return to the rear motor controller page.

![](images/e26217d531a611d93247ac72534a3211c2917f3ef12c8a13b182a65501be2c92.webp)

l. Select "motor back to 0 point calibration".

![](images/db583ea2cba445a10935dbb6605a59a499eaaadcaafe35c1947d05e84630a2a2.webp)

m. Click Read".

![](images/ed1bf721f52db660aa206dafb90eeb7e4cb661b90fcf66fa46fdc1e559a4d44a.webp)

n. Enter the 28-digit motor zero-position code of the loading motor (pay attention to capital and small letter) and click the run button.

![](images/6f42b714b2e33f152ecf6422ee56e6288c0eb87445421cb1c48fbcddf71cf828.webp)

o. If the code is correct, there is a prompt of "Operation succeeded" indicating that the zeroposition calibration is successful.

7. Restart the vehicle. VDS page operation: read the data flow to confirm whether the zeroposition calibration is successful and whether the zero-position code is correct (i.e., whether the latest zero-position code is consistent with the zero-position code of the current motor barcode).

### 0 Tip:

After zero-position calibration, the calibrated zero-position code can only be read after restarting the vehicle.
If the input of the zero barcode of the motor is correct, a “negative response” will be prompted during calibration, and several attempts can be made. If the “negative response” is still prompted, please record the barcode of the motor, the motor controller and the VIN of the vehicle, and timely feed it back to the manufacturer for handling.
The last four digits of the motor barcode are zero-position code, and the zero-position code displayed in the VDS data flow is checked against the zero-position code on the motor barcode.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Disable the high voltage power. Refer to: High voltage power disable and enable
4. Remove the battery pack rear mudguard assembly. Refer to: Battery pack rear mudguard assembly
5. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly
6. Drain coolant (cooling system). Refer to: Replace coolant (cooling system)
7. Drain the rear drive transmission gear oil. Refer to: Replace rear drive transmission gear oil
8. Remove the rear left/right wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
9. Remove the rear left/right drive half shaft assembly Refer to: Rear drive half shaft assembly
10.Remove the rear drive electric powertrain.

![](images/0ada27f0bca897a4238ae143e9dd88e97662e829685720e480ed6664fb2a04b4.webp)

a. Disconnect the low-voltage wiring harness connector of rear drive electric powertrain and disengage the wiring harness fixing clip.

![](images/3b8a6df1724cf57b0f1cd03e33f586d976c2352db92f5c4227044a2d1903dd48.webp)

b. Remove the 2 fixing bolts of ground wire. Torque: 22±2 N•m

![](images/4bf68280a6434380cbc444a576d3ae57726414981a90812d875d1ca09a71ebe1.webp)

c. Remove the elastic clamp and disconnect the coolant inlet pipe of rear drive electric powertrain.

![](images/ad2cc4423bad2fe8f81bfbbf8e15d7e85d291149af6e6d8b8847586e7590548d.webp)

d. Remove the elastic clamp A and the pipeline fixing clip, and disconnect the coolant outlet pipe of rear drive electric powertrain. e. Remove two fixing bolts B, and disconnect the HV wiring harness of the rear drive electric powertrain.

Torque: 7±1N•m

！ Warning: After the HV power cable is disconnected, use a special plug to seal the high voltage battery port and the wiring harness joint to prevent electric leakage or dust.

f. Check the periphery of rear drive electric powertrain, and disconnect all connected wiring harnesses and pipeline fixing clips to ensure that there is redundant connection. g. Lift the rear drive electric powertrain with the hydraulic lifting platform until the bracket is slightly stressed.

![](images/bc6e8be3bac4f4a39d24fe662287f9fd52ad2e16888a51099a48af0cfc00e1fd.webp)

h. Remove one fixing bolt A and 3 fixing bolts B, and take off the front suspension support assembly of rear drive motor assembly. Torque of bolt A: 85±5N•m Torque of bolt B: 85±5N•m

![](images/d1c5b1ed129412abe8ce4d91b2dd4d1935db9e151f4c3f72d9080f5cee91ef2e.webp)

i. Remove one fixing bolt and nut for connecting the left suspension support assembly of rear drive motor assembly and the rear auxiliary frame assembly.

Torque: 85±5N•m

![](images/a5c916a89117d51f88122fcd56c8047bbcdca8c20b4266d1fcaba19c24baabd4.webp)

j. Remove one fixing bolt and nut for connecting the rear suspension support assembly of rear drive motor assembly and the rear auxiliary frame assembly.

### Removal procedures

Torque: 85±5N•m

k. Slowly lower the bracket and lift down the rear drive electric powertrain.

i Caution:

During lowering, check whether there are interfering parts around the rear drive electric powertrain, which should be removed or avoided.

### Disassembly procedure

1. Disassemble the rear drive electric powertrain

Caution:

Before disassembling the rear drive electric powertrain, be sure to drain the residual coolant inside it. At the coolant inlet, use a pneumatic gun to blow out the coolant in the water channel.

![](images/65074b8f7d544c4db06aeb31d95ce2799aed77e203f9d7f08bd4277b4da9db68.webp)

a. Remove the 3 fixing bolts, and take off the left suspension support assembly of rear drive motor assembly.

Torque: 85±5N•m

![](images/6a7c803f4e5d73ff78648ed86c02859db4cc395621dc51d6b6743a47d528a559.webp)

b. Remove the 3 fixing bolts, and take off the rear suspension support assembly of rear drive motor assembly.

Torque: 85±5N•m

![](images/9113ffb83b2d168a790759f2253620e90e8853d1842437b435bc422ae0b51420.webp)

c. Remove the breather plug assembly. Torque: 16±2 N•m

![](images/3f5e65a782222927e02f97cbac6b13e830f98337fba03d3e1b71e9908379d462.webp)

d. Remove the 13 fixing bolts and take off the motor end cover.

i Caution: Remove the fixing bolts in diagonal order.

Torque: 6±1N•m

![](images/9b2031da391ac169d53d5fa0f712156140ed93290c3de4ef6ba2645c0ecfc88c.webp)

e. Remove the 2 fixing bolts and take off the shielding case. Torque: 6±1N•m

![](images/e44fdacb5b501ccc5890ffa3ab114a630039bc605a73c4c5e5079831979645d0.webp)

f. Remove the 3 fixing bolts and disconnect one connector A.

Torque: 10.5±1N•m

![](images/e8b2195c2085c928c61002783c38dece991104c4c1cd40d6c7f1883fa6638a68.webp)

g. Remove the 5 fixing bolts of the motor controller and take off the motor controller assembly upwards.

i Caution: Remove the fixing bolts in diagonal order.

Torque: 35±1N•m

![](images/971f13ba513ddad7e99f7ee81e493b5fd49d970756cc75bc04c25abbfb432e31.webp)

h. Replace the O-ring with a new one and protect the coolant inlet from bumping.

### 0 Tip:

Use a pneumatic gun to dry the residual water at coolant inlet and outlet.

![](images/aa5ec9534d2cf2545a3b8993ebd15cd794db84c1597d9133ec179869af30115b.webp)

i. Replace the controller seal ring with a new one.

![](images/66cd12e124495f6c767b561f27a4a1149bb50dea64a04f56bd750e210a2dfd01.webp)

j. If it is necessary to check the internal gears of the transmission, remove the 16 fixing bolts A and 3 fixing bolts B and separate the left and right cases of the transmission.

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> Remove the fixing bolts in diagonal order. Since the left case of transmission is integrated with the drive motor, only the right case of transmission can be removed.
>
> ![](images/9b5f75779f790c713968dda17bcfeadbca0430c95ae249afa7dfa79785226a2a.webp)
>
> k. Remove the clamp spring A of input shaft, and take off the input shaft ①, countershaft ② and differential ③ together.

### i Caution:

According to the maintenance requirements, dismantle the corresponding parts for maintenance or replacement.

### Assembly procedure

1. Assemble the rear drive electric powertrain in an order reverse to its disassembly and pay attention to the following:

![](images/4ea9dbd5d947ead391a79998a4820965f1dff0048c8501c570cdf2e67f115b11.webp)

a. Install the input shaft ①, countershaft ② and differential ③ together, and then install the clamp spring A of input shaft.

### i Caution:

After installation, turn the clamp spring and check that it is correctly installed in the clamp spring groove.
Turn the input shaft and check that all gears rotate smoothly.
b. Remove the residual sealant on the joint surfaces of the left and right cases of transmission.
c. Apply sealant to the joint surface of the right case of transmission, with the adhesive track along the inner side of the bolt hole. Specification of sealant: TONSAN 1596F

![](images/336b60da69ebe90268807411d91aa369b38e281e9542fc0ecc4da0802eee6ffd.webp)

d. Rotate the fixing disc on the countershaft so that its 3 bolt holes are aligned with the 3 bolt holes on the right case of transmission as much as possible.

e. Close the right case of transmission, and insert 2 screwdrivers or equivalent tools into the bolt holes of the fixing disc on the countershaft through the bolt holes of the right case of transmission before touching the sealant, so that the bolt holes are aligned to facilitate the installation of bolts.

### 0 Tip:

Avoid the fixing disc falling into the gear groove.

f. Install a long bolt into another bolt hole and screw it in several turns.

g. Remove the screwdriver and install the 2 fixing bolts.
h. Remove the long bolt and install the remaining one fixing bolt.
i. Install other fixing bolts of transmission case in diagonal order.

![](images/ab38f1475c4d411d8c321ebf16e8430958bbb342177d4e04aab63564eefc887d.webp)

j. Fasten the 16 fixing bolts A and 3 fixing bolts B in diagonal order. Torque: 25±2 N•m

k. Remove the residual sealant on the motor end cover and mounting surface.

![](images/848692a6a990352fa970976677886b511f8f649d48831fa0f1e5fd40e71a5eae.webp)

l. As shown in the figure, apply glue to the motor end cover, with the adhesive track along the inner side of the bolt hole. Specification of sealant: TONSAN 1596F

![](images/49fc1461c1b54bb67824ef69f313762ed02cb2ddaaca3bb42765c509e2c4acc0.webp)

m. Pay attention to checking the O-ring of coolant inlet pipe during installation to ensure that the Oring is installed in place.

n. Install the fixing bolts in diagonal order.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear drive electric powertrain in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

![](images/cba738553fe2456cae7f1fac7a572dfe0eae779d4443a0498abc2d21bffcffe8.webp)

a. Record the motor zero-position barcode on the motor. After the assembly is completed, use VDS to perform the motor electronic control zeroposition calibration. Refer to: Zero-position calibration

b. Replace the damaged fixing clips and cable ties, and fix them firmly. c. Add coolant. Refer to: Replace coolant (cooling system) d. Fill the rear drive transmission gear oil. Refer to: Replacing rear drive transmission gear oil e. After installation, start the vehicle and conduct a road test inspection.

### Removal procedures

0 Tip: This manual takes the removal and installation of the left differential oil seal as an example. For the removal and installation of the right differential oil seal, please refer to the left side.

1. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the rear drive half shaft assembly. Refer to: Rear drive half shaft assembly
3. Remove the differential oil seal

![](images/d5a5b6c635868bcb2a35cc3131848e8427e182393d118c219a679f7b62ae6398.webp)

a. Remove the differential oil seal with the removal tools for oil seal.

### i Caution:

The differential oil seal must be replaced after removal.
When removing the differential oil seal, avoid damaging the differential oil seal mounting base.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the differential oil seal in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Install the differential oil seal on the installation tool for rear motor half shaft oil seal. Special tool: installation tool for rear motor half shaft oil seal
b. Align the installation tool for rear motor half shaft oil seal with the differential oil seal mounting base hole.
c. Gently tap the installation tool for rear motor half shaft oil seal with a hammer to install the differential oil seal, so as to ensure that the differential oil seal and oil seal lip are smooth without bumps.
d. After all components are installed, perform road test inspection to ensure that the differential oil seal does not leak oil.

### 3.8.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. When the parts of vehicle control system are detected to be damaged, they should be replaced as a whole. Disassembly and removal operations are strictly prohibited; otherwise the normal operation of other parts may be affected.

2. Do not remove any parts or components or connectors of the system from their installation positions to avoid damage.

3. Before repairing the vehicle controller, be sure to power off the vehicle, turn off all electrical loads, and disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).

4. The reliability of the parts of vehicle control system is high. When the vehicle or drive motor is abnormal, first check whether the related mechanical components are in good condition, and whether the system connectors, wiring harnesses and ground wires are in good contact.

5. Faults of the vehicle control system mainly include wiring harness faults and connector faults, which are generally broken wiring harness, poor contact of connector, connector terminal being pulled out or not plugged into the bottom, and parts grounded.

6. It is rare for the wiring harnesses to be broken in the middle, and most of them are broken at the connector, so it is especially important to carefully check the wiring harnesses at the sensor and connector.

7. Poor contact may be caused by corrosion of connector terminals, external dirt entering terminals, or reduced contact pressure between connector plug and socket. If the connector is separated and plugged in again, its connection condition can be changed and normal contact can be restored.

8. During fault diagnosis, if there is no abnormality when checking the wiring harness and connector, and the fault disappears after reconnection, it can be considered that the wiring or connector is faulty.

9. Do not prick the wiring harness with fine needle for checking the electrical signals of the system;

10.When replacing the vehicle controller, handle it with care to avoid damage. Any impact or falling off may cause great damage to its performance.

11.Tighten the fixing bolt or nut to the specified torque.

12.When performing arc welding for the vehicle, be sure to disconnect the anode and cathode cables of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). If necessary, the vehicle controller and other control units can be disassembled to avoid damage to the vehicle controller caused by high voltage power during arc welding. When repairing the vehicle body near the vehicle controller or sensor, special care should be taken to avoid damaging these electronic components.

13.When installing or removing the vehicle controller, the operator should first make himself grounded to remove the static electricity; otherwise, the static electricity of human body may damage the circuit of vehicle controller.

14.All power supply systems used in automobiles are cathode GND. When installing the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), special attention should be paid to the fact that the anode and cathode should not be connected reversely to avoid damaging electronic components.

### 3.8.3.1 Warnings and precautions

15.In case of a system fault, if the system fault is not eliminated after the diagnostics device clears the DTC, the DTC will remain when the DTC reading step is performed again until the fault is eliminated, and the historical fault code should also be cleared after maintenance.

### 1. System Overview

a. The core control component of vehicle control system is the vehicle controller, which mainly collects vehicle information, identifies the driver's intention, controls vehicle operation and vehicle diagnosis, etc. It can manage, coordinate and monitor each link of the vehicle power chain to improve the energy utilization efficiency of the vehicle and ensure the safety and reliability.

### 3.8.6.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021 ” “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Vehicle Controller (BYD)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/b31da79f5d321af305b2b6dd821380d83de713a20518fc98696d3c74231419b1.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of the vehicle controller without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021 “New Tang EV 2021 General” “ECU module” → “Vehicle Controller (BYD)”

6. Read data flow

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

### Diagnostic steps

![](images/84d2be9476499b2eec971688c142f7251cb1dc543738acbf4e93c31727419ac1.webp)

a. Read and clear the DTC. Refer to: DTC reading and clearing
b. Check if the fault code exists.

Diagnose it as an occasional fault, and check whether the corresponding connector is loose or damaged, and whether the wiring harness terminal is corroded.

Yes

![](images/08049ac7e2ec8fe7031c4cf4d680f9a554d4e04a399cea2f3ad01c99dcb6c7fb.webp)

a. Read and check the data flow "Collision warning" Refer to: Read data flow
b. Check whether the vehicle suffers from a collision.

Yes

Repair the SRS.

![](images/25a4f7e4ac3c4d4383912a03d3f0d062dd70caa10d4cd385cc2de72bfe6b0507.webp)

a. Read and clear the DTC of SRS. Refer to: DTC reading and clearing
b. Check if the fault code exists.

View the DTC list of SRS for troubleshooting. Refer to: DTC list (DTC)

![](images/dc5e3669bd11bc9a374082b673547e83e75c2f77cfa75a5043ff61442c3f03cd.webp)

a. When the vehicle is OFF, disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and wait for 90s.
b. Disconnect the wiring harness connector K118 of vehicle controller and the wiring harness connector KG10 of SRS electronic control unit.
c. Measure the resistance between the terminal 33 of K118 and terminal 46 of KG10 with a digital multimeter.

![](images/e045ac4e91424ed7019c0dd8768bf5fa670d6d9b0c39488956c314e1713df352.webp)

Resistance:
![](images/07fb4f786dd083975b30e2de704751f9da7b7da2707c942e09461d511918377f.webp)

d. Check whether the result is normal?

Repair or replace the collision signal wiring harness.

Yes

![](images/e8308a07f712e7249a35889228c577de93191d16c26ed15e03680add214283a2.webp)

a. Replace the vehicle controller with a new one and restore the vehicle.
b. Perform VIN self-learning for vehicle controller. Refer to: Self-learning of VIN V
c. Perform inclination calibration for the vehicle. Refer to: Inclination calibration

d. Clear all module fault codes, and perform the test drive for functional inspection. e. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

Follow the above diagnostic steps and check again.

### Check the electronic accelerator pedal assembly

1. Check whether the connector of electronic accelerator pedal assembly is connected in place, and reconnect it in case of falling off or looseness.
2. Check whether the electronic accelerator pedal assembly is damaged or loose, and replace it if it is broken or deformed; If the electronic accelerator pedal assembly is loose, re-tighten the fixing bolts.
3. Check whether the accelerator pedal mounting bracket assembly is damaged or loose, and replace it if it is broken or deformed; f the accelerator pedal mounting bracket assembly is loose, re-tighten the fixing bolts and nuts.
4. Press the electronic accelerator pedal to end and confirm that the electronic accelerator pedal can return to the original position within 400ms after release.

### 3.8.7.2 Inclination calibration

0 Tip:

After replacing the vehicle controller, be sure to perform inclination calibration for it.

### 1. Preparations

a. Drive the vehicle into the maintenance station and activate the parking brake. b. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly c. Power off the vehicle and disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).

Remove the rear left door sill shield assembly. Refer to: Rear door sill shield assembly

3. Remove the lower left shield assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left shield assembly of dashboard

4. Remove the front left door sill shield assembly. Refer to: Front door sill shield assembly

5. Remove the left B-pillar lower shield assembly. Refer to: B-pillar lower shield assembl
6. Remove the driver seat assembly. Refer to: Driver seat assembly

7. Remove the vehicle controller.

![](images/88e50f8b21d489463c90fff1e89c817ad47157b97f5d47e0cabbd99af0a2886b.webp)

a. After installation, check that the electronic accelerator pedal assembly should work properly.

### 4.1.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Be sure to perform thorough inspection before repair or replacement of parts.
2. Try to keep the working environment clean while working to prevent foreign matters from entering the parts.
3. Clean disassembled parts (except rubber parts) with detergent and dry them.
4. After installation, the fasteners must be checked according to the tightening torque.
5. When installing bolts and nuts, fix the bolts with a wrench, so that they do not rotate with the nuts.
6. During installation, the installation order of the bolts connecting the tow arm assembly, the front control arm assembly and the rear steering knuckle is to install the bolts connecting the front control arm assembly and the rear steering knuckle first, and then install the bolts connecting the tow arm assembly and the rear steering knuckle.
7. Be sure to check the four-wheel alignment after repairing the suspension parts.
8. Perform a road test on the vehicle on the premise of ensuring safety and complying with all traffic regulations. Do not try any operation that may endanger the control over the vehicle.

### 4.1.5.1 Symptom list

![](images/9eaad1d87152c8dd0eca5b36b09e9c2227d0fcc4a71e6b4324585a7e47cfb84d.webp)

![](images/767e5c8c1e0aa890a45057d45059f4a7c3fae3372665be4fb1f0ecfc378f045c.webp)

![](images/361ee694443f3ae25225317035b1f49b2e8d0ddff799fdb8765dbed4c0f4b512.webp)

### Check front suspension

1. Check all connecting bushings for aging or damage.

2. Check all connecting bolts for looseness.

3. Check each connecting component for deformation and cracks.

4. Check the front stabiliser bar assembly.

a. Shake the front stabiliser bar assembly up and down by hand, and check whether the front stabiliser bar assembly gets loose. If so, it indicates that the bushing for the front stabiliser bar assembly is aged and needs to be replaced.

5. Measure the front vehicle body height.

a. Measure the heights of the (front) vehicle body on the left and right sides from the ground at the same position. The two measured heights should be the same.

0 Tip:

Make sure that the tyre pressure reaches the standard tyre pressure when measuring the vehicle body height.

### i Caution:

If the two measured heights are different, check whether the front suspension of the vehicle is damaged or deformed.

6. Check the front shock absorber pillar assembly

a. Visual inspection.

Check the front shock absorber strut assembly for oil leakage. Check the dust cover of the front shock absorber for damage. b. Road test. Stop the vehicle after driving it on a special test road or a road with poor road conditions for 10 km. Check whether the front shock absorber strut assembly leaks oil. Touch the shell of the front shock absorber strut assembly by hand. If the front shock absorber strut assembly is not hot, it indicates no resistance inside the assembly and no operation of it, and replacement of the assembly is required.

### 7. Check the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly.

a. Place the crowbar between the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly and the steering knuckle, and pry it up and down. • If the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly is firmly connected with the steering knuckle, it means that the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly is normal. If there is relative movement between the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly and the steering knuckle, replace the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly.

### Check rear suspension

1. Check all connecting bushings for aging or damage.
2. Check all connecting bolts for looseness.
3. Check each connecting component for deformation and cracks.

### 4. Check the rear stabiliser bar assembly

a. Shake the rear stabiliser bar assembly by hand, and check whether the rear stabiliser bar assembly gets loose. • If so, it indicates that the bushing for the rear stabiliser bar assembly is aged and needs to be replaced.

5. Measure the rear vehicle body height.

a. Measure the heights of the (rear) vehicle body on the left and right sides from the ground at the same position. The two measured heights should be the same.

0 Tip:

Make sure that the tyre pressure reaches the standard tyre pressure when measuring the vehicle body height. i Caution: If the two measured heights are different, check whether the rear suspension of the vehicle is damaged or deformed.

6. Check the rear shock absorber pillar assembly

a. Visual inspection.

Check the rear shock absorber strut assembly for oil leakage. Check the dust cover of the rear shock absorber for damage. b. Road test. Stop the vehicle after driving it on a special test road or a road with poor road conditions for 10 km. Check whether the rear shock absorber strut assembly leaks oil. Touch the shell of the rear shock absorber strut assembly by hand. If the rear shock absorber strut assembly is not hot, it indicates no resistance inside the assembly and no operation of it, and replacement of the assembly is required.

### 4.1.7.1 Front shock absorber pillar assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left shock absorber assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right shock absorber assembly, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
3. Remove the front left/right compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
4. Remove the front left and right wiper arm and blade assemblies. Refer to: Front wiper arm and blade assembly
5. Remove the ventilation cover assembly. Refer to: Ventilation cover assembly
6. Remove the front shock absorber pillar assembly
a. Remove one fixing bolt A and move away the front left wheel brake hose ①. Torque: 25 N•m
b. Disconnect the 2 fixing points B connected with the front shock absorber strut assembly, and move away the wheel speed sensor wiring harness ②.

![](images/24fc1f69c9da0fe803f2f8f7f4850d2e54c6ad31ffcf4f8327fe9381dc7be575.webp)

![](images/3bb5d4ef42d6c8bd19e548dddf444acadbd51c5520429e856251850fd8ab6527.webp)

c. Remove the fixing bolt A and move away the front stabiliser bar tie rod and ball joint assembly ①.

0 Tip: Fix the ball joint with an Allen wrench to prevent it from rotating with the nut.
Torque: 90 N•m

d. Remove the 2 fixing nuts B and pull out the bolts.

0 Tip:

When removing the nuts, fix the bolts with a tool to prevent them from rotating.

Torque: 230 N•m

![](images/32e4a0835c684cbaef2bbd5496d9e530ee5fbdd989ffb0f432dc6512e29b5245.webp)

e. Remove the 3 fixing nuts and remove the front shock absorber strut assembly from the underbody of the vehicle.

Caution:

An assistant is required to support the front shock absorber strut assembly to prevent it from falling off.

Torque: 50 N•m

### Disassembly procedure

1. Disassemble the front shock absorber pillar assembly a. Fix the front shock absorber strut assembly on the working stand.

![](images/dd4cd7665d17ad061ed6bd621d4af27dd8bb2bbd662c7ed963718672ac76793c.webp)

b. Install the spring compressor. c. Compress the spiral spring of front shock absorber until it is separated from the upper seat assembling unit of front shock absorber spring.

i Caution: Do not use electric or pneumatic tools.

![](images/192d704fe52f83cc012865a4d2f82f49fb91297dd7a14849562ccda268d4b8b9.webp)

d. Remove the dust cover of front shock absorber and remove the lock nut.

Special tool: removal and installation tool for
shock absorber nut
Torque: 85 N•m

e. Remove the upper support assembling unit of front shock absorber, the bearing assembling unit of front shock absorber, the buffer block assembling unit of front shock absorber, the upper seat assembling unit of front shock absorber spring, the dust cover of front shock absorber, the spiral spring of front shock absorber, and the lower cushion pad of front shock absorber spring in order.

### 1. Check the damper assembly of front shock absorber:

a. Compress and stretch the damper of front shock absorber for more than 4 times to check whether the working damping force is normal. If not, replace the damper.

b. Check whether the bearing assembling unit of front shock absorber is damaged. If so, replace it.

### Assembly procedure

1. Assemble the front shock absorber strut assembly in an order reverse to its disassembly and pay attention to the following:

a. Install the lower cushion pad of front shock absorber spring by aligning it with its positioning hole.
b. Fit the lower end of the spiral spring of front shock absorber with the groove of the lower cushion pad of front shock absorber spring.
c. Replace the lock nut.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front shock absorber strut assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. After all bolts and nuts are installed, tighten them according to the specified torques. b. After installation, check for wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment

### 4.1.7.2 Front lower swing bar assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left lower swing bar assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right lower swing bar assembly, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly
3. Remove the front lower swing bar assembly

![](images/4bb6ee0384fc1823ef49c9f7de09736fbaa2e10690ee0e51382ccf86e1d90408.webp)

a. Remove one fixing bolt A and two fixing nuts B. Torque: 105 N•m

![](images/f0f0f61cbf3899f7477078e6e49bfd9b9a602eba9020acd8ab4df1c030cdb9a9.webp)

b. Remove the 2 fixing bolts. Torque: 210 N•m

![](images/4b5c8000dce61b18f83c7f65d1c61ca4d606003fa58ae6541ae75a123fa5c7ca.webp)

c. Remove one fixing bolt and nut, and remove the front lower swing bar assembly.

### 0 Tip:

When removing the bolt, fix the nut with a tool to prevent it from rotating.

Torque: 210 N•m

d. Check whether the front lower swing bar assembly is damaged and whether the rubber bushing is aged and damaged, and replace the front lower swing bar or bushing assembly in case of any damage or rubber aging.

Warning: Never reuse any repaired front lower swing bar and bushing assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front lower swing bar assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. When installing the mounting bolts after the lower front swing arm assembly, the bolts should first pass through the side with the mounting bracket.
b. After installation, check for front wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly.

0 Tip:

For the removal of the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly, please refer to the front steering knuckle. Refer to: Front steering knuckle

2. Check the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly.

a. Fix the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly and shake the ball pin back and forth five times.
b. Pull the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly up and down. If there is any gap, replace the assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

0 Tip:

Refer to the front steering knuckle for the installation of the front lower swing bar ball joint assembly. Refer to: Front steering knuckle
a. Install a new cotter pin.
b. Turn the slotted nut by 60°if its slot is not aligned with the pin hole of the ball joint.
c. Be careful not to damage the ball joint dust cover during installation.
d. After installation, check for front wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment

### 4.1.7.4 Front auxiliary frame assembly

#

Removal procedures
1. Remove the front wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly
3. Drain coolant (cooling system). Refer to: Replace coolant (cooling system)
4. Drain coolant from the battery temperature control system. Refer to: Replace coolant (battery temperature control system)
5. Remove the front left/right drive half shaft assembly. Refer to: Front drive half shaft assembly
6. Remove the electronic accelerator pedal assembly. Refer to: Electronic accelerator pedal assembly
7. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
8. Remove the front left/right compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
9. Remove the grille upper cover assembly. Refer to: Grille upper cover assembly
10.Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
11.Disable the high voltage power. Refer to: High voltage power disable and enable
12.Remove the charging and distribution assembly. Refer to: Charging and distribution assembly
13.Remove the electric coolant pump assembly Ⅰ. Refer to: Electric coolant pump assembly
14.Remove the electric compressor assembly. Refer to: Electric compressor assembly
15.Remove the front drive electric powertrain. Refer to: Front drive electric powertrain
16.Remove the battery thermal management coolant pump assembly. Refer to: Battery thermal management coolant pump assembly
17.Remove the front auxiliary frame assembly.

![](images/c89f8ef6ceae2a3add54cfeaaabe75601edf60c0866adab00fe329b93b8f6b23.webp)

a. Loosen the fixing clip of the coolant pipe ① and disconnect the 3 connectors of the electric power steering gear.

![](images/331b0cce464e07dd774c4417b0843a3396c79db237432671cd731896dc2d42ec.webp)

b. Lift the carpet, remove the 3 plastic nuts, and remove the dust cover II.

![](images/24848903bee07e1a30d6385885f54a1a76ada18baf08cf29b018879c71e1bf65.webp)

c. Remove one fixing bolt and disconnect the universal joint assembly from the electric power steering gear. Torque: 40 N•m

![](images/c420592598ed3cad3f1f55985312b0b1aed63d35197cc978159596d2a70140b9.webp)

d. Lift the front auxiliary frame assembly with a hydraulic lifting platform until the assembly is slightly stressed. e. Remove 2 fixing bolts A, 2 fixing bolts B and 4 fixing bolts C, lower the hydraulic lifting platform, and move out the front auxiliary frame assembly.

i Caution: Pay attention to moving away or avoiding interfering parts during lowering.

Torque of bolt A: 105 N•m Torque of bolt B: 25 N•m Torque of bolt C: 200 N•m

f. Remove the fixing bolts and nuts of the front left and right lower swing bar assemblies, and remove these assemblies. g. Remove the front and rear stopper bushings of the front auxiliary frame.

![](images/4b0f8cd6899323c808d31dcbe8cc0d0dffbf0bf75265a3cf3cd3e6c57064fdfa.webp)

### 4.1.7.4 Front auxiliary frame assembly

h. Remove the 4 fixing bolts A and remove the front stabiliser bar assembly ①. Torque of bolt A: 50 N•m
i. Remove the 2 fixing bolts and nuts B, and remove the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly ②. Torque of bolt B: 120N•m

### 18.Check the front auxiliary frame assembly

a. Check whether the front auxiliary frame body assembly is deformed and cracked and whether the rubber bushing is aged and damaged, and replace the damaged front auxiliary frame body or bushing assembly if the front auxiliary frame body assembly is deformed or damaged or the rubber bushing is aged. Never attempt to repair them.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front auxiliary frame assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The bolts for connecting the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly and the front auxiliary frame assembly should be installed from the rear, and the left fixing bolts and nuts should be tightened before the right ones.
b. After all bolts and nuts are installed, tighten them according to the specified torques.
c. After installation, check for wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment
d. Road test.

### 4.1.7.5 Front stabiliser bar assembly

Refer to the front auxiliary frame assembly for removal and installation of the front stabiliser bar assembly. Refer to: Front auxiliary frame assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the rear left shock absorber assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the rear right shock absorber assembly, please refer to the rear left one.

### Removal procedures

2. Remove the rear shock absorber pillar assembly

![](images/ade133db2afacd93b4068bd0224d08f2e652a795bc6692ef9f016386bb1899a1.webp)

a. Remove one fixing bolt and move away the rear wheel brake hose. Torque: 25 N•m

b. Remove the 2 fixing nuts A, and remove the rear stabiliser bar tie rod and ball joint assembly ①.

c. Remove the 2 fixing nuts B and pull out the bolts. Torque: 230 N•m

![](images/cca08c47a473cd7ad43be740f45dcf97439d49fee94cf55074fb01d60d618e95.webp)

d. Remove the left handrail ① of the boot and the maintenance hatch cover assembly ② for the left shock absorber of the boot.

e. Remove the 3 fixing nuts and remove the rear shock absorber strut assembly from the underbody of the vehicle.

### Disassembly procedure

1. Disassemble the rear shock absorber pillar assembly a. Fix the rear shock absorber strut assembly on the working stand b. Install the spring compressor. c. Compress the spiral spring of rear shock absorber until it is separated from the upper support assembling unit of rear shock absorber.

![](images/64e08a0b90010b355e7ab92f9651f7612dbee7f732f05bdfb918c4c5201fa6d4.webp)

i Caution: Do not use electric or pneumatic tools.

![](images/82d6f3b61ae1cd9127cde93bd624f4c9bb1fef50804f6f959e80b3e0a827fa76.webp)

d. Remove the dust cover of rear shock absorber and remove the lock nut. Special tool: removal and installation tool for shock absorber nut Torque: 85 N•m
e. Remove the upper support assembling unit of rear shock absorber, the dust cover of rear shock absorber, the buffer block assembling unit of rear shock absorber, the spiral spring of rear shock absorber, and the lower cushion pad of rear shock absorber spring in order.

### 1. Check the damper assembly of rear shock absorber

a. Compress and stretch the damper of rear shock absorber for more than 4 times to check whether the working damping force is normal. If not, replace the damper.

### Assembly procedure

1. Assemble the rear shock absorber strut assembly in an order reverse to its disassembly and pay attention to the following: a. Install the lower cushion pad of rear shock absorber spring by aligning it with its positioning hole. b. Fit the lower end of the spiral spring of rear shock absorber with the groove of the lower cushion pad of rear shock absorber spring.

![](images/28e5cfaef7276f0616e88ed1c426b4a27c60b76c352307b6fd07a160daa4d832.webp)

d. Replace the lock nut.

c. Rotate in a direction shown in the figure to align the upper support assembling unit of rear shock absorber.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear shock absorber strut assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. After all bolts and nuts are installed, tighten them according to the specified torques. b. After installation, check for rear wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the
cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Disable the high voltage power. Refer to: High voltage power disable and enable
4. Remove the rear left/right wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
5. Remove the battery pack rear mudguard assembly. Refer to: Battery pack rear mudguard
assembly
6. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard
assembly
7. Drain coolant (cooling system). Refer to: Replace coolant (cooling system)
8. Remove the rear left/right drive half shaft assembly Refer to: Rear drive half shaft assembly
9. Remove the front right control arm assembly. Refer to: Front right control arm assembly

12.Remove the rear left and right control arm assemblies. Refer to: Rear control arm assembly

![](images/9a02e1ee0e58b6b53a5d9b021305b13371514b8e55276b6a6d789ea07c609a61.webp)

### 1. Check the rear auxiliary frame assembly

a. Check whether the rear auxiliary frame assembly is deformed and cracked and whether the rubber bushing is aged and damaged, and replace the damaged rear auxiliary frame assembly or bushing assembly if the auxiliary frame assembly is deformed or damaged or the rubber bushing and limit bushing are aged. Never attempt to repair them.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear auxiliary frame assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. After all bolts and nuts are installed, tighten them according to the specified torques.

b. After installation, check for rear wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment
c. Road test.

### Removal procedures

1. Lift the vehicle.
2. Remove the rear stabiliser bar fitting assembly

![](images/12dbe26f143ea8fbae6e33bbe34ce23955b56b1677a615dd2085d5d8c6096d99.webp)

a. Remove the 2 fixing nuts (one on the left and one on the right).

0 Tip:

Fix the ball joint with an Allen wrench to prevent it from rotating with the nut.

Torque: 90 N•m

![](images/3c7e3638826b101f5af234a119073bff07eb8aa1f4de163688a989f73f2b8de9.webp)

b. Remove the 4 fixing bolts and remove the rear stabiliser bar assembly. Torque: 50 N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear stabiliser bar assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. After all bolts and nuts are installed, tighten them according to the specified torques. b. After installation, check for rear wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front left control arm assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

### 4.2.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Precautions for removal and installation of tyre assembly

i Caution: Do not hold the rim with fingers when removing the wheel, in order to avoid crushing fingers.

### 2. Precautions for tyre transposition

i Caution:

Tyre transposition at regular intervals is required due to different driving conditions and driving habits.
Generally, tyre transposition is performed every 24,000 km of the vehicle's travelling mileage.

### 1. Function

a. Tyres are in direct contact with the road surface and they are key components of the vehicle. They can:

alleviate the impact on the vehicle during its running, and ensure that the vehicle has good ride comfort and driving smoothness;
ensure good adhesion between tyres and road surface to improve the traction, braking and passing performance of the vehicle;
bear the weight of the vehicle.

### 4.2.4.1 Exploded view of components

Wheel assembly

![](images/618bcb2ccd364ec050cab6e9374a37d096a1e7e39d02a1e2d37ca320aaa94bea.webp)

T-4302A15

![](images/7fa8496e4e72986143cf34c48d83436ca255b6a05ae56d98162767f9953ad82c.webp)

![](images/7b1c65c1e22f7f5b0224052ffb49fab9faefd67b5c3817445450f052f67951a2.webp)

### Check tyres

1. Check the wheel specifications.

a. Check the specifications and sizes of tyres and rims to ensure that those with recommended sizes are installed on the vehicle. Tyre specifications: 265/40 R22, 255/50 R20

### 2. Check tyre pressure

a. Check whether the tyre pressure reaches the standard value, and make adjustment if it does not.

Tyre pressure: 260kPa Tyre pressure (for rear wheels of the vehicle with above 4 seats): 290 kPa

0 Tip:

The tyre pressure should not be lower than 10% of the standard tyre pressure at normal temperature.

b. Check the tyre valve for air leakage with soapy water.

0 Tip:

Remove the tyre valve caps, and apply a proper amount of soapy water on each tyre valve to observe whether it leaks air.

### 3. Check for tyre wear

a. Check the tyres for cracks, damages, etc., and replace them as appropriate.
b. Check whether there are gravels or other foreign matters in the groove on the tyre tread, and remove them if any.
c. Check the tyres for abnormal wear, and if any, find out the cause.

### 4. General tyre wear

0 Tip:

Repair the faulty parts according to the wear, and replace the tyres or perform wheel transposition.

![](images/f78ac15b9a73584c0ba46022c00e8d16c688f10f98fe06488cdb8a051737e10f.webp)

a. Insufficient tyre pressure will cause quick wear of tyre shoulder, tyre deflection and increase in rolling resistance.

![](images/06e692ca6f68b5f424798f023705308b3c748449ac5f9b7dc081d99bba347a73.webp)

b. Excessive tyre pressure will cause quick wear in the middle of tyre crown and decrease in the buffering capacity of the tyre.

![](images/d8b7ce04ff29af14b12620013ddb03e822fdaf71175ce0467c9471d10479081d.webp)

c. Excessive (or insufficient) toe-in of front and rear wheels will cause feather-like tyre wear.

![](images/b733e9caf8aefe4453ecfc54c092e5e9e6adbc784d34c82a7691dd7c078f302a.webp)

d. Tyre wear on one side will cause outward inclination.

![](images/3ce41b2c1197ae59fc244fdfb4819a5a9d076c898fd2e7099e21f6d0fb1a4e6b.webp)

e. Observe the wear mark at the bottom of the tyre groove. If the tread is worn to the wear mark, the tyre must be replaced.

### Check axial clearance of hub bearing

1. Check axial clearance of hub bearing

a. Lift the vehicle.
b. Remove the wheel assembly.
c. Install appropriate flat washers and wheel nuts and tighten them. Tightening torque: 130N•m

![](images/dd17f0b73eb27c6ee508fdcdccc45a761e9c7b310ae01067c3e36f856cb84a65.webp)

d. Put the dial gauge as shown in the figure, shake the brake disc back and forth in the direction of the drive half shaft, and measure the axial clearance of bearing.

Standard value: 0\~0.05mm

### Wheel Balance

0 Tip:

The unbalance of tyres will cause the vibration of wheels (especially front wheels) when they rotate at a high speed. Such vibration will make the front wheels swing, affecting the driving safety and smoothness of the vehicle and increasing the wear of tyres. Therefore, it is very important to test and adjust the dynamic balance of tyres.

### i Caution:

If sundries in the tyre crown are not removed, they will fly out of the tyre under the centrifugal force, easily causing personal injury. Check the tyre crown and sidewall for defects that may affect the wheel balance.

b. Remove the balancing weight. c. Inflate the tyre to the standard tyre pressure. Tyre pressure: 260kPa

0 Tip: The tyre pressure should not be lower than 10% of the standard tyre pressure at normal temperature.

2. Check the wheel balance a. Install the wheel correctly on the balancing machine.

![](images/df2411f71904e6dc18c8eb641208f0a5b5c6ece1b75cd6def86e848563dfa4c3.webp)

b. Fix the tyre, and input the three parameters, namely width of wheel rim, diameter of wheel rim, and distance from the outer edge of wheel rim to the balancing machine.
c. Put down the protective cover and start the balancing machine, with the balancing speed set as 450 r/min, to start the measurement.
d. Stop rotating the tyre and then open the protective cover, turn the tyre by hand, and read the unbalance amount through the left and right display screens to determine the unbalanced position.

3. Adjust the wheel balance

### i Caution:

Do not reuse any balancing weight, and always use the genuine balancing weight of the OEM.
Do not paste one balancing weight on another.

a. Add a corresponding balancing weight to the unbalanced position according to the unbalance amount displayed on the balancing machine.

i Caution: • Be sure to clean the fitting surface of the wheel before installing the balancing weight.
b. When installing a balancing weight on the wheel, align the centre of the balancing weight with the position (or angle) indicated by the wheel balancing machine.
c. The balancing weight added to the wheel should not exceed 40g on the inner or outer side and 70g on both sides, and the maximum residual unbalance amount should not exceed 10g on the inner or outer side and 15g on both sides.

### Wheel transposition

1. Wheel transposition adjustment

![](images/c678d6315c31f5acde3f030e4e09252d759f54e6cbd8331bf437b75c7f6c44ce.webp)

a. Transpose the wheels in the sequence shown in the figure.

①: Non-directional tyres
②: Directional tyres

### 0 Tip:

In order to make the tire wear evenly and prolong the service life of the tyre, it is recommended to perform wheel transposition according to the maintenance schedule. However, the most time suitable for wheel transposition depends on the driver's driving habits and road conditions.
After wheel transposition, it is necessary to rematch and learn the tyre pressure monitoring module. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring module matching
Self-learning of tyre pressure monitoring module: After parking for above 30min and driving for above 10min when the vehicle speed exceeds 40km/h, self-learning is successful.

### Four-whee alignment

0 Tip:

The front wheel king pin caster angle and inclination angle and front or rear wheel camber angle are not adjustable. If they are not within the specified values, check the suspension components for bending or damage. If the suspension components are bent or damaged, be sure to replace the damaged parts. Do not try to repair them by tapping and other methods. If the front wheel toe-in is correct, but the steering angle is not within the specified range or the left inner steering angle is different from the right one, check the suspension components for bending or damage. If the suspension components are bent or damaged, be sure to replace the damaged parts. Do not try to repair them by tapping and other methods.

### 1. Check before alignment

i Caution: Do not try to align the parts by straightening, and damaged parts must be replaced.

a. Release the parking brake to avoid incorrect measurement.
b. Make sure that the suspension device is not changed.
c. Make sure that the 4 tyres are in the same size and correct, and the tire pressure is within the specified pressure range.
d. Make sure that there is no people or extra load in the vehicle.
e. Check whether each fixing point of suspension is loose and deformed, and check that the clearance of each ball head of suspension is not too large.
f. Check the vibration of the wheel.
g. Check that the heights of the corresponding positions on both sides of the vehicle should be consistent.
h. When the wheels are in a straight forward position, the steering wheel must be centred.
i. Carry out a dynamic balance test on the wheel. Install the wheel back on the vehicle after the test.
j. Make the wheel device bounce up and down for several times to stabilise the suspension.

2. Test

0 Tip: Check the wheel alignment according to the operating instructions of the four-wheel aligner.

3. Adjust the rear wheel toe-in

![](images/39c59f15833ae5785c555399fc127bc2623c113bdc29b7a7855729f39805deb8.webp)

a. Fix the adjusting sleeve ① of the rear control arms on both sides with a wrench, and loosen the lock nuts A and B.
b. Rotate the adjusting sleeve ① of the rear control arms on both sides until the rear wheel toe-in is correct. Rear wheel toe-in (Single side):0°±0.08° (Required absolute difference between left and right sides<0.03°)

c. After adjustment, fix the adjusting sleeve ① of the rear control arms on both sides and tighten the

Torque: 90±5N•m

### 4. Adjust the front wheel toe-in

a. Lock the steering wheel assembly to prevent it from rotating.

![](images/8560a9afc72505169216b2ebbdfa107c0d8c2ca9dc7033a5aec57132f1a39e32.webp)

b. Loosen the lock nut A and elastic clamp B on the left and right sides of the steering tie rod.
c. Twist the toe-in adjusting rods ① on both sides as required to adjust and measure the toe-in value until it reaches the specified value. Front wheel toe-in (Single side):0°±0.08° (Required absolute difference between left and right sides<0.03°)
d. Tighten the lock nut A and install the sheath elastic clamp B. Torque: 90±5N•m

e. After adjustment of the front wheel toe-in, check whether the steering wheel is in the middle position, and adjust it if not.
f. Perform the steering angle calibration and zeroing according to the prompt of the diagnostics device.

### 4.2.7.1 Wheel assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left wheel assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of front right, rear right and rear left wheel assemblies, please refer to the front left one.

### 1. Preparations

a. Drive the vehicle into the lifting position, activate the parking brake, and power off the vehicle.
b. Use a trimming cover removal clamp to remove the protective trimming covers of wheel nuts.
c. Unscrew the wheel nuts.
d. Lift the vehicle.

2. Remove the wheel assembly a. Remove the 5 fixing nuts of the wheel assembly and remove the wheel assembly. Torque: 130 N•m

![](images/2f6ecddd0bff6d6ade6ffc182e71ce4cc3fa997701d278b7fe63bc19be5e5b0c.webp)

![](images/b2ce5621f85e1f7418f25d90bcd4ab0efa750bd2c7ba986c6f276a41a80556a6.webp)

b. Remove the wheel core cover assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the wheel assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

![](images/16a447b1318b6c3125a709f90a174d37c83ba723cc8f1f787542067ef7b06793.webp)

a. Remove rust and dust from the wheel, hub and brake disc mounting surface.
b. Install the wheel assembly and pre-tighten the 5 wheel nuts.
c. Lower the vehicle, tighten the wheel nuts as per the order shown in the figure, and drive the vehicle away from the lift station. Torque: 130 N•m

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

2. Remove the tyres

a. Removal the valve cap.
b. Loosen the valve core with a valve core wrench to release the tyre pressure. Screw out the valve core after the tyre pressure is completely released.

![](images/ec60dec56e7248a58a1d8868e56cb8a1fc52155419a3e3ecd807990ee9add38a.webp)

c. Place the tyre onto the tyre changer. Adjust the clearance between the wheel rim edge and the separating shovel to the range of 10\~20mm. Step on the pedal to separate the tyre from the wheel rim;

### i Caution:

When using a tyre changer, place the tyre vertically to prevent the rim from being damaged by the separating shovel.
When removing and installing tyres, avoid the valve position to prevent the valve and the tyre pressure monitoring module from being damaged.
Separate the tyre and the rim at different positions for 2\~3 times.
d. Press the other side of the tyre out of the rim using the same method.
e. Fix the tyre on the working plate and adjust its position.
f. Press the lifting lever to make the dismantling head contact with the rim edge.

![](images/fa9ccfaf26340379bf14fc16a2debe5db4d870b4046bb99200b8d738c35ce380.webp)

### i Caution:

Pay attention to the distance between the dismantling head and the rim to avoid causing damage to the rim surface. Avoid the valve position to prevent the valve and the tyre pressure monitoring module from being damaged.

g. Use a tyre crowbar to pry the upper edge of the tyre to the top of the dismantling head, and press the rotary switch to separate one side of the tyre from the rim.

### i Caution:

Fix the rim firmly and check it before starting the machine.
Never separate tyres by hand when the machine is running.
Be careful not to damage the tyre opening to prevent air leakage.

h. Lift the tyre obliquely upward, use a tyre crowbar to pry the lower edge of the tyre to the dismantling head with, and press the rotary switch to completely separate the tyre from the rim.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the tyre in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Apply a little lubricant to the lip of the tyre, and fit part of the lower edge of the tyre on the rim.

![](images/1b73ee37084d4e6b940b8de09f1e2428af2beb07fdf852972daa8022a85b08f6.webp)

b. Adjust the position of the rim so that the mounting head of the tyre changer is at the position shown in Figure A, and make sure that the tyre pressure monitoring module is in the area indicated by the hatching.

c. Apply lubricant to the wheel rim and tyre. Fit the lower bread onto the wheel rim. Rotate the wheel rim so that the whole lower bread is mounted onto the wheel rim. Make sure that the bead does not contact the tyre pressure monitoring module during the mounting.

i Caution: Be careful not to damage the tyre opening to prevent air leakage.

d. Install the tread on the other side of the tyre using the same method.

![](images/1575a8ad7f375bd066d4905942e81b70cdb2b740ee33d56844887e82a161dffd.webp)

e. Install the valve core and tighten it, and then inflate the tyre to the specified tyre pressure. f. Install the valve cap and tighten it.

2. Check the wheel balance. Refer to: Wheel balance

### i Caution:

Make sure that the lift is in a good condition before lifting the vehicle. Before lifting the vehicle, check whether the lifting position is correct. Never support any part except the lifting point. Make sure nobody is around or under the vehicle when lifting the vehicle.

### i Caution:

Do not rub the dust cover of drive half shaft with other parts or have it collided with sharp objects for a long time during vehicle running or its removal, to avoid causing damage.
Avoid contaminating parts during maintenance to prevent the ingress of foreign matters.
Please clean the outer surfaces of parts before disassembly and assembly.
Clean disassembled parts (except rubber parts) with detergent and dry them.

3. Important warnings for road test

A Warning: Perform a road test on the vehicle on the premise of ensuring safety and complying with all traffic regulations. Do not try any operation that may endanger the control over the vehicle.

### 1. Function

a. The drive half shaft assembly transmits the power from the transmission to wheels, and it contains a constant velocity universal joint to ensure the direction variability and continuity of power transmission.

### 2. Working Principle:

a. The transmission transmits the power of drive motor to the drive half shaft assembly, both ends of which are provided with a constant velocity universal joint each to ensure the stable power transmission when the wheel position is changing constantly.

### Check the drive half shaft assembly

1. Check the drive half shaft assembly

a. Check the inner dust cover and the outer dust cover on the drive half shaft assembly for any crack, damage or lubricating grease leakage and check whether the dust cover clip is loose or not. If any defects are checked, replace the dust cover and dust cover clamp.
b. Turn the drive half shaft assembly to make sure that the joint clearance between the external spline and the differential's internal spline is not too large.
c. Confirm that the drive half shaft assembly is free of twist and that its surface has no rust or cracks; otherwise, replace the drive half shaft assembly.
d. Check and make sure that the inner and outer CV joints swing or slide freely without any jamming.
e. Check whether the dust cover has wrinkled. If so, replace it.

### 4.3.7.1 Front drive half shaft assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left drive half shaft assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right drive half shaft assembly, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly
3. Remove the front drive half shaft assembly

![](images/75e25c960628b57641f7d42dd3f2efd1514145a6e43a2abb3914c91d37b944bc.webp)

a. Remove one fixing bolt and move away the front wheel brake hose. Torque: 25±2.5N•m

![](images/d68c16feac6b0b7d475a9b2183ec3bfed688b09d90098d3ecf1ce27cb8dd3456.webp)

b. Remove one fixing bolt and pull out the front wheel speed sensor assembly.

i Caution: Wrap the front wheel speed sensor assembly to avoid bumping.

Torque: 10 N•m

![](images/692a951fbfd17cc1ecc790619f23fa7cb14aa67353b8ac032fe29bee5f9c4546.webp)

c. Insert a screwdriver ① into the position shown in the figure, and remove the shaft head nut A.

### i Caution:

Use an auxiliary tool to restore the end lip of the shaft head nut to its original state, and then remove the shaft head nut. As the shaft head nut is a disposable part, it must be replaced after being removed each time.

Torque: 300±2N•m

d. Remove the split pin and the slotted nut C, and separate the tie rod from the steering knuckle using a ball joint remover. Torque: 50 N•m

e. Remove two fixing nuts A and one fixing bolt B, and separate the front lower swing bar ball joint from the front lower swing bar. Torque of nut A: 105 N•m Torque of bolt B: 105 N•m

f. Move the front steering knuckle outward, and take the outer CV joint spline of the front drive half shaft assembly out of the front steering knuckle.

### i Caution:

If necessary, tap the threaded end face of the outer CV joint using a rubber hammer to knock out the outer CV joint.
Avoid using a metal hammer; otherwise, deformation of threads and the spline will be caused due to impact.

![](images/e6055037c6411cd35457a327b3ef9105b3455d995c6c9ffe292ae9952eba1c06.webp)

g. Use a special tool ① to pry out the front drive half shaft assembly ②.

### i Caution:

Do not directly pull the half shaft with force. Be careful when using a special tool to avoid damaging the oil seal.
Never make the drive half shaft be in a natural drooping state during maintenance. Check the wear of the half shaft spline, and replace the drive half shaft assembly if the half shaft spline is seriously worn.
Check the spring retainer ring and replace it if damaged.
Plug the differential oil seal to prevent dust or foreign matters from entering the transmission.

Special tool: removal tool for rear motor half shaft

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front drive half shaft assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. During assembly and transportation, be sure to handle with care to avoid the contact and collision between the sealing sheath and hard objects such as the station apparatus rack and chassis parts.
b. Use solvent or brake cleaner to thoroughly clean the contact area between the half shaft and the differential, and then dry it with compressed air.
c. Replace the axle head nut.
d. During assembly, replace the sheath with a new one if there are signs of damage or scratch.
e. During installation, do not hold the sealing sheath by hand to prevent it from wrinkling.

![](images/00d886b9b6852552688d9034daaeab85bcdf81733359f2492fc61f154e18589d.webp)

f. During installation, use a special tool ① to protect the oil seal to avoid causing damage to it. Special tool: installation protection tool for motor half shaft oil seal

g. Install the inner CV joint end of the front drive half shaft onto the transmission output shaft until the locating retainer ring is locked.

![](images/e531d676614c6fcb824b8af556fb190c5c9c218188dca6a645669c261ca2f0ec.webp)

h. Use an auxiliary tool to bend the shaft head nut into the wedge groove on the shaft head.

i. Check the front wheel alignment and adjust it if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment

### 4.3.7.2 Rear drive half shaft assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the rear left drive half shaft assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the rear right drive half shaft assembly, please refer to the rear left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the rear drive half shaft assembly

![](images/5c2eaffba835f592d78d05cfb40d3869d50caf536a3519bee87119f30524bb99.webp)

a. Remove one fixing bolt A and one fixing bolt B, and pull out the rear wheel speed sensor.

i Caution: Wrap the rear wheel speed sensor to avoid bumping.

Torque: 10 N•m

![](images/1462744454880a15f72ea274a4c3a1b3d69b02622b3c4937928dba4b615c0b9b.webp)

b. Insert a screwdriver ① into the position shown in the figure, and remove the shaft head nut A.

### i Caution:

Use an auxiliary tool to restore the end lip of the shaft head nut to its original state, and then remove the shaft head nut. As the shaft head nut is a disposable part, it must be replaced after being removed each time.

Torque: 300±2N•m

![](images/f6f038bbb9266b5827ac4a26a10e5aeae404b8a7ddb4ddff0ebb1aa5bb728559.webp)

c. Remove one fixing bolt A and nut, and move away the rear control arm assembly.

### 0 Tip:

Use a wrench to fix the bolt to prevent it from rotating with the nut.

Torque: 180 N•m

d. Remove one fixing bolt B and nut, and move away the tow arm assembly.

### 0 Tip:

Use a wrench to fix the bolt to prevent it from rotating with the nut.

Torque: 180 N•m

e. Remove one fixing bolt C and nut, and move away the front control arm assembly.

### 0 Tip:

Use a wrench to fix the bolt to prevent it from rotating with the nut.

Torque: 180 N•m

![](images/2e6a4bccd163e9edf5ab491e70e9c6ff62313301bb2888b7f430ec3bbd1805dc.webp)

f. Remove one fixing nut and move away the rear stabiliser bar tie rod ①.

0 Tip:

Fix the ball joint with an Allen wrench to prevent it from rotating with the nut.

Torque: 90 N•m

g. Move the rear steering knuckle outward, and take out the outer CV joint spline of the rear drive half shaft assembly from the rear steering knuckle.

### i Caution:

If necessary, tap the threaded end face of the outer CV joint using a rubber hammer to knock out the outer CV joint.
Avoid using a metal hammer; otherwise, deformation of threads and the spline will be caused due to impact.

![](images/3a5af5379f72aee8d092740fb1f6b65f60822bd8a02cf6da90ad36c236a4c146.webp)

h. Use a special tool ① to pry out the rear drive half shaft assembly ②.

### i Caution:

Do not directly pull the half shaft with force. Be careful when using a special tool to avoid damaging the oil seal.
Never make the drive half shaft be in a natural drooping state during maintenance. Check the wear of the half shaft spline, and replace the drive half shaft assembly if the half shaft spline is seriously worn.
Check the spring retainer ring and replace it if damaged.
Plug the differential oil seal to prevent dust or foreign matters from entering the transmission.

Special tool: removal tool for rear motor half shaft

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear drive half shaft assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. During assembly and transportation, be sure to handle with care to avoid the contact and collision between the sealing sheath and hard objects such as the station apparatus rack and chassis parts.
b. Use solvent or brake cleaner to thoroughly clean the contact area between the half shaft and the differential, and then dry it with compressed air.
c. Replace the axle head nut.
d. During assembly, replace the sheath with a new one if there are signs of damage or scratch.
e. During installation, do not hold the sealing sheath by hand to prevent it from wrinkling.

![](images/06a0a48f629093d3255ea915f2dcdf2e085554b4515668c8dde0a5b32580e9a6.webp)

f. During installation, use a special tool ① to protect the oil seal to avoid causing damage to it. Special tool: installation protection tool for motor half shaft oil seal

g. Install the inner CV joint end of the rear drive half shaft onto the transmission output shaft until the locating retainer ring is locked.
h. Make sure that the differential oil seal is normal, and remove the installation protection tool for motor half shaft oil seal.

![](images/718927513d3dbf78c998da0a1d13089a831aba67792ce90265ce752fef41cc71.webp)

i. Use an auxiliary tool to bend the shaft head nut into the wedge groove on the shaft head.

j. Check the rear wheel alignment and make adjustment if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment

### 4.4.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Place the vehicle on a level and dry ground when checking the steering system.

2. Check the wheel alignment after maintenance of the electric power steering gear.
3. Do not weld the steering gear and any parts of system bars in any way.
4. Keep the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) in good condition, because low SOC of this battery will lead to heavy steering.
5. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) before repairing the electric steering column.
6. Do move the vehicle when the steering wheel is locked; otherwise, the steering system parts will be damaged.
7. Carefully check whether the steering system parts are subjected to abnormal impact, and replace any damaged parts in time.
8. Before disconnecting the universal joint assembly, keep wheels in the front direction and fix the steering wheel to prevent it from turning; otherwise, the clock spring on the steering column will deviate from the centre position, or even be damaged due to too many turns of the steering wheel.
9. Comprehensively check the easiness and flexibility of steering after reinstallation of the steering system. No heavy steering should be felt and no looseness should be found when the steering wheel is turned.
10.Tighten the bolts/nuts of all steering system parts to the specified torques.

### 1. Overview of EPS System

a. EPS (Electric Power Steering) system is a steering system that uses the steering power provided by an EPS motor to assist a driver in performing steering operations. Like other control systems, this system consists of an EPS ECU, an actuator (EPS motor in the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly) and other related mechanical components.

b. The EPS system is designed based on a mechanical steering system, with the latest electronic technology and high-performance motor control technology applied to a vehicle steering system. Based on the original vehicle steering system, the following parts are modified and added for the EPS system: EPS electronic control unit, EPS motor, etc. The transmission mechanism of the system is driven by motor instead of traditional mechanical hydraulic mechanism. It can provide drivers with real-time steering wheel assistant power in various environments.

c. An EPS system generally consists of the following parts: EPS electronic control unit EPS Motor Related mechanical structure

d. The EPS motor (in the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly) provides the EPS system with assisting power, which is adjusted and controlled by the EPS ECU assembly in a real-time manner. Different powers are provided for different vehicle speeds to improve the vehicle steering feature, reduce operating force required in parking and low-speed running and improve operating stability in high-speed running, thereby increasing the active safety of the vehicle.

### 2. Functions of EPS system

a. Power-assistant control function

The power-assistant feature of the EPS is of vehicle speed sensing type. This means with the same steering wheel torque input, the target motor current changes with the vehicle speed, satisfying both the steering easiness and road feel requirements. The powerassistant feature of the EPS is characteristic of sectionalized power to guarantee steering easiness when the vehicle runs at low speeds and the operating stability and good road feel when the vehicle runs at high speeds.

b. Return-to-centre control function

During steering, the steering wheel has the automatic return function by virtue of its king pin caster angle and king pin inclination angle. Based on the mechanical steering mechanism, an EPS motor and speed reduction mechanism are added for the EPS system. The EPS system controls the steering return-to-centre of the EPS motor through the EPS electronic control unit, and together with the aligning torque produced by front wheel alignment, implements the steering return-to-centre action. This enables the steering wheel to quickly return to centre, inhibits steering wheel vibration, maintains road feel, increases steering sensitivity and stability, optimizes the steering returnability and shortens the convergence time. The return-to-centre control is implemented by adjusting the return-tocentre compensating current, which produces an aligning torque. The torque causes the steering wheel to return to centre along a direction.

c. Damping control function

When the vehicle runs at high speed, damping control is completed by controlling the damping compensation current to strengthen the road feel and improve the steering stability under high-speed running.
