### 4.4.7.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New
Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” “ECU module”
6. Read and clear the power steering (TRW) DTC

![](images/ad599ae1a4a4184f79c9777bb5c083b1e543bf4feadf4c460458ec3a97463223.webp)

a. Select "Power steering (TRW)" "Fault detection" to read the DTC.
b. Select "Power steering (TRW)" → "Clear fault" to clear the DTC.

7. Read and clear the DTC of the electric steering column (BYD)

![](images/e16024df3f02be2a14b44d9767a10b76d15e7d25842d4c0b368d1fd2f493ec21.webp)

a. Select Electric steering column (BYD)" → "Fault detection" to read the DTC.
b. Select "Electric steering column (BYD)" → "Clear fault" to clear the DTC.

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of the steering system without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New
Tang EV 2021 ” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module”
6. Read the power steering (TRW) data flow.

![](images/25528919312d13a1eef1102ac85f719679c9c7934684702be5d44dfbdd1cb5f4.webp)

a. Select "Power steering (TRW)" "Data flow" to read the data flow.

7. Read the data flow of the electric steering column (BYD).

a. Select "Electric steering column (BYD)" → "Data flow" to read the data flow.

3. Start the vehicle.

### Step 11 Check the electrically adjustable steering column ECU assembly

a. Replace the electrically adjustable steering column ECU with a new one.
b. Restore the vehicle, clear all module fault codes, and perform the test drive for functional inspection.
c. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

Follow the above diagnostic steps and check again.

### 1. Check the installation

a. Check whether the wiring harnesses of related components of the steering system are worn, pinched or cut, and check whether the connectors are connected correctly.
b. Check whether the fixing nuts and bolts of the steering gear assembly get loose. If so, tighten them to the standard torques.
c. Check whether the steering outer tie rod assembly gets loose. If so, replace the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly with a new one.
d. Check whether the dust cover for bellows of the steering gear is cracked or damaged. If so, replace the steering gear assembly with a new one.
e. Check whether the dust cover for the outer tie rod ball joint end of the steering tie rod is cracked or damaged. If so, replace the steering gear outer tie rod assembly.

### 1. Check the free clearance of steering wheel

a. Make the front wheels in a straight driving position.
b. Power off the vehicle.
c. Mark the top of the steering wheel.
d. Lean a ruler against the top of the steering wheel.
e. Measure the maximum distance that the steering wheel can turn left under the condition that the front wheels do not rotate.
f. Turn the steering wheel back to its original position.
g. Measure the maximum distance that the steering wheel can turn right under the condition that the front wheels do not rotate.
h. If the sum of the left and right measured values is not above 30mm, the free stroke of the steering wheel is normal; otherwise, check the steering system.

![](images/691f0a7787a0bdecbbbc4299ec39bb25dbbcc85022824619889fddfbeb54bf09.webp)

### Instructions for EPS steering angle information calibration

1. The steering angle of the EPS system should be re-calibrated after the steering wheel, steering column or steering gear is removed, replaced and reinstalled or four-wheel alignment is performed.

### Precautions for EPS steering angle information calibration

1. When performing calibrations with VDS, keep hands off the steering wheel so that the steering wheel is not affected by external forces; otherwise, serious damage faults may be caused.

2. Check for normal tyre pressure. Make the vehicle be supported by its wheels under normal load condition, and have nobody or only the driver sit in the vehicle.

3. Four-wheel alignment has been completed before EPS system calibration;

4. Make sure that the vehicle generates no obvious vibration, i.g. no closing of doors, bonnet, etc.

5. Check and confirm that the mechanical position of the steering wheel is at the middle zero point.

6. Make the wheels face the front.

### EPS steering angle information calibration process

### Instructions for writing software configuration word

1. The software for the steering system of the vehicle should be reconfigured after the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly is replaced. To write the configuration word, it is necessary to enter the corresponding interface according to the vehicle model and write the corresponding configuration word.

### Precautions for writing software configuration word

1. Writing software configuration word should be performed after replacement of the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly, four-wheel alignment or steering angle calibration of the vehicle is completed.
2. To write a configuration word, it is necessary to enter the corresponding interface of the VDS according to the vehicle model and select the corresponding configuration word. If the incorrect configuration word is selected, it may cause such problems as function mismatch and hand feeling mismatch.

### Process for writing software configuration word

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and wait for 90s. Refer to: Disconnect cathode of 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Remove the driver airbag module. Refer to: Driver airbag module
4. Remove the steering wheel assembly. a. Turn the steering wheel back to the centre, so that the front wheels face the front of the vehicle.

![](images/235af25d80e6192f0e8c6dc356650f6c51b1dbef0d0a0a4a913925fe1acd9bb9.webp)

b. Disconnect the connectors A and B of the steering wheel assembly, remove the fixing nut C of the steering wheel assembly, and remove the steering wheel assembly.

### i Caution:

Before removing the steering wheel, install the steering wheel fixing nut on the steering column until the end face of the nut is flush with the upper end face of the steering column, to prevent people from being hurt by excessive force during removal of the steering wheel.

### Torque: 35 N•m

![](images/991c320f640d40a2fb1af921bc3ef7ababda2eb1c75638583acea7fbc2eb1420.webp)

c. Remove the 2 fixing screws, and release the clamping tongue of the steering wheel switch set ①.
d. Turn over the steering wheel switch set ①, disconnect the 3 connectors and remove the steering wheel switch set ①.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the steering wheel assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. When installing the steering wheel switch set, avoid damaging wiring harnesses and connectors and make sure that the connectors are connected correctly. b. Centre the clock spring. Refer to: Centre the clock spring.

![](images/52a94d8e712b104f2931794ada346dd2b7124508e4272e20170e56c84c6beb2b.webp)

c. When installing the steering wheel assembly, align the fitting mark on the steering wheel assembly with that on the steering column.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Remove the lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard
4. Remove the lower left shield assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left shield assembly of dashboard
5. Remove the electronic accelerator pedal assembly. Refer to: Electronic accelerator pedal assembly
6. Remove the driver airbag module. Refer to: Driver airbag module
7. Remove the steering wheel assembly. Refer to: Steering wheel assembly.
8. Remove the upper shield assembly of multi-function switch. Refer to: Upper shield assembly of multi-function switch
9. Remove the lower shield assembly of multi-function switch. Refer to: Lower shield assembly of multi-function switch
10.Remove the clock spring. Refer to: Clock Spring
11.Remove the multi-function switch. Refer to: Multi-function switch
12.Remove the steering column and universal joint assembly

![](images/476dd085b976f5966d1e63ff27835efdb3079a1637b9c1be189768b0ec609194.webp)

a. Lift the carpet, remove the 3 nut-type plastic clips, and remove the dust cover II.

![](images/2c89dda1f3931f48f41161145865253d175bd3a55cbe7f7abb1a64eb954ab097.webp)

b. Remove one fixing bolt and disconnect the universal joint assembly from the electric power steering gear. Torque: 40±4 N•m

![](images/ebabd240533fab450378e8c8ba7d27250191b269f784e8c467b7f3f84f414c5d.webp)

![](images/b697d6d79277e7f62ed34a60ac78a009d560b3a3fc4ca837bbd00b1367e7ae0e.webp)

c. Disconnect connectors A and B, and disengage all wiring harness fixing clips on the steering column.

d. Remove one fixing bolt, disengage the wiring harness fixing clip, and move away the wiring harness junction box. Torque: 6 N•m.

e. Remove 2 fixing bolts A and 2 fixing nuts B, and remove the steering column and universal joint assembly.

Caution:

Prevent the steering column and universal joint assembly from falling off during removal.

Torque of bolt A: 30±3 N•m Torque of nut B: 30±3 N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the steering column and universal joint assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. When installing the steering column and universal joint assembly, install the upper fixing nut before the lower fixing bolt.
b. Check and confirm that the wheels are at the driving positions facing the front, and that the bolt hole at the lower end of the universal joint assembly is aligned with the missing tooth position on the pinion shaft of the steering gear, and install the universal joint assembly on the pinion shaft of the steering gear.

c. Confirm that the mounting bolt at the lower end of the universal joint assembly can be accurately fitted into the groove of the pinion shaft of the steering gear, so that the lower end of the universal joint is installed in place.

### i Caution:

The mounting bolt at the lower end of the universal joint assembly should be installed from the non-threaded side. The side of the universal joint yoke without threads has a milled plane. Screw in a bolt from this side. d. Confirm that the connector are connected correctly and the wiring harness fixing clips are fixed. e. Perform steering angle calibration. Refer to: Steering angle calibration f. Read the steering system data with VDS to confirm whether a DTC exists. If so, find out the cause and eliminate it. g. Perform software configuration word writing. Refer to: Software configuration h. Road test.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly.

0 Tip:

Refer to the front auxiliary frame assembly for removal and installation of the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly. Refer to: Front auxiliary frame assembly

2. Remove the steering gear outer tie rod.

0 Tip:

The removal methods of the left and right steering gear outer tie rods are the same.

![](images/a82ca733798ec5b10f938c8486a94ab96dc37012d0b220b6fbc3d39c1c8f2bc6.webp)

a. ① Draw assembly marks on the steering gear outer tie rod and the inner tie rod. b. Loosen the lock nut A and remove the steering gear outer tie rod ①.

### Check Procedure

1. Check the steering gear outer tie rod a. Fix the steering gear outer tie rod assembly onto a vise.

i Caution: Do not over-tighten the vise. b. Check whether the steering outer tie rod ball head gets stuck and loose. If so, replace the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly.

2. Check the no-load torque of the steering gear.

a. Check the no-load torque of the steering gear with a torque wrench to see if sticking or other abnormality exists.

### i Caution:

The steering gear tie rod should be adjusted to the straight driving position. 0 Tip: If the no-load torque of the steering gear has sticking or other abnormalities, replace the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly.

3. Check the dust covers of bellows

a. Turn the pinion shaft of the steering gear, and check whether the dust covers of left and right bellows expand and contract smoothly and whether they are cracked or damaged.

0 Tip:

If the dust covers of bellows are cracked or damaged, replace the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly.

### 4. Check the dust cover of steering gear outer tie rod ball joint.

a. Visually check whether the dust cover of the steering gear outer tie rod ball joint is cracked or damaged.

0 Tip: If so, replace the steering gear outer tie rod assembly.

5. Check the steering gear inner tie rod ball joint

a. Fix the steering gear, rotate the inner tie rod, and check whether there are abnormal phenomena such as jamming and looseness during rotation.

0 Tip: If so, replace the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the electric power steering gear with tie rod assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Fit the lock nut and the steering gear outer tie rod to the electric power steering gear until their assembly marks are aligned, and tighten the lock nut.
b. Replace the cotter pin of the steering gear outer tie rod ball joint.
c. After installation, check for wheel alignment, and adjust the wheel alignment to the standard range if necessary. Refer to: Four-wheel alignment
d. Perform steering angle calibration. Refer to: Steering angle calibration
e. Read the steering system data with VDS to confirm whether a DTC exists. If so, find out the cause and eliminate it.
f. Perform software configuration word writing. Refer to: Software configuration
g. Road test.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard
2. Remove the lower left shield assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left shield assembly of dashboard
3. Remove the electronic accelerator pedal assembly. Refer to: Electronic accelerator pedal assembly

4. Remove the universal joint assembly.

![](images/c695c05a7cd78b6b7400be1a3444f7e6860cd8e9637dda821d27d4a3dc8dce71.webp)

b. Confirm that the mounting bolt at the lower end of the universal joint assembly can be accurately fitted into the groove of the pinion shaft of the steering gear, so that the lower end of the universal joint is installed in place.

### 1 Caution:

The mounting bolt at the lower end of the universal joint assembly should be installed from the non-threaded side.
The side of the universal joint yoke without threads has a milled plane. Screw in a bolt from this side.

c. Centre the steering wheel assembly, install and tighten the fixing bolts for connecting the universal joint assembly and the steering column.

### 4.5.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. When repairing the front brake, wear a dust mask to prevent inhaling the dust on the brake pad into the lungs.

2. When repairing the brake system, prevent brake pads and brake discs from being contaminated by oil/fluid; otherwise, the braking effect may be affected.

3. Do not clean the brake assembly with compressed air or a brush, but use a vacuum cleaner or brake cleaner for cleaning the same.

4. Please use a flare nut wrench when removing and installing fluid pipes.

5. After disconnecting the brake fluid pipe, seal the fluid pipe port with a dust cover to prevent foreign matters from entering the hydraulic brake system.

6. Do not reuse any discharged brake fluid. Due to the strong water absorption of brake fluid, it should be placed in a sealed container when recycled.

7. Brake fluid is highly corrosive. If any brake fluid splashes on the skin, it should be immediately wiped off the skin with a rag and then the skin should be thoroughly washed with soap and water. Brake fluid is also highly corrosive to the paint on the vehicle body, so it is necessary to prevent the brake fluid from splashing on the painted surface of the vehicle body. In case of any splashing of brake fluid, the painted surface should be washed with water immediately.

8. When removing the front brake caliper, do not step on the brake pedal; otherwise, the piston will pop up and be damaged.

9. During the replacement of brake system components, those with the same part number or equivalent ones must be used, and no defective products or substitutes can be used for replacement.

10.During the installation of brake system components, the fixing bolts or nuts of each component should be tightened in strict accordance with the tightening torques given in this manual.

![](images/76e62cf11927a0abaf655da1afc308c4e29c10df7ca61c7b747ba9f6d2b0db41.webp)

a. Check whether the clearance of brake light switch meets the design requirements (1.5\~2.5 mm) and whether the brake pedal returns normally. b. Check whether the result is normal?

Adjust the clearance of brake light switch or check the condition of the brake pedal.

![](images/e0844a084eb78b98d20cc336b85876fa7bcdfd1752a0ea98805c7d3e915ef3c4.webp)

No

Look for other reasons that may cause abnormal wear and drag of brake pads.

Yes

![](images/b1d8cf7dbc5eaaf083c0a5d338aaf710e97ebac8007867cf1e82dc8e5e0ff49d.webp)

a. Is any wheel affected by brake drag? b. Check whether the result is normal?

No

replace the IPB system assembly.

a. Is any wheel affected by brake drag? b. Check whether the result is normal?

### Check the front brake disc

1. Check the runout of the front brake disc end face

a. Remove the front wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly b. Remove and move away the front brake caliper assembly.
c. The vehicle is in neutral gear.
d. Thoroughly clean the brake disc and remove all rust corrosion.
e. Check if the surface of the brake disc is subject to damage or cracks.
f. Install appropriate flat washers and wheel nuts and tighten them.

![](images/e1a669a2fda81ec3996ef789f7aee67acde22c8ec9a18879b89a4b875d87e58a.webp)

g. Install the measuring support of brake disc runout. Special tool: measuring support of brake disc runout

![](images/86708a35f4c3fcd316883f92a5214b500db3a95206e374a4c097e4935404dd80.webp)

h. Put the dial gauge as shown in the figure, and measure the runout at 10mm from the outer edge of the brake disc.

### 0 Tip:

If the runout of the brake disc exceeds the service limit of 0.08mm, adjust the brake disc with an optical disc drive.
If the thickness of brake disc is less than the adjustment limit, replace it.

Flatness of front brake disc: ＜0.08mm i. Install the front brake caliper assembly. j. l. Install the front wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

2. Check the thickness of the front brake disc a. Remove the front wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly b. Remove and move away the front brake caliper assembly.

![](images/28fb17416d06d4af9c695102bc284286c42ebde3c3cee4c6c1fd85cd0cd97520.webp)

c. Use a micrometer to measure the thickness of the brake disc at 8 points 10 mm from the outer edge of the brake disc and at the intervals of about 45°. If the minimum measured value is less than the adjustment limit, replace the brake disc. Allowable wear thickness of front brake disc: ≥32\~34mm (thickness after wear)

d. Install the front brake caliper assembly. e. l. Install the front wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

### Check the front brake pad

1. Check the thickness of the front brake pad a. Check whether the thickness of brake pad friction material meets the requirements (excluding the thickness of steel backing) with a brake pad thickness gauge.

![](images/74028f688729064447c950a019fc2b107375f9b9a4f4701d6112e099451149cb.webp)

### i Caution:

If the thickness of brake pad friction material is less than the service limit, replace the whole set of brake pad.

Allowable wear thickness of front brake pad: 2.75\~9.85mm (thickness after wear)

### Check the rear brake disc

1. Check the runout of the rear brake disc end face a. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly b. Remove and move away the rear integrated EPB caliper assembly. c. The vehicle is in neutral gear. d. Thoroughly clean the brake disc and remove all rust corrosion. e. Check if the surface of the brake disc is subject to damage or cracks. f. Install appropriate flat washers and wheel nuts and tighten them. g. Install the measuring support of brake disc runout. Special tool: measuring support of brake disc runout

![](images/42f395dbae2eb28a0541784204ca71e0d670ce99e47f88b323e0d316c72b0bf8.webp)

h. Put the dial gauge as shown in the figure, and measure the runout at 10mm from the outer edge of the brake disc.

### 0 Tip:

If the runout of the brake disc exceeds the service limit of 0.08mm, adjust the brake disc. If the thickness of brake disc is less than the adjustment limit, replace it.

Flatness of rear brake disc: ＜0.08mm

i. Install the rear integrated EPB caliper assembly. j. Install the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly 2. Check the thickness of the rear brake disc a. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly b. Remove and move away the rear integrated EPB caliper assembly.

![](images/00b2ac2fb304a70c0aecff88ff57f0e0b56cecde86e45d801a990f0cda70495b.webp)

c. Use a micrometer to measure the thickness of the brake disc at 8 points 10 mm from the outer edge of the brake disc and at the intervals of about 45°. If the minimum measured value is less than the adjustment limit, replace the brake disc. Allowable wear thickness of rear brake disc: 28\~30mm (thickness after wear)

d. Install the rear integrated EPB caliper assembly. e. Install the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly

### Check the rear brake pad

1. Check the thickness of the rear brake pad a. Check whether the thickness of brake pad friction material meets the requirements (excluding the thickness of steel backing) with a brake pad thickness gauge.

![](images/0d52a8725f2c42b662c2a1ae2646a49ac5d29eb2663e7373709ab381305f2655.webp)

### i Caution:

If the thickness of brake pad friction material is less than the service limit, replace the whole set of brake pad.

Allowable wear thickness of rear brake pad: 3\~11.1mm (thickness after wear)

### Reset front brake caliper piston

1. Reset front brake caliper piston

![](images/782e9bd948d77a5b6fecd2442e567c3cefe30583d1273e1c729191ef0de3c786.webp)

a. Install the brake caliper piston return tool to the brake pad position, and turn the bolt in the middle of tool to complete resetting.

### i Caution:

When installing the brake caliper piston return tool, avoid bumping against the brake caliper piston to prevent causing damage to it.

Special tool: brake caliper piston return tool

### 4.5.7.1 Front brake pad assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left brake pad assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right brake pad assembly, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front brake pad assembly

![](images/0f38e044e2dde859a77c607400a8339cbc62b753f5c071fc94ced4bff2a05439.webp)

a. Remove the 2 pins A and the leaf spring ①.

![](images/286d1ea9e9288afdf2ae2d106025cb9818961f76a45f17b0ecd5e66789b19066.webp)

b. Remove one fixing bolt and then remove the pin shaft.

Torque: 30±3 N•m

![](images/6e334f49480b53d3b498e435a22be0bb2f336e898109f5fd781fac8014f0f70e.webp)

c. Split the brake pad, reset the brake caliper piston, and take out the front brake pad assembly.

### 0 Tip:

In some vehicles, The bake pad and the brake caliper piston may stick together in some vehicles. In this case, remove the brake caliper and then remove the brake pad.

Special tool: brake caliper piston return tool

d. Thoroughly clean the brake caliper, remove all rust and check it for grooves and cracks, if any, replace it.
e. Check the brake disc for damage or cracks, and replace it if any.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front brake pad assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Before installing the brake pad, reset the brake caliper piston using a brake caliper piston return tool. Special tool: brake caliper piston return tool
b. Correctly install the front brake pad assembly. Install the brake pad with the wear alarm on the outer side.
c. Press the brake pedal for several times, confirm if the brake operates normally, and then conduct the trial run.

i Caution: • After a full set of brake pads is just installed, longer pedal travel may be required for braking. Press the brake pedal several times to restore the normal pedal travel. d. Upon installation, check if the interface or connecting mechanism between the front brake hose and pipeline leaks; refasten it if necessary.

### 4.5.7.2 Front brake disc

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left brake disc as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right brake disc, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front brake disc.

![](images/39820408f91b48d007b14a4579dcf054699e6ad04315c21dff06337af3437b58.webp)

a. Remove the 2 fixing bolts and take off the front brake caliper assembly.

i Caution: Fix the front brake caliper assembly and avoid excessive force on the front brake hose.

Torque: 195±5N•m

b. Remove the 2 fixing screws and remove the front brake disc.

### i Caution:

Use rust remover during removal if the front brake disc is rusty. Do not forcibly remove the brake disc from the hub; otherwise, the brake disc may be damaged.

Torque: 10±1N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front brake disc in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Before installing the brake disc, the disc surfaces on both sides should be polished evenly to ensure sufficient wear allowance.
b. Simultaneously replace the two brake discs on the same axle.
c. After replacement, the brake pedal needs to be pressed several times before the whole vehicle can be powered on; otherwise, the brake system may give an alarm.
d. Road test.

0 Tip:

Refer to the front hub unit assembly for removal and installation of the front brake mudguard. Refer to: Front hub unit assembly

### 4.5.7.4 Front brake caliper assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of front left brake caliper assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right brake caliper assembly, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front brake caliper assembly.

![](images/6fda453c40b35cc4d750d5452818137e0d049b46118f5ecbab5195427f902027.webp)

a. Remove one hollow bolt A and move away the front wheel brake hose ①.

0 Tip: Block the front wheel brake hose and brake caliper ports with plugs.

Torque: 35±3 N•m

b. Remove the 2 fixing bolts (B) and take off the front brake caliper assembly ②. Torque: 195±5N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front brake caliper assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Do not reuse the hollow bolt gasket of the front wheel brake hose, but replace it with a new one.
b. Before installing the front brake caliper, reset the brake caliper piston using a brake caliper piston return tool. Special tool: brake caliper piston return tool
c. Add the brake fluid and bleed the brake system. Refer to: Bleeding of brake system
d. After installation, press the brake pedal several times to confirm that the brake system works normally.
e. Road test.

### 4.5.7.5 Front wheel brake hose

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left wheel brake hose as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right wheel brake hose, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and enter the installation (factory) mode. Refer to: Enter
installation (factory) mode.
3. Drain the brake fluid. Refer to: Bleeding of brake system
4. Remove the front wheel brake hose.

![](images/667e12d25ea3137b58b6eef93d8ffb0b2b018265467c594d06bcf7a7873ef23d.webp)

a. Remove one hollow bolt. Torque: 35±3 N•m

![](images/4f9de2a31b8ffea56a6ee8d1d0b0d522bf1835d01b7bf676c3370d08bf1a00a3.webp)

b. Remove one fixing bolt A and E-clamp B, loosen the fluid pipe joint nut and remove the front wheel brake hose. Torque of bolt A: 25±2 N•m Torque of fluid pipe joint nut: 18±2 N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front wheel brake hose in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Before installation, clean the periphery of the port to prevent dirt from entering the brake system.
b. Do not reuse the hollow bolt gasket of the front wheel brake hose, but replace it with a new one.
c. After installation, press the brake pedal several times to confirm that the brake system works normally.
d. Add the brake fluid and bleed the brake system. Refer to: Bleeding of brake system e. Exit installation (factory) mode. Refer to: Exit installation (factory) mode.
f. Road test.

### 4.5.7.8 Rear brake pad assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the rear left brake pad assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the rear right brake pad assembly, please refer to the rear left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Perform the maintenance mode release procedure. Refer to: EPB maintenance mode release
3. Remove the rear brake pad assembly

![](images/c9aab6c20c05ba551cb0c6440531937a39f239ec7cd4e1936e7574ae54714f21.webp)

a. Disconnect connector A, remove one fixing bolt B, and turn the rear brake caliper upward.

### 0 Tip:

When removing the bolt, fix the floating pin with a wrench to prevent the floating pin from rotating with the bolt.

### i Caution:

Be careful when fixing the floating pin to avoid damaging the dust cover of floating pin.

Torque: 30±2 N•m

![](images/3eb156c4f7c6790cb9af8ac8412d48ce8f87bb3d4010e04e9684142856abc86b.webp)

b. Remove the rear brake pad assembly and the brake pad fixing reed.

c. Clean the brake caliper to remove all rust, and check the brake caliper for grooves and cracks. Check whether the brake disc for damage and cracks, and replace it if any.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear brake pad assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Correctly install the rear brake pad assembly. Install the brake pad with the wear alarm on the inner side.
b. During installation of the brake pad, ensure no excessive deformation of the return reed on the brake pad.
c. After installation, push the brake pad to check whether it returns well. If it does not return well, reassemble the brake pad or replace it with a new one until the brake pad returns well.

d. Use a piston resetting tool to reset the caliper piston, make sure that the piston sheath is not damaged or deformed, and slowly turn the caliper downward to prevent the piston or its sheath from bumping against the brake pad.

i Caution:

Pay attention to observing the fluid level in the brake fluid reservoir when resetting the piston, to prevent excessive liquid level which may result in overflow of the brake fluid.

![](images/428b36c53e867b94ae3fe6f5342b05f447a730907858a9462bb612806c097fe7.webp)

e. Make sure that the bump on the inner brake pad is just caught in the groove on the brake caliper piston.

f. After replacement, the brake pedal needs to be pressed several times before the whole vehicle can be powered on; otherwise, the brake system may give an alarm.

i Caution: After the brake pad is replaced, the brake pedal travel is relatively long. In this case, press the brake pedal several times back and forth to restore the normal pedal travel.

g. Perform EPB maintenance mode clamping operation, confirm that no EPB DTC exists, and then carry out a road test. Refer to: EPB maintenance mode clamping

### 4.5.7.9 Rear brake disc

0 Tip:

### 4.6.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Integrated EPB controller is a safety-related component. It is forbidden to reuse a repaired internal circuit of the integrated EPB controller.

2. The integrated EPB controller must be installed and maintained by technicians who have received professional training and mastered relevant maintenance skills, and must be replaced with the OEM's product corresponding to the vehicle model.
3. The integrated EPB controller must be installed horizontally, and its front and rear orientations cannot be exchanged. Make sure that the wiring harness of the integrated EPB controller is not interfered by other electrical appliances and wiring harnesses. Never refit the original wiring harness of the integrated EPB controller.
4. Be sure to set the power to the "OFF" position before repairing or replacing the integrated EPB controller.
5. Avoid accidental activation when EPB motor drive assembly is replaced. Therefore, make sure that the wiring harness connector is disconnected before removing the EPB motor drive assembly from the brake caliper body.
6. When the integrated EPB controller applies or releases parking brake, the rear brake caliper assembly will produce a sound of mechanical rotation.

### 4.6.3.2 System descriptions

1. The EPB system uses simple EPB switch operation in place of the conventional parking brake lever to achieve the parking function by using the integrated EPB controller to control the EPB motor. This system can also assist in driving safety.

2. The EPB system mainly consists of electronic parking switch, integrated EPB controller, EPB motor drive assembly, wiring harness and other components.

3. The EPB system has the following main functions:

Automatic parking: When the vehicle is powered off or the gear is in the P position, the system will automatically start parking.
• Manual parking: When the electronic parking switch is pulled up, the system will start parking. Automatic parking brake releasing upon pressing accelerator pedal: With the vehicle started in the D or R mode and the parking system activated, when the accelerator pedal is pressed gently, the parking system will be released depending on the road conditions.
Automatic parking brake releasing upon shifting the gear: With the vehicle started in the P or N mode and the EPB activated, when the brake pedal is pressed to shift to the R or D mode, the parking system will be released automatically.
Manual parking brake releasing: With the vehicle started and the gear shifted to a mode other than P mode, when the EPB switch is pressed, the system will cancel parking.
Emergency braking function: When the vehicle is running, in case of brake failure, one can use the EPB system to brake the vehicle.

### i Caution:

When the vehicle is running, do not operate the EPB except for emergency brake.
Do not drive the vehicle with the parking brake unreleased.

### 4.6.7.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New
Tang EV 2021 9 → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “EPB(SAC)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/1d4b26f1ef329b1dab11b7ab7a9d41fd6c4c8d3f442d25b38ce3b647f4980479.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

### 4.6.7.3 Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of the parking brake system without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” “New
Tang EV 2021 “New Tang EV 2021 General” “ECU module” “EPB(SAC)”

6. Read data flow.

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

Without disassembling any parts, use VDS to conduct action test on the suspected parts, and then judge whether the suspected parts function normally. Active test when troubleshooting can avoid unnecessary disassembly and improve diagnosis efficiency and accuracy.

### Check parking brake system

1. Check parking brake system

a. Pull up the EPB switch, so that the vehicle can park at 20% gradient. In case of vehicle slip, repair the EPB system. b. Check whether the EPB harness is worn and whether the connection is reliable.

2. Check the EPB motor drive assembly.

a. Connect the VDS to the OBD interface.
b. Power up the vehicle and wait until its self-test ends.
c. Read and record the DTC, and confirm whether the DTC represents a current fault or a historical fault.
d. Check each detected DTC according to the description in the DTC list from top to bottom. If the troubleshooting conclusion is that the EPB motor drive assembly is faulty, replace it.

### i Caution:

After maintenance release is activated by method 1 and method 2, all functions of EPB will be disabled, thus avoiding damage to EPB motor drive assembly caused by unexpected actions during maintenance. After the maintenance is completed and the vehicle status is restored, be sure to perform EPB maintenance mode clamping operations make the EPB system return to normal.

### EPB maintenance mode release (method I)

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. EPB maintenance mode release

a. Select "VDS2000 Vehicle Diagnosis System".

![](images/7e242209a678211a492573b0fc3370815655342d1c6a9f832e8d2c442d5127e8.webp)

T-4304A32

![](images/7fc0ccf7b66443569ffb1f5cab9172e886ac27f1d8bfca7ba42b68d4d271d4f2.webp)

b. Select Passenger car".

![](images/50f15fef07c2993182c24238ab27ebec1bb1ba7c33d207039e89ba531c61e34c.webp)

c. Select "EV series".

![](images/e6cf520b7c4ab229496bbb6d461f743e4cd642f039e70a4623a77c2cee6efb08.webp)

d. Select "New Tang EV 2021".

![](images/e01f06e94945bd8b332dec2ef2a8f7578aec23411caa102f156169968ce2a0e6.webp)

![](images/b8d4c4c5ab42f583828a235f6d5db3d0d5a772934bc9e7ed53f94e993564bdeb.webp)

![](images/f0d56a8091b9606044bf4f9b003d44eefd90af1f20dd7b6919893bce9edc1619.webp)

![](images/df1c0e59575cfa1bbb1d4c844d31b2dac2a9498f9e3c87287abab21f930871fa.webp)

![](images/c9941729c03c520cb066cd6408d193fb2e8920d05d330bfaea458f5337b84b1c.webp)

![](images/9812af672c784ddf39f4f47a731235d51bfb04149a87dc26e081cec15ff55299.webp)

### EPB maintenance mode release (method II)

1. EPB maintenance mode release

a. Make sure the vehicle is powered on ("OK").
b. Keep pressing the brake pedal.
0 Tip: After the brake pedal is pressed, the brake light will stay on;
i Caution: Keep pressing the brake pedal during the whole process;

c. Press and hold the EPB switch for above 10s, and the parking system fault warning light on the instrument will flash.

i Caution:

If the holding time is less than 10s or above 12s after the switch is pressed, the system will automatically return to the initial state so that operations need to be conducted again.
d. Release the EPB switch within 2s when the parking system fault warning light starts flashing.
e. Start timing after the EPB switch is released and press the EPB switch again within the subsequent 3 \~ 5 s;

### i Caution:

If the switch is pressed again within 3s or upon 5s after the switch is released for the first time, the system will automatically return to the initial state so that operations need to be conducted again;

f. Start the EPB to perform maintenance mode release, and the parking system fault warning light will stay on.

g. Release the brake pedal.

i Caution: After the system is completely released, it is necessary to perform EPB maintenance mode clamping to exit maintenance mode release.

### EPB maintenance mode release (method III)

1. EPB maintenance mode release

0 Tip:

If method 1 and method 2 fail due to electrical equipment failure, mechanical maintenance release can be carried out as follows:

a. Remove the EPB motor drive assembly. Refer to: EPB motor drive assembly

![](images/b062a58e6ccc2249e2d0bc95b05493690452b8179c496c27fc1d784f34825c59.webp)

b. Connect a torque wrench and a sleeve into the spline of the brake caliper.

c. Turn the spline on the brake caliper body clockwise to release the brake caliper piston.

0 Tip: Loosen the brake piston until the thrust screw of the brake caliper body can rotate freely.

### 4.6.8.3 EPB maintenance mode clamping

0 Tip:

After the EPB maintenance is released, the EPB maintenance clamp operation is required before the maintenance release state exits. After EPB maintenance mode clamping is performed, the EPB system returns to normal and can respond to all functions.

### i Caution:

Once the EPB motor drive assembly is removed from the vehicle, do not drive the vehicle by power-on.

### EPB maintenance mode clamping (method I)

![](images/8c134874b94276aa59bfea36c53fd838e70a97cdc6bcee15ca1cb6ea31ed0f38.webp)

i. Select "Maintenance mode clamped".

![](images/b9972eb6abab73f8c5f9158ee5301596c7c7d530ad3d629e5102847754da2859.webp)

j. Click Read".

![](images/7a5a6e98bfb203c8afb9f15c55a089ef640cff1ec0671d95111f8a7620cb42d2.webp)

k. Click the run button to perform maintenance mode clamping.

![](images/cdc1200093f385715a702d80ad4cdeb227171fefaaf881bbedbb3b24b0e76b1e.webp)

l. EPB maintenance mode clamping succeeded.

Use the EPB switch to perform EPB maintenance mode clamping as follows (method II)

1. Perform EPB maintenance mode clamping.

a. Make sure the vehicle is powered on ("OK").
b. Keep pressing the brake pedal.
0 Tip: After the brake pedal is pressed, the brake light will stay on;
i Caution: Keep pressing the brake pedal during the whole process;

c. Pull up and hold the EPB switch for above 10s, and the parking system fault warning light on the instrument will flash.

i Caution:

If the holding time is less than 10s after the switch is pressed, the system will automatically return to the initial state so that operations need to be conducted again.

d. Release the EPB switch and pull it up again within the subsequent 5s.

i Caution: If the switch is pulled up again 5s after it is released, the system will automatically return to the initial state so that operations need to be conducted again.

e. EPB performs clamping action, and the parking system fault warning light goes out and the EPB indicator lights up.

f. Release the brake pedal.

### 0 Tip:

After the maintenance release exits, the EPB system returns to normal and can respond to all functions.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the middle toolkit assembly of boot. Refer to: Middle toolkit assembly of boot
2. Remove the integrated EPB controller. a. Take out the boot sponge block.

![](images/76f386cb19248523c3cae41e568f534993b44d8ef794a6838fb8cfd4ddfc3c8a.webp)

b. Disconnect one connector A, remove 2 fixing bolts B to remove the integrated EPB controller. Torque: 9 N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the integrated EPB controller in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Ensure that connectors are installed in place.
b. After installation, check that the parking brake system can work normally.

### 4.6.9.2 EPB motor drive assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the rear left EPB motor drive assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the rear right EPB motor drive assembly, please refer to the rear left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Perform the EPB maintenance mode release procedure. Refer to: EPB maintenance mode release
3. Remove the EPB motor drive assembly.

![](images/1d8a512353ca5fee2fbc6c114dc89ccc9cf446979bec32cd46cc5bdc81f503d2.webp)

a. Disconnect one connector A, remove two fixing bolts B, and stably remove the EPB motor drive assembly from the brake caliper body in the axial direction.

Torque: 8±2 N•m

![](images/66fd0994b90829f8a1c2b92d63295fa9e4e68e80144528a8848006017063d604.webp)

b. Remove the O-ring from the O-ring groove of brake caliper body using a tool with soft tip.

### i Caution:

Do not damage the O-ring groove of the brake caliper body during disassembly. Scratches will lead to leakage, damage to the transmission assembly and even complete parking failure.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the EPB motor drive assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

![](images/4700cbfe4d03a71ec85e40a1f4fcb4ba58bac864f422c67adc828ec3e388f762.webp)

a. Install a new O-ring on the O-ring groove of brake caliper body.

### i Caution:

The new O-ring must be free of dust and contamination. After installation, check the O-ring for twist and tear.

b. Clean the threads in the threaded holes of the brake caliper body and remove the threadlocker on the threads. c. Stably push the EPB motor drive assembly onto the brake caliper body in the axial direction.

### i Caution:

The EPB motor drive assembly must be pushed to be completely attached to the mating surface of the brake caliper body, and the fixing hole of the EPB motor drive assembly must be aligned with and attached to the corresponding screw hole of the brake caliper body.

d. When tightening bolts, do not bring any torque, shear force and tension between the EPB motor drive assembly and the brake caliper body.

i Caution:

Threadlocker is applied to bolt threads and it can only ensure locking at the time of its first application. Do not use any used bolts; otherwise, looseness of bolts will occur.

e. Perform EPB maintenance mode clamping and confirm that no EPB DTC exists. Refer to: EPB maintenance mode clamping

f. Road test.

### 4.7.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Before diagnosing the IPB system, first remove identified faults (if any) of the basic brake system, such as noise generated by the brake system, soft feel of brake pedal, brake pedal vibration during normal braking, vehicle running to one side during brake, and parking brake system fault.

2. The IPB system assembly can only be replaced as a whole and cannot be disassembled for inspection or partially replaced/interchanged.

3. Brake fluid is corrosive. Be careful not to contaminate other parts of the vehicle with brake fluid.

4. Brake fluid is corrosive. Do not contaminate the skin with brake fluid. If contaminated, wash the skin immediately with plenty of clean water.

5. After removal of brake pipe joint nuts, seal the pipe, IPB system assembly and other ports with plugs to avoid the ingress of foreign matters.

6. Due to easy displacement of fluid pipe joint nut, screw 3\~5 threads of the nut into the screw hole by hand before tightening the nut with a flare nut wrench.

7. The IP system must be repaired by technicians who have undergone professional trainings and mastered repair skills and only parts and components from the manufacturer are allowed to be used for replacement.

8. After repair of the IPB system, be sure to carry out a strict inspection and a road test on it for checking its normal function before handing it over to the customer.

9. Be sure to replace the corresponding brake pipe clamp when replacing the brake pipe.

### 1. System Overview

a. IPB stands for "Integrated Parking Brake" and IPB system is an electronically controlled brake system. Compared with a conventional vacuum booster pump brake system, this system responds more quickly and controls more accurately. This system significantly enhances the efficiency of regenerative braking energy recovery. In addition, IPB integrates the ESP system. Compared with a non-integrated brake system, IPB system is lighter in weight and occupies less space in the vehicle.
b. IPB system mainly consists of IPB system assembly, yaw rate sensor, wheel speed sensor assembly, instrument cluster, brake pedal assembly and brake pipe.

### 4.7.7.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “electro-hydraulic brake(Bosch)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

![](images/1b101827ab0becf18cb21930732079dabd515da6c0329cf0315e1ca5f2db7e0b.webp)

### 4.7.7.3 Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of the IPB system without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “electro-hydraulic brake(Bosch)”

6. Read data flow.

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

### 4.7.8.1 Adjustment of brake light switch clearance

Adjustment of brake light switch clearance

1. Adjustment of brake light switch clearance

a. Remove the lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard
b. Disconnect the brake light switch connector.
c. Turn the brake light switch ① counterclockwise to remove it.
d. Place a flat plate with a thickness of 1.5 mm on the brake light switch stop pad ③.
e. Insert the brake light switch into its mounting bracket ② to completely compress the switch contact, clockwise turn and tighten the switch, and pull out the flat plate.
f. After installation, press and release the brake pedal several times. Wait until the brake pedal returns naturally, check whether the clearance of the brake light switch (namely, the exposed length of brake light switch contact) is 1.5\~2.5 mm. If not, readjust the clearance.

![](images/a62b42181279b06ff58ddbcdafb7fd24959f822b4ecaa87f7942e958398480a5.webp)

g. Install the lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard

### 1. Check brake fluid level

a. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly b. Check that the brake fluid level should be between "MAX" mark and "MIN” mark. If the level is below the "MIN” mark or above the "MAX” mark, fill or pump out the brake fluid.

![](images/f2de5087bf4422fa3a87c973efd4cd3e2f88133fbe274c197aa6a6a75c438915.webp)

### Description of bleeding of brake system

1. Bosch IPB system assembly is adopted for this vehicle. When the brake system is subject to repair or maintenance, if air is mixed in the brake hydraulic circuit, bleeding must be carried out as per the operation requirements specified in this section; otherwise, insufficient bleeding, IPB degradation without assistance or brake system alarm may occur, affecting the brake safety.

### i Caution:

The brake fluid discharged cannot be used anymore.
Be sure to use the pure “HZY6” or “BASF Hydraulan 404” brake fluid. Use of brake fluid other that those specified may cause corrosion, and reduce the service life of the brake system.
Do not splatter brake fluid on the vehicle; otherwise, the paint coating may be damaged. If brake fluid has been splattered on the paint coating, remove it with water immediately. The brake fluid pressurising equipment and the diagnostics device are needed for bleeding. Before bleeding, make sure that the brake fluid for the pressurising equipment is sufficient, the injection pressure is set to be 2bar (0.2MPa) and the filling cover are tightened; otherwise, the brake fluid will be ejected.
After bleeding, make up the brake fluid or remove excess brake fluid as required, so as to ensure that the maximum fluid level is at the MAX mark of the brake fluid reservoir.

2. Dry-type bleeding and wet-type bleeding may be adopted for this vehicle.

### 1. Scope of application of wet-type bleeding

a. When brake bleeding is required for replacing or removing installing brake caliper, brake hose or brake pipe.

i Caution: Dry-type bleeding is required when the IPB system assembly is replaced.

2. Precautions for wet-type bleeding:

a. Set the IPB system to "Installation mode" with a VDS, and then carry out replacement. If this step is not performed before replacing or removing installing the brake caliper, brake hose or hard pipe, dry-type bleeding must be required.
b. After successful bleeding, the vehicle dashboard shall have no ABS, ESP or brake system alarm, and the process of pressing brake pedal shall be normal without any abnormal sound.
c. The filling pressure of the brake fluid filling device is 2 bar. Do not increase the pressure; otherwise the brake fluid reservoir may be damaged!

### 4. Operation steps for wet-type bleeding

a. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and enter the installation (factory) mode. Refer to: Enter installation (factory) mode.
b. Power off the vehicle.
c. Replace or remove/install the brake caliper, brake hose or brake pipe.
d. Connect one end of a clean and transparent exhaust hose to the bleed screw, and put the other end into the waste liquid collection bottle.
e. Connect the brake fluid pressurizing equipment, and make sure that the equipment and the brake fluid reservoir opening are well sealed and firmly fixed without leakage.
f. Turn on the brake fluid pressurizing equipment, increase the pressure to 2 bar, loosen the brake bleed screw, and press the brake pedal normally once every 2s until there is no bubble

in the brake fluid from the bleed hose, indicating that no air is in the brake line. press the brake pedal and tighten the bleed screw.

i Caution: Bleeding is only required for the removed hydraulic circuit.

g. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and exit the "Installation (factory) mode". Refer to: Exit installation (factory) mode.

h. Clear the DTC.

i. Make sure that the vehicle dashboard has no ABS, ESP or brake system alarm, and the process of pressing brake pedal is normal without any abnormal sound, which means that the bleeding is successful, otherwise, re-operate it with a dry-type bleeding method
j. Turn off the brake fluid pressurizing equipment, and disconnect it after the pressure drops to 0.
k. Remove the excess brake fluid in the reservoir to ensure that the maximum fluid level is at the “MAX” mark.

### Dry-type bleeding

0 Tip:

VDS operation interface of dry-type bleeding. Refer to: VDS operation interface of dry-type bleeding

1. Application scope of dry-type bleeding

a. When the brake fluid is replaced;
b. replace the IPB system assembly.
c. When the brake caliper, brake hose and brake pipe are replaced directly without entering the "Installation mode" of the IPB system;
d. When wet-type bleeding fails.

2. Precautions for dry-type bleeding:

a. The filling pressure of the brake fluid filling device is 2 bar. Do not increase the pressure; otherwise the brake fluid reservoir may be damaged!
b. Bleeding must be carried out as per the specified sequence; otherwise, bleeding is required again.
c. During bleeding, do not exit the VDS bleeding operation interface; otherwise, bleeding is required again.

i Caution: VDS battery must be kept sufficient during bleeding.

d. During bleeding calibration, the pedal surface will push against the foot. In this case, the driver can stabilize the pedal, and it is forbidden to press the pedal firmly. e. When the bleeding calibration is terminated by ECU, please restart this round of bleeding; in case of failure for multiple times, please wait for 2 min in the failure interface and then restart this round of bleeding. f. When a single brake caliper has two bleed holes (bleed screws), bleeding is required for both holes separately. Please conduct bleeding twice for such brake caliper. g. After successful bleeding, the vehicle dashboard shall have no ABS, ESP or brake system alarm, and the process of pressing brake pedal shall be normal without any abnormal sound.

### 4. Operation steps for dry-type bleeding

a. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and enter the installation (factory) mode. Refer to: Enter installation (factory) mode.
b. Power off the vehicle.
c. Carry out brake fluid maintenance, or replacement or removal/installation of IPB system assembly.
d. Connect one end of a clean and transparent exhaust hose to the bleed screw, and put the other end into the waste liquid collection bottle.
e. Connect the brake fluid pressurizing equipment, and make sure that the equipment and the brake fluid reservoir opening are well sealed and firmly fixed without leakage.
f. Turn on the brake fluid pressurizing equipment and increase the pressure to 2bar.
g. Power up the vehicle, connect the VDS, and perform "Stage Ⅰ: air exhaust of rear left wheel". Refer to: VDS operation interface of dry-type bleeding Next, loosen the brake bleed screw and press the brake pedal normally once every 2s until the calibration is completed. After this operation, no bubbles should be contained in the brake fluid from the exhaust hose, indicating that the air has been exhausted completely. After bleeding, press the brake pedal and tighten the bleed screw.

### 0 Tip:

During the process, the pedal surface will push against the foot. In this case, the driver can stabilize the pedal, and it is forbidden to press the pedal firmly.

### i Caution:

If some bubbles are still contained in the brake fluid from the exhaust hose, conduct such operations again until there are no bubbles

![](images/32c15a9f3401c551bd3d07ca312d8f329de779cda6a61ecc7c72b5bc8feefa9e.webp)

h. In accordance with the order shown in the figure, orderly conduct the above mentioned operation for each wheel until the brake fluid discharged from the exhaust hose is free of air bubbles.

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> Bleeding must be carried out as per the specified sequence; otherwise, bleeding is required again.
>
> i. After the wheel bleeding is completed, turn off the pressurizing equipment, and disconnect it after the pressure drops to 0.
>
> j. Perform "Stage 5: IPB Housing exhaust" until the calibration is completed. It is unnecessary to press the brake pedal during this operation.

### i Caution:

Do not cover the brake fluid reservoir in this process; otherwise, the brake fluid reservoir may be damaged.

k. Perform "Stage 6: PFS and TMC2 exhaust". Press the brake pedal normally once every 3s until the calibration is completed. l. Exit installation (factory) mode. Refer to: Exit installation (factory) mode. m. Clear the DTC. Make sure that the vehicle dashboard has no ABS, ESP or brake system alarm, and the process of pressing brake pedal is normal without any abnormal sound, which means that the bleeding is successful, otherwise, re-operate it with a dry-type bleeding method

n. Remove the excess brake fluid in the reservoir to ensure that the maximum fluid level is at the “MAX” mark.

### Instructions for model configuration writing

1. After replacing the IPB assembly, write the model configuration and calibrate (VPC) valve body (if the calibration fails, wait for 10 minutes before recalibration), and then calibrate the IPB internal sensor. After successful calibration, clear the IPB DTC and power up and off the vehicle again to check whether any brake system alarm is displayed on the instrument.

### Notes for writing model configuration

1. Before writing the model configuration, the brake system is faulty, so please do not drive the vehicle;

2. Pay attention to writing the model configuration according to the actual model and configuration.

### Instructions for VPC valve body calibration

1. After successful calibration, clear the IPB DTC and power up and off the vehicle again to check whether any brake system alarm is displayed on the instrument.

### Instructions for internal sensor calibration

0 Tip: Internal sensor calibration means yaw rate sensor calibration.

1. After replacing the IPB assembly, write the model configuration and calibrate (VPC) valve body (if the calibration fails, wait for 10 minutes before recalibration), and then calibrate the IPB internal sensor. After successful calibration, clear the IPB DTC and power up and off the vehicle again to check whether any brake system alarm is displayed on the instrument.

### Precautions for internal sensor calibration

1. The vehicle is supported by its wheels.
2. Only the driver is sitting in the vehicle.
3. Turn the steering wheel to the front position where the front wheels should be in a straight
state.
4. Both the load and the tyre pressure are normal.
5. Interference such as closing doors or the bonnet is not allowed.
6. The calibration may be implemented on the rotating hub tester, or on flat road surfaces.

![](images/9bf51224bfa428e2b4c0137cceb3f57d80384b13d74c33d7dcbe2e83d0096191.webp)

### 1. Check brake line

a. Check brake hoses for damage, aging, leakage, mutual interference or distortion. If any, replace them.
b. Check brake pipes for damage, corrosion or leakage. If any, replace them.
c. Check brake pipes for obvious deformation. If any, replace them.
d. Check if the joints and connections between the brake hoses and brake pipes leak, and refasten them if necessary.
e. Check the IPB system assembly for damage and check each joint for leakage. If any, repair or replace the relevant parts.

### 4.7.9.1 Brake pedal assembly

a. Disconnect one connector and rotate counterclockwise the brake light switch ① to take it out.

![](images/d698b7c92c2264761140e19cdf40ee28f1c114e53881d87ee932bd33fd01c419.webp)

b. Remove one fixing bolt. Torque: 30±3 N•m

![](images/95bad690a74c341d42e07eb651d62523bbb80de997d2a8597b2343d31e0bd49c.webp)

c. Remove the 4 fixing nuts and disconnect all wiring harness fixing clips. Torque: 25±2 N•m

![](images/0c6fe255d3ba3a5dd17db171922e865fbc10c19c69f4f8f4064254cf5cc287df.webp)

d. Spread the brake pedal ball socket with a special tool and remove the brake pedal assembly. Special tool: brake pedal ball socket spreader tool

### Installation procedures

1. Install the brake pedal assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Adjust the brake light switch clearance. Refer to: Adjustment of brake light switch clearance Brake light switch clearance: 1.5-2.5 mm

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard
2. Remove the brake light switch. Refer to: Brake light switch
3. Remove the brake light switch stop pad.

a. Remove the brake light switch stop pad.

![](images/f28fb2d5e34342a68b438e848728f8bef098ebdd55b35e27e8849cb5624bce9c.webp)

### Installation procedures

1. Install the brake light switch stop pad in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Adjust the brake light switch clearance. Refer to: Adjustment of brake light switch clearance Brake light switch clearance: 1.5-2.5 mm

### Removal procedures

1. Power up the vehicle

2. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and enter the installation (factory) mode. Refer to: Enter the installation (factory) mode

3. Power off the vehicle

4. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly

5. Remove the front compartment right trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly

6. Remove the brake light switch. Refer to: Brake light switch

7. Drain the brake fluid.

8. Remove the IPB system assembly

![](images/eb3cecc8ae69b7b3d70768354ccdb383d1f06a5f9715bd581ecc0fc101d78760.webp)

a. Disconnect the connector A. b. Remove the elastic clamp B and pull out the connecting fluid pipe.

i Caution: Plug the fluid pipe and brake fluid reservoir ports with dust plugs.

c. Disconnect the connector B.

![](images/12dc512030f003e00975ba4058a7ab3d4524b9f27517e4fa3766403399e92da7.webp)

d. Remove the 4 fluid pipe joint nuts and move away the brake pipe.

i Caution:

Block the brake pipe and IPB system assembly ports with plugs.

Torque of M10 pipe joint nut: 18±2 N•m Torque of M12 pipe joint nut: 20±2 N•m

![](images/f5c6f7605e4045e4fe73e9d67a198cef06518360ac967c11c9928bd82e2ddd6f.webp)

e. Remove the 4 fixing nuts. Torque: 25±2 N•m

![](images/e60669a2cdf1cfb5fbab6806546ab5a633aa9b4c3f72c4e40ad8628a96d4cc40.webp)

f. Spread the brake pedal ball socket with a tool, and take out the IPB system assembly from the front compartment.

### i Caution:

Prevent the IPB system assembly from falling off the front compartment.
Prevent the bracket of the brake pedal assembly from deforming.
Avoid causing damage to or deformation of the brake pipe.

### Installation procedures

1. Take and move the IPB system assembly in the correct way.

![](images/4ff8af0b4a0d388c025ed2766c34ac546abe0154a7337cdcdd76214b988dbe89.webp)

a. Handle it by holding both motor and auxiliary area

![](images/7c3f8d57fd9cc2a4a2ea3eec33d4e1af7c9ac169666b31e84644c2200dd2b343.webp)

b. Handle it by holding both mounting plate and auxiliary area

c. Hold the auxiliary area with one hand, and touch the green area shown in the figure only with the other hand.

i Caution:

The green area can be held with hand, but the red area cannot.

2. Install the IPB system assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Ensure that the IPB system assembly will not be impacted during installation, and that the mounting gasket of the IPB system assembly and the body mounting surface are clean and free of foreign matters.
b. Gently press the brake pedal surface to push the thrust rod ball joint of the IPB system assembly into the brake pedal ball socket. Avoid pushing the thrust rod of the IPB system assembly from the side during connection.

### i Caution:

Do not pull the brake pedal upward after the thrust rod of the IPB system assembly is connected with the brake pedal, to avoid damaging the internal structural parts of the IPB system assembly. c. Remove sealing plugs of the fluid outlet of the IPB system assembly and the brake pipe using a suitable tool to avoid damaging the threads and sealing areas. d. Be careful not to install the brake pipe incorrectly; otherwise, it will lead to brake failure. e. Adjust the brake light switch clearance. Refer to: Adjustment of brake light switch clearance Brake light switch clearance: 1.5-2.5 mm f. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and exit the "Installation (factory) mode". Refer to: Exit installation (factory) mode. g. Bleeding of brake system. Refer to: Bleeding of brake system h. Execute "Model Configuration Writing". Refer to: Model configuration writing i. Perform BPC valve body calibration. Refer to: VPC valve body calibration j. Perform internal sensor calibration. Refer to: Internal sensor calibration

k. Power up the vehicle again, and check that all brake system warning lights should go out. l. Clear DTC of IPB system
m. Road test.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and enter the installation (factory) mode. Refer to: Enter
the installation (factory) mode
3. Pump out the brake fluid from the brake fluid reservoir assembly.
4. Remove the brake fluid reservoir assembly.

![](images/5895fa2fd95e37bbecd18966050c886869dc619977f8cca47f16936aadfa206f.webp)

a. Remove the 2 fixing bolts. Torque: 10±0.1 N•m

![](images/6968931ba0ce58663deec49e7a73e0003b1af0fde9b1b608b019e378e6ad8256.webp)

b. Remove the elastic clamp, pull out the brake fluid reservoir connecting hose assembly, and remove the brake fluid reservoir assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the brake fluid reservoir assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Add brake fluid.
b. Perform wet-type bleeding of the brake system. Refer to: Bleeding of brake system
c. Connect VDS, power up the vehicle and exit the "Installation (factory) mode". Refer to: Exit installation (factory) mode.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Remove the rear trimming panel assembly of auxiliary dashboard. Refer to: Rear trimming panel assembly of auxiliary dashboard
4. Remove the gearshift control mechanism cover assembly. Refer to: Gearshift control mechanism cover assembly
5. Remove the gearshift control mechanism assembly. Refer to: Gearshift control mechanism assembly
6. Remove the auxiliary dashboard body assembly. Refer to: Auxiliary dashboard body assembly
7. Remove the yaw rate sensor.

![](images/a0aef88ea2bf1a0c2663a995333ebf5053c9b9ee4cc38f71a29449445c1ef79a.webp)

a. Remove the four fixing nuts A and one snap fastener B, disengage the wiring harness fixing clip, and remove the rear mounting bracket assembly ① of auxiliary dashboard. Torque: 10 N•m

![](images/accadb961d5b7ed63affc40a1582f0bd17441482ed213b177ff70475f5475a6e.webp)

b. Remove one fixing nut A, and take off the rearrow face level air duct assembly Ⅲ ①. Torque: 6 N•m.

![](images/aedb3c47d6a2ef9694b78234631ed76058c5bd19f5e6f51341ef9775735812ff.webp)

Remove the 4 fixing nuts A, disengage the wiring harness fixing clip, and remove the gearshift control mechanism mounting bracket assembly

Torque: 23 N•m

![](images/af0c7115bea294ceccf67aa20e89b311e855857dcd228f0fccb38afdc4f9d675.webp)

d. Remove the wiring harness fixing clip on the stud, remove the 2 fixing nuts A, and remove the rearrow face level air duct assembly I ①. Torque: 6 N•m.

![](images/bb1486dd73d25ea6ae50c407bfe8a2fd603f08df9674bd175069903e06b6e20b.webp)

e. Disconnect connector A, remove the 2 fixing bolts B, and remove the yaw rate sensor ①. Torque: 10 N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the yaw rate sensor in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Make the arrow on the yaw rate sensor face the front of the vehicle. b. Perform internal sensor calibration. Refer to: Internal sensor calibration

### 4.7.9.6 Front wheel speed sensor assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left wheel speed sensor assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right wheel speed sensor assembly, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the front left wheel mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front wheel mudguard assembly
3. Remove the front wheel speed sensor assembly.

![](images/1aec220d6cf963817af3382fd908348f1383c3b1f6c374120f030b6d3e77f42d.webp)

a. Remove one fixing bolt and pull out the front wheel speed sensor assembly. Torque: 10 N•m

![](images/e69646a35841fce04bdef0a696244efa74d50231cff55527b831f72c7bdd38e1.webp)

b. Disengage the 4 fixing clips of the front wheel speed sensor assembly.

c. Disconnect one connector A, remove all fixing clips of the front wheel speed sensor, and remove the front wheel speed sensor assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front wheel speed sensor assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following: a. After installation, check that the front wheel speed sensor assembly should work normally.

### 4.7.9.7 Rear wheel speed sensor assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the rear left wheel speed sensor assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the rear right wheel speed sensor assembly, please refer to the rear left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the rear wheel speed sensor assembly.

![](images/94ccdd4f23f190db0e77ce8f079ebd60ee500d1e6498332914b3a9d356a1e712.webp)

a. Disconnect one connector A and remove the two wiring harness fixing clips B.

![](images/aabe28e82c66d58535f688a49ddefed5a17dafda7d1cdad45349503b17be0482.webp)

b. Disconnect one connector A and remove one fixing nut B. Torque: 10 N•m

![](images/415c0802a32fead7a34a16b7048abaafef3694b851c846e23d5daae76ba69d69.webp)

c. Remove one fixing bolt A. Torque: 10 N•m
d. Remove one fixing bolt B and pull out the rear wheel speed sensor assembly. Torque: 10 N•m

![](images/c1d6ff1a9393211129649bc2403973b68c92ac47387796c2abe2a2579d6b3faa.webp)

e. Remove one fixing nut and remove the rear wheel speed sensor assembly.

Torque: 10 N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear wheel speed sensor assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following: a. After installation, check that the rear wheel speed sensor assembly should work normally.

### 5.1.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Be careful not to scratch the light cover surface when removing a light assembly.

2. Set the power to "OK" when detecting the voltage in a circuit. 3. Do not make the positive and negative probes of the tester get too close when using the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) during inspection; otherwise, a short circuit will be caused. 4. Check that all light assemblies can work properly after their installation.

### 5.1.3.2 System descriptions

1. Lighting system provides light for vehicles driving at night. External lights mainly include headlights, reverse lights, license plate lights, fog lights, etc. Internal lights mainly include interior lights, door lights, various switch backlights, etc. Each light is installed in its required position and provided with respective control switch, circuit and fuse, thereby forming the lighting system.

2. Lighting system is also capable of signaling. It generates optical signal to warn drivers of other vehicles and passengers to draw their attention and ensure driving safety. Such signals include turn signal, brake signal, hazard warning signal, contour signal, reversing signal, etc.

3. In addition to traditional lighting features, this vehicle also has automatic lighting and headlight delayed turn-off features so that the light usage is more convenient and user friendly.

4. Automatic low beam: when the light switch set is turned to AUTO position, it will automatically control the clearance lights or low beam to turn on and off based on the outside light intensity sensed by the four-in-one sensor.

5. Headlight delayed turn-off: with the headlights on, when the vehicle is powered OFF from ON mode, the headlights will not turn off immediately; instead, the light switch set will count down to allow the headlights to remain on for 10s (the specific duration can be set by customers) before turning off the headlights.

### 5.1.7.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New
Tang EV 2021 ” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Saloon light(BYD)”
6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/a5cf8257608ac1d3bf7f5a4ab46fe42bcc8824c31981d983884fb84fc20cb7b6.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

7. Refer to "Saloon light (BYD)" for reading and clearing the DTCs of front left combination light (BYD) and front right combination light (BYD).

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of light without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New
Tang EV 2021 ” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Saloon light(BYD)”
