### 5.1.8.1 Light adjustment of headlights

1. Preparation of test screen a. The test screen is 1.2 m (height) × 2 m (width). A longitudinal centreline of the vehicle and a test paper position box are drawn on the screen, as shown in the figure:

![](images/e2aef0e20a0978a5c31eb2f7d9fcdc4e67ff0f8c4e42cfb3b0aafa994bfcd4fb.webp)

![](images/5117f1a143724f7e2a9012a20efee7472ff487437c9624d7b8b1002d878893b5.webp)

b. The requirements for drawing dimensions of the centreline and the test paper position box are as follows:

### 2. Preparation of test paper

a. Print the test drawings on A2 (420 mm × 594 mm) printing papers.
b. Cut the printed test papers along the dotted line and plastic package them;
c. During printing, make sure that the test drawings are printed in a 1:1 scale, with the dotted line box of left and right headlights being 400 mm × 350 mm. Please measure whether the dimensions are correct after printing;
d. Paste the test paper in the corresponding position box in the test screen when in use, and put it in a folder or file bag when not in use, and put it in the spare parts warehouse for proper preservation;

### 3. Preparation of test site

a. Make sure that the test site is flat and spacious and avoid the influence of strong light irradiation on light adjustment;

![](images/cb6cdab71bbb1c92d77016566775b4bd2b48a83c4bb6069479e554890dfb32b0.webp)

b. Draw a straight line parallel to the test screen on the ground 3m away from the test screen, and draw the vehicle centreline on the ground, and make sure that the centreline is perpendicular to the 3m line and the test screen, as shown in the figure below:

### 4. Preparation of test vehicle

a. Check and make sure that there is no damage or deformation around the vehicle and headlights;
b. Make sure that the vehicle lubricating oil level and the coolant level are at the levels required by design;
c. Make sure that the tyre pressure of the vehicle meets the standard inflation pressure;
d. Never place other articles in the vehicle, but be sure to place the tools delivered with the vehicle at the specified positions;
e. Have a person with a weight of 75 kg seated in the driver seat (in case of underweight, the counterweight method can be used to reach the standard weight of 75 kg);
f. Place the vehicle on a horizontal plane and shake the vehicle body from side to side to make the chassis suspension of the vehicle stay in a stable state.
g. Set the headlight adjustment switch to "0" before making adjustment.

5. Test steps

a. Paste the test paper of the corresponding vehicle model in the position box. b. Park the vehicle in front of the 3m line, that is, the low beam reference centre (the intersection point between the low beam bulb axis and the light cover) is 3m away from the test screen. In addition, keep the actual vehicle centreline overlap with the vehicle centreline drawn on the ground and be vertically aligned with the centreline on the test screen. c. Start the vehicle and turn on the headlights. d. Check whether the light pattern centre of the headlights is in the corresponding test box. If so, the headlights are normal. If not, the headlights need to be adjusted.

### 6. Precautions

a. The lower inflection point of the cut-off line is taken as the light pattern centre of low beams, while the brightest spot is taken as the light pattern centre of high beams;
b. Since headlight covers are made of plastic, if it is necessary to shield low beams when making adjustment for high beams; however, the headlight surfaces cannot be directly shielded or the shielding time cannot exceed 2 minutes, so as to avoid the gathering of heat that may cause burn-out of headlight covers.
c. When making light adjustment, observe the beam position while rotating the adjusting screw, and try to make proper adjustment at one time as far as possible. Do not use an electric screwdriver to rotate the adjusting screw continuously for a long time; otherwise, excessive adjustment will occur and adjustment in the opposite direction is needed.
d. adjust the light inflection to the centre of the test box.

Try to point

### 5.1.9.1 Front combination light assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the front left combination light assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the front right combination light assembly, please refer to the front left one.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left/right compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
2. Remove the grille upper cover assembly. Refer to: Grille upper cover assembly
3. Remove the front left/right wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly
4. Remove the front bumper assembly. Refer to: Front bumper assembly
5. Remove the front left combination light assembly

![](images/531f51abd79e34d5fddb4fc2ab474e7c71d7db97e60e43fda1eba139c136ed16.webp)

a. Turn over the dust cover of the connector and disconnect the connector of the front combination light assembly.

![](images/3af0917914ac496a530f8750e6ce23e9c3bf4ca448073d00157ef8aeff6f2607.webp)

b. Remove the 5 fixing bolts and remove the front combination light assembly. Torque: 4N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front left combination light assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.

b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that all lights of the front combination light assembly can go on and go out properly by operating the light switch.

### 5.1.9.2 Rear combination light assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the rear left combination light assembly as an example. For the removal and installation of the rear right combination light assembly, please refer to the left side.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear left combination light assembly

![](images/75e2df03da2a77c888b37f8d2db136f1fa5325d4d6b0168d381a9bd5642c7ac4.webp)

a. Pry out one metal clip and one plastic clip, and remove the bolted cover of the rear combination light.

![](images/f4ec3d94f558f23acf9f4f31cd1ff2e37cf26d1596e2e17c762c73938fe7b39f.webp)

b. Remove the 2 fixing bolts and push out the rear combination light assembly backward. Torque: 4N•m

![](images/f1622a8a2745a25891fda721f1c0e672205b2516cfb933cfd5e58dc6405fb3a1.webp)

c. Disconnect the connector and remove the rear left combination light assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear left combination light assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. Ensure that the rear left combination light is fitted into the mounting position and then install the fixing bolt.
c. Replace damaged clips.
d. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the rear combination light assembly can work properly.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the upper shield assembly of boot lid. Refer to: Upper shield assembly of boot lid
2. Remove the lower shield assembly of boot lid. Refer to: Lower shield assembly of boot lid
3. Remove the middle taillight.

![](images/1221e992954366a521c32c957427bebf95269fe865915387ad0e02abe2831fd5.webp)

a. Disconnect the connectors A on both sides.
b. Remove the 4 fixing nuts B and the 2 fixing nuts C Torque: 4N•m

![](images/79574166475462c7991ead8a35e6f3934493cf91236cc299f1751229ecbb9c6b.webp)

### 5.2.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. In case of accidental blockage of the wiper during use, the power supply should be cut off in time to prevent the wiper motor from burning out. In this case, it is not enough to turn off the wiper switch only. The right way is to disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and then disconnect the wiper motor connector.

2. During use, the wiper blade should be closely attached to the front windscreen assembly without clearance; otherwise, the wiper blade will not show the effect of cleaning.

3. Dry wiping is prohibited during use to prevent the wiper blade from being damaged. If the wiper switch is accidentally turned on, it should be turned off in time.

4. Attention should be paid to the cleaning and maintenance of the front windscreen assembly and wiper blade to prevent dust accumulation.

5. The washer motor cannot work for a long time, and it should work for no longer than 5s each time. The service intervals of the washer motor should not be less than 10s. Do not turn on the washer motor in case of no washer liquid.

6. Spray hoses should be fastened. It is strictly forbidden to unplug the spray hoses casually. Be careful not to flush the nozzle of the spray hose for a long time when washing the vehicle to avoid corrosion and aging.

7. For low-temperature areas, be sure to add the detergent that meets the local temperature requirements.

8. Do not use antifreeze or other substitutes, in order to avoid damaging the windscreen and body paint.

### 5.2.3.2 System descriptions

1. The wiper and washer system mainly consists of front wiper arm and blade assembly, front wiper drive system assembly, washer fluid reservoir assembly, washer hose and nozzle, rear wiper and blade assembly, and rear wiper motor assembly. This system has various wiping functions, such as single-step wiping, intermittent wiping, slow wiping and quick wiping. 2. Wiper and washer system aims at providing drivers with convenient, safe and reliable means to ensure the view of windscreen.

### Diagnostic steps

a. Replace the rear compartment distribution box with a new one.
b. Restore the vehicle, clear all module fault codes, and perform the test drive for functional inspection.
c. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

Follow the above diagnostic steps and check again.

### 1. Check the working condition of the wiper and washer system

a. Power up the vehicle for rain test, turn the multi-function switch for wiper to the LO, HI, AUTO modes respectively and observe whether the system works normally; if not, refer to the relevant contents of the symptom list for repair.
b. Power up the vehicle for rain test, turn the multi-function switch for wiper and check whether the wiping effect of wiper is good; if not, refer to the relevant contents of the symptom list for repair.
c. Power up the vehicle, turn on the washing function, and check whether the spraying condition of washer fluid is good; if not, refer to the relevant contents of the symptom list for repair.

### 2. Check the system components

a. Check whether the system has obvious signs of mechanical or electrical damage; if so, repair it. b. Check whether the system has obvious signs of collision-induced deformation; if so, repair it. c. Check whether the system fasteners (such as bolts or nuts) are loose; if so, retighten them.

3. Check the washer fluid

a. Check whether the washer fluid meets the standard; if not, replace it.
b. Check whether the washer fluid is sufficient.

0 Tip:

As washer fluid is a consumable product, please check it regularly. If it is insufficient, please add washer fluid. It is also necessary to add washer fluid in the warm season, because its strong cleaning ability can remove the dirt on the front and rear windscreen assemblies.

4. Check the washer pipeline

a. Check the washer pipeline for looseness, breakage, aging, etc. If any, replace the washer pipeline.

5. Check the nozzle assembly

a. Check whether the spray direction of the washer nozzle is incorrect; if so, reinstall the nozz b. Check whether the washer nozzle is blocked; if so, dredge the nozzle.

6. Check the washer fluid reservoir a. Check the washer fluid reservoir for cracks, breakage, aging, etc.; if any, replace it.

7. Check the wiper blade a. Check the wiper blade rubber strip for aging, cutting, deformation, wear, etc. and replace it if necessary.

8. Check the wiper arm a. Check whether the wiper arm is installed at the correct position; if not, reinstall it. b. Check the wiper arm spring for good elasticity; if the spring fails, replace it.

9. Check the front wiper drive system assembly a. Check whether the wiper drive mechanism is deformed or damaged; if so, replace it.

b. Check the wiper drive mechanism for rust or insufficient lubrication; if any, apply grease to its moving parts.

### 10.Treatment for abnormal sound of wiper

a. First, lift the wiper blade and wiper arm away from the windscreen and restart the multifunction switch for wiper for wiping and washing operations. Next, determine whether the abnormal sound is caused by the contact between the wiper blade and the windscreen or by the fault of the wiper system itself. Finally, clean, adjust and repair the parts producing abnormal sound, and replace them if necessary.
b. Check the windscreen: If there are foreign matters on the windscreen, clear them away; if there are thick scratches or cracks on the windscreen, replace the windscreen; check whether the wiper blade or wiper arm is deformed or damaged, and repair or replace it according to the actual situation.
c. Check the washer fluid: If the washer fluid does not meet the standard, replace it with standard one to ensure that the wiper blade works smoothly.
d. Windscreen cleaning method: Use qualified windscreen cleaning agent for cleaning the windscreen; after cleaning, if the water does not form water droplets but is evenly distributed on the entire windscreen surface, it indicates that the windscreen has been cleaned.
e. Wiper blade cleaning method: Lift each wiper blade assembly from the windscreen assembly, wipe and clean the wiper blade rubber strip with a rag soaked with washer fluid until the black deposits disappear, and clean the rubber strip of the wiper blade assembly with clean drinking water.

### 5.2.8.1 Wiper blade assembly of front wiper

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the left wiper blade assembly of front wiper as an example. For the removal and installation of the right wiper blade assembly of front wiper, please refer to the left side.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the left wiper blade assembly of front wiper a. Turn on the front wiper service mode.

![](images/fb26c7e6f9960fc826caac3d6c3b26d1633b28da32d3e43446d68331ea14a4a3.webp)

b. Lift the wiper arm, press the button, and take out the front wiper blade assembly in the direction of the arrow.

### i Caution:

After removing the wiper blade, gently put the wiper arm back to its original position to prevent causing damage to the front windscreen. Place a towel or equivalent between the wiper arm and the front windscreen to avoid damaging the front windscreen.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the left wiper blade assembly of front wiper in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the front wiper can work properly and clean the windscreen effectively.

### 5.2.8.2 Wiper arm and blade assembly of front wiper

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the left wiper arm and blade assembly of front wiper as an example. For the removal and installation of the right wiper arm and blade assembly of front wiper, please refer to the left side.

### 1. Remove the left wiper arm and blade assembly of front wiper

a. Open the bonnet and pry out the trim cover of front wiper arm nut.

![](images/9ee63f6f466c0bf45e5646babe61acf817e38eb8cd16f2dba339b6dcc1db3d04.webp)

b. Remove one fixing nut. Torque: 18\~22N•m
c. Shake the wiper arm and remove the wiper arm and blade assembly of front wiper.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the wiper arm and blade assembly of front wiper in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the front wiper can work properly and clean the windscreen effectively.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Remove the front left/right compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
3. Remove the left and right wiper arm and blade assemblies of front wiper. Refer to: Wiper arm and blade assemblies of front wiper
4. Remove the ventilation cover assembly. Refer to: Ventilation cover assembly
5. Remove the front wiper drive system assembly.
a. Turn over the waterproof rubber sleeve for connector and disconnect the front wiper motor connector.
b. Remove the 2 fixing bolts and the front wiper drive system assembly. Torque: 8.5\~10.5 N•m

![](images/a74c25e8ffabb0413f1e025972ae5c2852dd84cf7d01af70c7f6dcc414a6fd46.webp)

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front wiper drive system assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the front wiper drive system assembly can work properly.

### 5.3.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Be careful not to damage the side mirrors due to falling during removal.

2. A magnetic sleeve is required to remove and install the fixing nuts, so as to prevent the nuts from falling into the door sheet metals.
3. Since the NFC control module, panoramic view camera and side turning light are installed in the side mirror assembly, avoid damaging these components when removing and installing the side mirror assembly.

### 5.3.3.2 System descriptions

1. The electric side mirrors and assembly are adjusted with electric adjustment switch.

2. The electric exterior rearview mirror has the following functions:

a. Levelness adjustment of mirror.
b. Vertical adjustment of mirror.
c. Heating & defrosting functions of the side mirror.
d. Electric folding and unfolding.
e. Automatic folding function upon vehicle locking.
f. Automatic unfolding during unlocking.
g. Automatic mirror adjustment during reversing.
h. Memory function.

### 5.3.7.1 Exterior rearview mirror assembly

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the left side mirror assembly as an example.
For the removal and installation of the right side mirror assembly, please refer to the left side.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left door shield assembly. Refer to: Front door shield assembly
2. Remove the left side mirror assembly.

![](images/4e6f8394f5147408cf43fb9c3ef45652a90a370bdab12f542e8680db9b340a8c.webp)

a. Disconnect the left side mirror assembly connector A.
b. Disconnect the side-view camera assembly connector B.
c. Take off the mounting hole patch, remove the wiring harness through-hole rubber sleeve, and remove 3 fixing nuts. Torque: 7N•m

### 0 Tip:

When removing the nut, support the side mirror assembly from the outside of the door to avoid falling.

![](images/1eea85dd735728dbe340c2ac8ec04599e56723aed62a59fea5ec21846fd86db0.webp)

d. Remove the side mirror assembly.

### 0 Tip:

When removing the side mirror, the wiring harness should be slowly removed to avoid damage to the connector and the throughhole rubber sleeve.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the left side mirror assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following items:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the side mirror and turning light are working properly.
c. Check whether the panoramic view stitching effect is normal. If not, perform the panoramic camera calibration. Refer to: Panoramic camera calibration
d. After replacement of the left side mirror assembly, it is necessary to perform the NFC card matching again if an NFC key card is required. Refer to: NFC card matching

### 5.4.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. In case of accidental blockage of power sunroof/sunshade during use, the power supply of 12V battery (starter Fe battery) should be cut off in time to prevent the sunroof/sunshade motor from burning out.

2. When you need to enter the vehicle to work, be sure to cover the seats, steering wheel and other parts to avoid being stained with oil.

3. When repairing the sunshade, please wear gloves to prevent contaminating it.

4. Do not pull the wiring harness when disconnecting the connector, so as to prevent damage to the wiring harness.

5. After installation, the fasteners must be checked according to their specified torques to ensure that each part can be used normally.

6. Self-learning of sunroof/sunshade is required after installation.

### 5.4.3.2 System descriptions

1. The sunroof system of this vehicle is a panoramic sunroof. The sunroof control motor assembly rotates in both the forward and reverse directions by means of the control motor to implement the opening, closing, tilting-up and tilting-down of the sunroof.
2. This vehicle is also provided with electric sunshade system. It can be opened and closed depending on the opening and closing state of sunroof and by means of sunshade control switch.
3. Both the electric sunshade and power window have anti-pinch function.
4. When the sunroof/sunshade is obstructed while closing. In such case, the sunroof/sunshade will stop moving and automatically retract to some extent.

### 5.4.5.1 Symptom list

![](images/8a02f3289031b2115ab0b03fa207aad8a2833f6d8af8240ee2bb6bb99d6f84b2.webp)

![](images/813e934e62c3f3e90ae1b568a46d53a808678c79ab44d1bf7ed02d115969b074.webp)

### 1. Water leakage

a. Check if the sunroof and sealing strips are installed incorrectly or improperly;
b. Check if there is a gap between the outer sealing strip and the roof panel of vehicle body;
c. Check if the drain pipe and the water outlet are connected tightly and if the clamp gets loose;
d. Check if there is any looseness between fastening bolts and the top cover of vehicle body.

2. Motor noise

a. Check if the sunroof motor and the sunshade motor get loose.
b. Check if motor gear and gear shaft are worn.
c. Check if the flexible shaft assembly is deformed.

3. Motor running, but sunroof/sunshade not moving

a. Check if the motor gear or the interior flexible shaft is installed incorrectly;
b. Check if there is any foreign object between the guide rail and the sliding block;
c. Check if the interior flexible shaft gets loose;
d. Check if the flexible shaft assembly is installed properly.

4. Wind noise found during vehicle running

a. Check if the gap between the sealing strip of sunroof glass and the roof panel of vehicle body is too large.

5. Panoramic sunroof not moving and sunroof motor not running

a. Check if the connector gets loose and if any pin falls off;
b. Check if the sunroof switch is faulty;
c. Check if the voltage of the 12V battery starter (Fe battery) is insufficient.
d. Check if the sunroof motor is faulty.
e. Check if the glass is installed properly.

6. Panoramic sunroof sunshade not moving and sunshade motor not running

a. Check if the connector gets loose and if any pin falls off;
b. Check + f the sunshade switch is faulty;
c. Check if the voltage of the 12V battery starter (Fe battery) is insufficient.
d. Check if the sunshade motor is faulty;
e. Check if the sunshade is installed properly.

Troubleshooting.

Follow the above diagnostic steps and check again.

### 1. Check for foreign matters

a. Open the sunshade completely.
b. With the sunroof completely closed, push with both hands inside the vehicle to check whether the fixing bolts get loose. If so, retighten them.

i Caution: If the fixing bolts get loose, the sunroof glass may move up/down.

c. Open the sunroof completely, and clean the glass sealing strip with wet sponge to remove dust, sand and other impurities.
d. Check whether there are impurities, dust, etc. in the drain channels inside left and right guide rails. If any, gently wipe them off with a clean soft cloth or remove them with a brush. If the grease is wiped off, add some specified grease.
e. Check whether there are sundries in the drain hole. If any, use a high-pressure pneumatic gun or a relatively sharp tool to remove them, to avoid blocking the drain hole and causing water leakage of the sunroof.

### 2. Lubrication inspection

a. Open and close the sunroof, and check whether the sunroof glass gets stuck or produces any abnormal sound during its movement. If so, check the guide rail for foreign matters or excessive dust. After cleaning the guide rail, apply a proper amount of grease and make the sunroof glass move again to fully lubricate it.

### i Caution:

If too much grease is applied, wipe off the excessive grease with a soft cloth to avoid contaminating the interior trimmings and parts of the vehicle.

b. Wipe off the dust and foreign matters inside left and right guide rails with a soft cloth or remove the same with a brush.
c. After cleaning, apply grease to the guide rails with a brush.
d. Open and close the sunroof repeatedly to make the grease be evenly distributed in the guide rails.
e. Apply grease as thinly and evenly as possible to the outside of the roof sealing strip with a brush. No grease layer should be seen after application.

### 3. Fitting test

a. Fully close the sunroof.
b. Insert a 2 mm-thick shim between the roof sealing strip and the glass.
c. Pull out the shim. If you feel some resistance when pulling out the shim, it means proper fitting.
d. Complete fitting adjustment between the glass and the roof by changing the vertical height and alignment of the front sunroof glass.

### 4. Other inspections

a. Check other additional after-sales devices that may affect the normal operation of the sunroof system.

b. Check easily accessible or visible system components for obvious damage or conditions that may cause faults.
c. Check whether the initialisation of sunroof has failed.

### 1. Sunroof initialization

a. Close sunroof.

Tip: • The sunroof may not be closed completely in this process.
b. Call up the sunroof control interface on the centre console touchscreen.
c. Gently pull the sunroof switch for about 7s until the sunroof motor is stalled, and then release the sunroof switch.

d. The centre console touchscreen displays "Initialize sunroof".

![](images/146a18da5f2a2161a64766d28782552a2e8d0f3420b40c984ebc5b38e1bafd75.webp)

e. Click "OK" on the centre console touchscreen.
f. Close the sunroof manually until it is closed completely.
g. Initialisation of sunroof succeeded.

### 1. Initialization of sunshade

a. Close sunshade curtain

0 Tip: The sunshade may not be closed completely in this process.
b. Call up the sunroof control interface on the centre console touchscreen.
c. Gently push the sunshade switch forward for about 7s until the sunshade motor is stalled, and then release the sunshade switch.

![](images/b7d38b2fa87bfe0d69c27182b0704b2a21ec47bbf1f65973d30daec58bd9639f.webp)

d. The centre console touchscreen displays "Initialize sunshade".

e. Click "OK" on the centre console touchscreen. f. Close the sunshade manually until it is closed completely. g. Initialization of sunshade suceeded

![](images/f605266d528097251875c69da5b24ff8bff819cb96bd3c3ad828700596318aa6.webp)

![](images/2b6b173dd3e59ef6c2168fdb87174d3fc82a488ed6a07bb03babd275fdeb98c5.webp)

e. Pull out the sunshade guide blocks ① on both sides from the sunshade tie rods ②.

![](images/3454ff9bf619f47443028a0aa7531f678db476680bd2b515110328c59b90d265.webp)

f. Hold the sunshade tie rod ② to prevent the sunshade from rolling up, and disconnect the metal edges ③ on both sides of the sunshade from the guide block ①.

![](images/c1a181f0028b0115607798e04f9c4ca186461bd658172556deda61a6f6d8911f.webp)

g. Straighten the metal edges on both sides of the sunshade, and slowly roll up the sunshade ① with the rolling force. h. Insert a steel wire or equivalent tool ② into the sunshade locking hole to lock the sunshade.

![](images/ee13dfd5464368492a3ba8b2a1fed8f54d64f90466a19e22c83a0ff2e63297ec.webp)

i. Remove the 6 fixing screws of the sunshade protection steel frame, and remove the sunshade protection steel frame ①.

![](images/dfb7ada5dfce4aac60efecadb18380f7c05bb9893621c05c00b4faeb30a7d9f0.webp)

j. Remove one fixing screw A of the sunshade extension guide rail, and remove the sunshade extension guide rail ① (on left and right sides). k. Remove the 2 fixing screws B of the sunshade reel gland, and remove the gland ②.

![](images/e1191d662b4357b965464fbc446f2732c90d7875bcd78bf840435314ad260ee8.webp)

l. Use a tool to press the clip tongue from the small hole at the position of arrow A, take out one end of the sunroof sunshade assembly, and then remove the sunshade assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the spare parts of sunshade in an order reverse to their removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installing the sunshade for sunroof and before installing the roof, connect the sunroof switch, power up the vehicle and check the opening and closing effect of the sunshade to ensure that the sunshade can open and close normally.
c. If the sunshade cannot be closed completely, perform the sunshade initialisation operation. Refer to: Initialization of sunshade
d. If the sunshade cannot be initialised, operate as follows: open the sunshade completely and remove the 3 fixing bolts of the sunshade motor; have the sunshade execute the opening operation again and idle the motor until the sunshade moves to its fully-open position; and install the sunshade motor.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the air guide bar assembly.

![](images/53128aac0f7ba28482aae33189bcde665edb2d5f6b411f8c08e969889bb2395b.webp)

a. Open the sunroof glass and remove the 3 fixing screws at the front end of the air guide bar from the roof.

> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> The figure on the left is only a schematic diagram. Remove the air guide bar assembly without removing the sunroof assembly.
>
> ![](images/9cf1c95afad06d2f098bc94421f2b4dc3adccbde7ab42296665026ec8838056a.webp)
>
> b. Pry out the clips on both sides and take out the air guide bar assembly.

### 5.5.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Be careful not to damage the rear millimetre-wave radars due to falling during removal.

2. Do not remove or install rear millimetre-wave radars at will.
3. It is necessary to write the configuration for the rear millimetre-wave radars after their removal and installation.

### 5.5.3.2 System descriptions

1. The blind spot detection (BSD) system can judge the positions of rear and side rear objects by transmitting radar waves from rear millimetre-wave radars and receiving reflected waves from objects and combining with the current vehicle state. According to different driving conditions, when a certain risk of lane change or reverse collision is detected, the system can remind the driver by audible and visual alarms.

2. BSD system covers BSD, side assist, rear crossing traffic alert (RCTA), rear collision warning, and door opening warning.

3. BSD: When the rear millimeter-wave radar detects that there is a vehicle in the blind spot of a side mirror when the vehicle is moving at a speed of above 30 km/h, the alarm indicator on the corresponding side mirror will light up. If the turning light on the same side is turned on at this time, the warning indicator on the corresponding side mirror will flash, alerting the driver of possible danger if they insist on changing lanes.

4. Side assist: When the rear millimeter-wave radar detects that there is a vehicle quickly approaching from the adjacent lane while the vehicle is moving at a speed of above 30 km/h, the alarm indicator on the corresponding side mirror will light up. If the turning light on the same side is turned on at this time, the warning indicator on the corresponding side mirror will flash, alerting the driver of possible danger if they insist on changing lanes.

5. RCTA: RCTA uses rear millimeter-wave radar to detect moving vehicles on the left and right sides when the vehicle is reversing, alerting the driver of a risk of collision. If RCTA determines that a collision is about to take place with vehicles approaching from the left and right side while reversing, the warning indicator on the corresponding side mirror will flash to alert the driver of possible danger should they continue reversing and reminds them to drive carefully.

6. Rear collision warning: When the rear millimeter-wave radar detects that a vehicle is approaching quickly from behind and there is a risk of collision while the vehicle runs at a speed above 5 km/h, the turn signal on the dashboard and the alarm lights on both side mirrors will light up and flash to remind the driver to drive carefully.

7. Door opening warning: When the door is about to be opened while the vehicle is in Park, DOW can use the rear millimeter-wave radar to identify short-range targets behind and to the side of the vehicle, and will issue an alarm through the DOW indicator on the side mirrors to prevent possible accidents.

### 5.5.6.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select "VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system"→"Passenger car"→"EV series"→"New Tang EV 2021"→"New Tang EV 2021 General"→"ECU module"→"Right blind spot monitoring module (BYD 77G)".

6. Read and clear the DTC.

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear DTC” to clear DTC.

![](images/a419def18cf7f5f57148862e43765dd73b02b52c97e3c4e912192625a320c72f.webp)

7. Refer to "Right blind spot monitoring module(BYD 77G)" for reading and clearing DTCs for "Left blind spot monitoring module(BYD 77G)".

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of the BSD system without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select "VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system"→"Passenger car"→"EV series"→"New Tang EV 2021"→"New Tang EV 2021 General"→"ECU module"→"Right blind spot monitoring module (BYD 77G)".

6. Read data flow

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

![](images/5f090eda7dbd5783c8168000a91fb69ea12259af01cf15990cf2078dd0f5f95e.webp)

7. Select "VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system "→"Passenger car"→"EV series"→"New Tang EV 2021"→"New Tang EV 2021 General"→"ECU module"→"Left blind spot monitoring module (BYD 77G)".

8. Read data flow

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

![](images/314fabf561f7e872bd3e388093408fdd6dffb1b148f24ee2aa82f5871761418b.webp)

![](images/f1ae8d08724f49b3cb7c9f51eeb088fd531884919d702a1da88a0deaa0f2b880.webp)

![](images/4c79c100274b7b7debb98deb3af20b0a674b2e3c5325d8df8b91a661d5092eeb.webp)

### 5.6.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Dropping of any tyre pressure monitoring module should be avoided during its removal and installation.
2. It is necessary to re-match and learn the new tyre pressure monitoring module after replacement.
3. It is necessary to re-match and learn the tyre pressure monitoring module after tyre transposition.
4. The removed tyre pressure monitoring module should be kept in a dry and clean place.
5. Installing additional accessories on the vehicle may interfere with the normal operation of the tyre pressure monitoring system.
6. Driving near a high voltage power line or a wireless transmitter may interfere with the normal operation of the tyre pressure monitoring system.

### 1. Tyre pressure monitoring module

a. It is a module which is installed inside each tyre to measure the tyre pressure and transmit information through wireless transmitter.
b. It is installed near each tyre valve and integrated with the tyre valve. This module consists of a main part and a valve part.

2. Tyre pressure monitoring and control module a. This module receives and processes tyre pressure and other information from the tyre pressure monitoring modules and transmits signals to the instrument via the CAN bus.

### 3. Principle of Tyre Pressure Monitoring System

a. The tyre pressure monitoring system uses pressure sensors installed in each tyre to directly measure the parameters such as tyre pressure and acceleration and sends collected data to the tyre pressure monitoring module through radio frequency. The tyre pressure monitoring and control modules demodulate, analyze and process the data as CAN signals and send such CAN signals to the instrument, where the tyre-related information is displayed in real time in digital form. When the pressure of any tyre exceeds the set normal threshold, the system will send alarms to driver in audible and visual form to ensure driving safety.

### 5.6.7.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select "VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system"→"Passenger car"→"EV series"→"New Tang EV 2021"→"New Tang EV 2021 General"→"ECU module"→"tyre pressure management module (Baolong)".

b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

5. Select "VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system "→"Passenger car"→"EV series"→"New Tang EV 2021"→"New Tang EV 2021 General"→"ECU module"→"tyre pressure management module (Baolong)".

### 5.6.8.1 Check the tyre pressure monitoring system

0 Tip:

Determine the fault cause of the tyre pressure monitoring system based on different alarm modes displayed on the instrument cluster.

### 1. Low tyre pressure

a. Symptom: If the tyre pressure fault indicator on the instrument cluster is lit and the pressure value of a wheel is displayed as "000" (yellow) in the tyre pressure display interface, it means a low tyre pressure alarm.
b. Solution: Check whether the tyre is damaged (punctured by nail, etc.). If the tyre is normal, inflate the tyre with an inflator until the pressure reaches the standard tyre pressure (which is given on the type pressure label pasted on the vehicle body), and check the tyre pressure again after driving the vehicle for a period of time.

### 2. TPMS signal abnormality

a. Symptom: If the tyre pressure fault indicator on the instrument cluster is lit and the pressure value of a wheel is displayed as "Abnormal signal" (yellow) in the tyre pressure display interface, t means an abnormal tyre pressure signal of the tyre.
b. Handling method1: Ask the vehicle owner whether it is an occasional abnormal signal alarm (i.e., the alarm has occurred and got restored, and repeated thereafter). If it is an accidental abnormal signal alarm, perform troubleshooting according the procedure below: Check whether other electronic products (such as on-board WIFI, on-board air purifier, cigar lighter adapter, and vehicle data recorder) are installed in the vehicle and remove them if any. • Perform tyre pressure monitoring module matching for the wheel with abnormal signal, eliminate the fault, and tell the vehicle owner to use and observe the vehicle without removing the electronic products mentioned above for a period of time to confirm that the fault does not recur.
c. Handling method 2: Ask the vehicle owner whether the abnormal signal alarm has never been restored after it occurs. If yes, perform troubleshooting according the procedure below: Read the DTC with a diagnostics device and confirm the fault according to the DTC. Perform tyre pressure monitoring module matching for the wheel with abnormal signal. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring module matching If the matching fails, directly replace the tyre pressure monitoring module of the corresponding tyre. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring module

### 3. ID not registered

a. Symptom: If the tyre pressure fault indicator on the instrument cluster is lit, the pressure value of a wheel is displayed as white "—" in the tyre pressure display interface and the words "Please check the TPMS" are displayed on the instrument, it means that the tyre ID is not registered. b. Handling method: Ask the vehicle owner whether the abnormal signal alarm has never been restored after it occurs. If yes, perform troubleshooting according the procedure below: Read the DTC with a diagnostics device and confirm the fault according to the DTC.

Perform tyre pressure monitoring module matching for the wheel with abnormal signal. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring module matching

### 0 Tip:

This fault will not appear alone. "ID not registered" will be displayed when tyre pressure monitoring module matching fails. If the faulty vehicle has this DTC only, it can be preliminarily determined that matching has been performed for the vehicle outside the service store.

4. This indicates the loss of communication between the instrument and the tyre pressure monitoring and control module.

a. Symptom: If the tyre pressure fault indicator on the instrument cluster is lit, the pressure value of all the four types is displayed as yellow "—" in the tyre pressure display interface and the words "Please check the TPMS" are displayed on the instrument, it means that the instrument has lost communication with the tyre pressure monitoring and control module.
b. Handling method: Ask the vehicle owner whether the abnormal signal alarm has never been restored after it occurs. If yes, perform troubleshooting according the procedure below: Read the DTC with a diagnostics device and confirm the fault according to the DTC. Check whether connector of the tyre pressure monitoring and control module gets loose, and confirm whether the fuse of the tyre pressure monitoring system is blown. If there is no abnormality, please confirm whether the CAN-H and CAN-L are faulty. If all the above mentioned are normal, replace the tyre pressure monitoring and control module. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring and control module

### 5.6.9.1 Tyre pressure monitoring module

0 Tip:

This vehicle is provided with 4 tyre pressure monitoring modules, which are installed in four wheels respectively and follow the same procedure for removal and installation.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the wheel assembly. Refer to: Wheel assembly
2. Remove the tyre. Refer to: Tyre
3. Remove a tyre pressure monitoring module.

![](images/aed2c709bed0ec2c7198cbdc934ec3c2a8043b415581c2acb824a4487d69f609.webp)

a. Remove one fixing screw and the tyre pressure monitoring module.

![](images/051a86aeeb556f4fcb4e97ff6ffd44d42f38c96e470ca7d08a6cf124762a37be.webp)

b. Screw the valve puller ① into the valve to pull out the valve.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the tyre pressure monitoring module in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

![](images/9fbd19e3a1d2b1a6d19c4fc38e9d45966a9be3b7f70d8925ef035f401253a12b.webp)

a. Pass the valve ② of tyre pressure monitoring module through the rim mounting hole, and push the tyre pressure monitoring module into the rim using a tyre pressure sensor installation tool ①;

### i Caution:

When fitting a new tyre pressure monitoring module, do not disassemble the new module into valve part and electronic module part and then re-assemble them. When fitting a new tyre pressure monitoring module, use a tyre pressure sensor installation tool rather than pulling the module with pliers or other tools.

b. After installation, perform tyre pressure monitoring module matching. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring module matching

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Remove the middle toolkit assembly of boot. Refer to: Middle toolkit assembly of boot
4. Remove the tyre pressure monitoring and control module. a. Take out the boot sponge block.
b. Remove the 2 fixing nuts A. Torque: 4.5 N•m
c. Disconnect the connector B and remove the tyre pressure monitoring and control module.

![](images/d201e0f4d57ba858b2c13b135b9c09e536bfa5afbd2b52f7c9bdd0b5192d00f7.webp)

### Installation procedures

1. Install the tyre pressure monitoring and control module in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Ensure that connectors are installed in place.
b. After installation, perform tyre pressure monitoring module matching. Refer to: Tyre pressure monitoring module matching

### i Caution:

Do not put the key in a high-temperature area.
Do not pat the key with a hard object or fling it.
Put the key far away from magnetic field.
When the vehicle enters the anti-theft mode with doors locked, if you do not use the vehicle, please keep the key far away from the vehicle because the power will be consumed as the vehicle performs the automatic key locating function.

2. Precautions for possible failure of electronic intelligent key system

0 Tip:

The electronic PEPS system may not be able to serve in the cases below:
Key battery SOC is low.
There is a very strong magnetic field or electric field (such as TV signal tower) around the detection system.
Key is shielded by metal matters.
The key is put together with a smartphone.
There is another vehicle nearby with its electronic intelligent key system operating.
Carry the key closer to the magnetic card antenna when the key is within the detection range but cannot be identified.

### 5.7.2.2 System descriptions

1. This vehicle is provided with an electronic intelligent key system. As long as the driver carries the electronic intelligent key with him, he/she can open the door and start the vehicle.

2. The integrated vehicle body controller contains an intelligent key system controller, which will detect and verify the key when detecting the key within a detection area, and send operating signals to relevant executing ECU to complete the entire system work.

3. The detection system consists of 6 detection antenna assemblies and can detect the intelligent key in a certain range.

4. The intelligent key system mainly consists of the following components:

a. Integrated vehicle body controller.
b. Intelligent key.
c. Interior detection antenna assembly (in the front of auxiliary dashboard), installed at the front end of the auxiliary dashboard and under the cup holder on the auxiliary dashboard;
d. Interior detection antenna (in the rear of auxiliary dashboard), installed at the rear end of the auxiliary dashboard;
e. Interior detection antenna (under third-row seat), installed under the seat cushion of the third-row seat.
f. Interior detection antenna assembly (inside rear bumper), installed inside the rear bumper and on the rear anti-collision beam;
g. Left exterior detection antenna (inside front left door handle assembly), integrated in the front left door handle;
h. Right exterior detection antenna (inside front right door handle assembly), integrated in the front right door handle;
i. START/STOP button, integrated in the gearshift control mechanism panel assembly.

### 5.7.5.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “integrated vehicle body controller B1(BYD)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/b7d026816d2aa852aabdad73a0dee52cbe61359d76f78ac25b61a858b669dc63.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear DTC” to clear DTC.

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the state information of the intelligent key system without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “integrated vehicle body controller B1(BYD)”

6. Read data flow

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

### Precautions for intelligent key matching

1. Fail to replace the integrated vehicle body controller, and only match the intelligent key.

a. None of the original intelligent keys can be used (all intelligent keys are lost, and there is no old intelligent key), so the blank intelligent key needs to be matched. Apply for an activation code, and then follow the normal key matching process to match.
b. There is still original intelligent key (1 or 2 pcs), so add one blank intelligent key. Apply for an activation code, and then follow the normal key matching process to match the old intelligent key first, then the blank intelligent key.

2. Replace the integrated vehicle body controller, and match the intelligent key.

a. It is necessary to replace the new integrated vehicle body controller from the system and apply for a maintenance code.

0 Tip:

When applying for the maintenance code, it is necessary to provide the VIN, serial numbers of old integrated vehicle body controller and new integrated vehicle body controller.
b. The old intelligent key can be reused: After replacing the integrated vehicle body controller, re-match the old intelligent key according to the intelligent key matching process.
c. If it is necessary to match a blank intelligent key, be sure to follow the blank intelligent key process to match and apply for an activation code.

0 Tip: When applying for the activation code, it is necessary to provide the VIN, serial number of integrated vehicle body controller and blank intelligent key ID.

3. The original vehicle is provided with 2 intelligent keys, with a maximum of 4 intelligent keys for each vehicle.
4. All intelligent keys must be matched every time, and unmatched ones will be disabled.
5. Perform intelligent key controller programming after replacing the integrated vehicle body controller.

### Key lost

1. Mechanical key lost a. If the mechanical key is missing, replace the lock assy directly.

2. Intelligent Key lost

a. Confirm owner s identification.
b. Place order to buy a new key, send the new key ID, integrated body controller s ID and VIN to BYD HQ to apply activation code.

### 5.8.2.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Be careful not to damage the front millimetre-wave radar due to falling during removal.
2. Do not cover or shield the front millimetre-wave radar with other objects.
3. Do not remove or install the front millimetre-wave radar at will.
4. It is necessary to calibrate the front millimetre-wave radar after its removal and installation.

### Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) System

1. The adaptive cruise system is designed on the basis of traditional cruise control to detect the running vehicle and actively control the vehicle speed with radar detecting the relative distance and relative speed with a vehicle ahead. It helps to maintain a safe and reasonable distance between this vehicle and a vehicle ahead, avoiding possible rear-end collision accident. 2. The ACC system automatically follows the vehicle ahead at a safe and comfortable distance, and it is mainly used when driving on expressways and highways with good road conditions. 3. The ACC system consists of front millimetre-wave radar, vehicle controller, IPB system, EPB, HMI (including instrument and ACC switch), and integrated vehicle body controller.

### Front safety-related functions:

Predictive collision warning (PCW)

Emergency brake assist

Autonomous emergency braking intercity

Autonomous emergency braking urban roads

Autonomous emergency braking for pedestrians (with the support of video)

### i Caution:

The ACC function can assist the driver but not serve as a substitute for the driver in driving. The driver must always maintain control of the vehicle and be fully responsible for the vehicle. Even if the ACC is activated, the driver must be careful in driving and follow traffic rules.
The driver should set the distance from a vehicle ahead and reasonably set the ACC system depending on the traffic flow ahead and current weather conditions such as rain or fog. After the ACC system is reasonably set, the driver should make sure that the vehicle can be decelerated to stop at any time.
Maintaining a proper distance from a vehicle ahead is the responsibility of the driver. The ACC system cannot recognize pedestrians and vehicles travelling in the opposite direction.
For stationary objects such as vehicles, tail end of vehicle stream, toll stations, bicycles or pedestrians, the ACC will react in special conditions only which are highly specific.

### 1. Predictive Emergency Braking System (PEBS)

a. Continuously analyze the traffic situation ahead and the driver's reaction.
b. Detect the impending rear-end collision as soon as possible.
c. Trigger relevant measures to avoid/mitigate collision.

### 2. Predictive collision warning

a. Brake system preparation: Make pre-inflation and adjustment of hydraulic brake auxiliary threshold.
b. Give a pre-warning (audio/visual), or even a severe warning (brake pulse) in the case of an upcoming frontal collision.

### 3. Emergency brake assist

a. Be the extension of predictive collision warning (PCW) function.
b. Autonomously increase the braking force if the driver reacts but the braking force is insufficient.

### 4. Autonomous emergency braking

a. Autonomous emergency braking - intercity Apply partial autonomous braking to get more reaction time and guide the driver to make emergency braking. Avoid collision with other vehicles or reduce severe collisions.
b. Autonomous emergency braking urban roads Apply autonomous braking to avoid or mitigate collisions on urban road sections. Apply emergency braking for fixed targets to avoid collisions or reduce severe collisions on intercity roads.

### 5. Pedestrian protection

a. Apply pedestrian protection emergency braking to avoid or reduce the collision with pedestrians.
b. Pre-warning: to remind the driver of avoiding dangerous driving.
c. Pre-inflation: Hydraulic brake assist: prepare the brake system in advance to quickly output the braking force, or output the maximum braking force under certain conditions. Autonomous emergency braking: This function will be triggered in case of an imminent collision with pedestrian(s) and no driver reaction.

### 6. Emergency brake assist

a. The driver triggers the target-based emergency braking.
b. The system calculates the required deceleration to avoid collision.
c. The system enlarges the target braking force in case of insufficient braking force applied by the driver.

### Multi-function video controller (MPC) system

1. Traffic sign recognition

a. Provide stable and real-time calculation for recognition of circular road signs (speed limit signs).
b. Speed limit reminder: to display a warning in case of overspeed.

2. LDW/LKS (lane departure warning/lane keeping system)

a. When the vehicle deviates from the current lane unintentionally, the LDW system will give a warning to remind the driver, while the LKS will help the driver to keep in the current lane without giving any warning.
b. The camera helps to identify the road boundary line and the vehicle position. The LDW system gives a tactile, vocal or graphic warning to remind the driver of lane departure. The LKS keeps the vehicle in the current lane by applying steering torque. When any turning lights are activated or the vehicle speed is below 60 km/h, the LKS function will automatically turn off.

### 3. Intelligent control of headlights

a. Automatic switching among headlights will be performed when a vehicle is coming from the opposite direction or there is a vehicle ahead.

b. Headlights are in the vertical direction according to the distance information.
c. Headlights are controlled in the horizontal direction to illuminate side areas.

### Multi-function video controller assists front millimetre-wave radar

1. The multi-function video controller can assist the front millimeter-wave radar in identifying stationary vehicles ahead and remind the driver of active deceleration at a suitable distance, so as to avoid collision with such vehicles.
2. The multi-function video controller can assist the front millimeter-wave radar in identifying the vehicle ahead which runs inside the current lane and has a coincident trajectory with the current vehicle as the target, and allow the driver to follow the target in cruise control mode.
3. The multi-function video controller and the front millimeter-wave radar can timely identify the vehicles which run on both sides and try to change to the current lane as targets, and allow the driver to brake when necessary.
4. The multi-function video controller and the front millimetre-wave radar can identify pedestrians ahead in time, so that the collision possibility of the vehicle can be reduced.

### Functions to be achieved after integrating front millimeter-wave radar with multifunction video cont

The predictive emergency braking system has two functions: predictive collision warning (PCW) and automatic emergency braking (AEB). When the system detects a potential risk of collision between the vehicle and any other vehicle, pedestrian or other object ahead, an audible and visual alarm will be issued to provide the driver with sufficient reaction time and when the situation continues to worsen, apply a short brake or even make automatic emergency braking to assist the driver in avoiding collision or mitigating injury caused by collision.

### 5.8.4.1 Exploded view of components

Adaptive cruise control system

![](images/57166cfb5a95e22406324e10d4850eeae528aaa7017993abd5922814f4402b7c.webp)

![](images/6c994c626e04c5bb24a2b6ec6210c4fe41e27d76d8ba529cdb0e3977b68db112.webp)

### False triggering by signs at tunnel top

1. False triggering target: signs at tunnel top
2. Function falsely triggered: AEB-M \ PreWarning AcuteWarning (autonomous emergency braking at medium speed\ pre-warning acute waring)

![](images/a1540a56b0b6c18c994c6df11e7edc6becc8a937eab2a9787cb960708944d91b.webp)

3. Cause analysis: When the vehicle is far away (the function not activated), the MPC camera identifies the target as a truck, which leads to the increase in various parameters such as the probability of target existence and the probability of target being an obstacle after the front millimetre-wave radar and camera are integrated, thus triggering the Warning and AEB.

### False triggering by manhole cover

1. False triggering target: manhole cover
2. Function falsely triggered: AEB-M (autonomous emergency braking at medium speed)

![](images/a66eb588031d94ba10e9cd115131c452137c22976ef37ba341b53e57bae7d6cf.webp)

3. Cause analysis: There are several manhole covers on the ground before the moment of triggering and these manhole covers are interfering.

### False triggering by iron bar

1. False triggering target: iron bar
2. Function falsely triggered: AEB-M (autonomous emergency braking at medium speed)

![](images/f817d2b8af6bce641949eec1f0217059ff7cd5e22dcc4e6fa84b081a6f403c55.webp)

3. Cause analysis: If the radar detects an object on the ground at the same time, the object may be integrated with the video ghosting object, which will eventually lead to false triggering.

### 5.8.6.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “adaptive cruise control(Bosch)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

![](images/e24f111ca066cc204f57aa42ca74cfce5cc7a91692dcb3e3bd3ee71350d6dfdc.webp)

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the state information of the ACC system without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “adaptive cruise control(Bosch)”

6. Read data flow

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

![](images/8cab88f6e8e0edefd1f887f6df2c495f50691d0db7a40101a731f7a20f88d4ed.webp)

7. Read other data flows as per the steps similar to those described above.

### ACC calibration principle

1. The purpose of front millimetre-wave radar calibration is to calibrate the radar axis to coincide with the vehicle's dynamic axis (driving axis), thus achieving the calibration and compensation of the radar installation deviation.

2. The angles of -2°, 0° and +2° are formed by an inclined reflection board to measure the radar deviation from the vehicle's driving axis in the horizontal and vertical directions, and adjusting bolts of the radar are adjusted according to the indication of VDS to achieve the purpose of calibration.

### 1. Site Requirements

a. Maximum flatness of equipment placement area: 1 mm b. Maximum flatness of vehicle parking area: 10 mm c. Slope of vehicle parking area: -3°\~1°

### Lighting requirements

Refer to local standards for ambient brightness.

![](images/6e24cc7d5f779dbc22b6f620ecd352438ddb6cd09d77668ccdb6d24ddfc85cd6.webp)

### i Caution:

The static calibration may not be successfully completed in the case of pulsed LED lighting.

1. During calibration, the illumination intensity on the calibration board must be uniform, with special attention paid to the following:

a. The calibration board should not be directly illuminated by any light source (including direct sunlight).

b. The calibration board should not be illuminated by vehicle headlights.
c. No shadows should appear on the calibration board.

2. Illuminance requirements for calibration board

a. Illuminance of calibration board area: 200\~35,000 lx (without interference light source).
b. Brightness requirements for calibration board: White area: 60\~10,000 cd/m2 Black area: less than 3% of the white area

### Measuring steps

1. Park the vehicle, apply the parking brake, and centre the steering wheel.
2. Adjust the calibration service tool.

![](images/0658dd504b9172ed3fa1c695da35b412f03009dbbc9a41ee5e46d63013f9177c.webp)

a. Fit the two fixtures on the two rear hubs respectively.

![](images/d1506afd409d48d87d622bd0a3e541bf0ed4055ed4c75e68636408c53df4ef53.webp)

b. Install the laser transmitter on the rear wheel fixture, with the scale facing the front of the vehicle.

![](images/b7940ed4075d14509fe0f2f92124a024c4345eca60583f9a702806f36c352aed.webp)

c. Place the calibration frame in front of the vehicle and keep a proper distance.

### 0 Tip:

Make sure that the centre of the calibration cross beam is 2,130 mm from the centre of the front axle.

![](images/80aee1e8d25e84a38c05690099a224d8755cb6f9792c34f068eb346f91a4d378.webp)

d. Adjust the three supports of the calibration frame so that the four wheels on the base are off the ground, and adjust the height of the three supports so that the radar reflection board is level (refer to the levelling tool).

![](images/79a953beb3cb5636c495fb54923814ae9f0d523792c748e92a7ce6c113ac28f5.webp)

e. Turn on the power supply of the laser transmitter installed on the rear wheel, and make the laser beam hit the scale on the cross beam.

f. Adjust the cross beam fine-tuning handle A to make the scales marked by the left and right laser points be consistent, and tighten the locking handle B to lock the cross beam.

![](images/f34217ed9f6cfee767ef0b7fc53f0a15aab554ee015f418ab776d3c257be57e7.webp)

g. Adjust the cross beam fine-tuning handle, so that the laser beam is reflected on the scale plate of the laser transmitter and the effects on left and right sides are the same.

![](images/7cc47ed4bd60520c2c483e97b9f47f68aa10a3d9b5315771692c5bc4f490d407.webp)

h. Press the unlock button A, and adjust the height of the radar reflection board centre to be the same as that of the front millimetre-wave radar centre by operating the lifting handwheel of the calibration service tool.

i. After these operations, start the calibration.

### MPC calibration principle

1. The camera may deviate from the specified installation position during the replacement and installation of the front windscreen or camera.

2. To compensate for the said deviation, the system must be calibrated to determine the relative installation error between the camera and the vehicle body and the installation error should be compensated using a software.

### 1. Site Requirements

a. Maximum flatness of equipment placement area: 1 mm b. Maximum flatness of vehicle parking area: 10 mm c. Slope of vehicle parking area: -3°\~1°

### Lighting requirements

Refer to local standards for ambient brightness.

![](images/b78b07d9f8b75f985fcefc92da3a0935ca2da01c55a8353e31227f5687f087de.webp)

### i Caution:

The static calibration may not be successfully completed in the case of pulsed LED lighting.

1. During calibration, the illumination intensity on the calibration board must be uniform, with special attention paid to the following:

a. The calibration board should not be directly illuminated by any light source (including direct sunlight).
b. The calibration board should not be illuminated by vehicle headlights.
c. No shadows should appear on the calibration board.

2. Illuminance requirements for calibration board a. Illuminance of calibration board area: 200\~35,000 lx (without interference light source).

b. Brightness requirements for calibration board:

White area: 60\~10,000 cd/m2 Black area: less than 3% of the white area

### 1. As for camera calibration, there are the following requirements for the vehicle:

a. Vehicle headlight must be turned off.
b. It is required to ensure that the vehicle has undergone four-wheel alignment before camera calibration.
c. The tyre pressure is correct.
d. The driving axis of the vehicle body needs to be level with the normal of the calibration board.
e. During calibration, the vehicle is empty and there is no one in the vehicle;
f. The vehicle speed is 0, and the vehicle power is set to "OK".
g. Use the parking brake.

2. No obstruction exists between the calibration board and the camera, with special attention paid to the following:

a. The windscreen near the camera is clean and free of dirt.
b. Close the bonnet.
c. No one is or other obstructions are allowed between the vehicle and the calibration board.
d. No smoke or gas that may affect the visibility lies between the vehicle and the calibration board.
e. The camera should not be directly illuminated by any light source (including direct sunlight).

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left/right compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
2. Remove the grille upper cover assembly. Refer to: Grille upper cover assembly
3. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
4. Remove the front left/right wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly
5. Remove the front bumper assembly. Refer to: Front bumper assembly
6. Remove the front millimeter-wave radar

![](images/e50119ff45b21bb9f2ae5d37d4dd6a9e27fcb2221525d0d273669e19c3f65aec.webp)

a. Disconnect the front millimetre-wave radar connector.

![](images/70978520899e68afe7fee93dd4966ca1ff98ac467799578bbac251b09be9dada.webp)

b. Turn the 3 front millimetre-wave radar fixing clips clockwise and remove the front millimetre-wave radar.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front millimetre-wave radar in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following: a. Calibrate the front millimeter-wave radar. Refer to: Front millimeter-wave radar calibration b. After calibration, check that the front millimetre-wave radar can work properly.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly 2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)

3. Remove the multi-function video controller assembly

![](images/870378d001f0cc925ac5fcc9e357c37e8ffb15193eeac2db9f03b9029b7e134b.webp)

a. Pry up the lane departure warning system protection cover II ② from the left side, then move it leftward to remove it.

### i Caution:

The right sides of the protection cover II and the protection cover are of latch structure, so they must be pried from the left side to avoid damage.
b. Pry out the lane departure warning system protection cover ①.
c. Pry out the multi-function video controller assembly, disconnect the connector and remove the multi-function video controller assembly.

![](images/164b08c107001c2179e17351142d52869f31b4ad68f8b24c4383d05bda0ba606.webp)

### Installation procedures

1. Install the multi-function video controller assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Ensure that connectors are installed in place.
b. Perform MPC calibration. Refer to: MPC calibration
c. After calibration, start the vehicle and carry out a road test to check that all functions can be used normally. • Lane departure warning system (LDWS)/lane keeping system Lane keeping system (LKS) Traffic sign recognition (TSR) Intelligent high beam assist (HMA) Intelligent cruise control (ICC) system Functions to be achieved after integrating radar with camera

### 5.9.1.1 Warnings and precautions

1. The rear view mirror is too close to the front windscreen, special attention is required during removal and installation of this mirror to avoid damaging the windscreen.

### 5.9.1.2 System descriptions

1. This vehicle is equipped with an automatic anti-glare rear view mirror. Its lens automatically adjusts the color according to the light intensity collected. This helps reduce the interference of harsh light on your rear view.

2. When the rear view mirror collects the light intensity of the following vehicle, it will automatically activate the anti-glare function, and enter the slight/moderate/severe antiglare state depending on the light intensity.

3. The rear view mirror deactivates the anti-glare function when the vehicle is in R mode;

### 5.9.4.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select "VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system"→"Passenger car"→"EV series"→"New Tang EV
2021"→"New Tang EV 2021 General"→"ECU module"→"Interior Rearview Mirror (BYD)".

6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/7139bf2b0058ec14f0e8b5f983893a8b81428688a4308c16707c962c45d171df.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

### 5.9.4.3 Action test

Use a VDS diagnostics device to test whether the rear view mirror functions normally for easy analysis.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select "VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system"→"Passenger car"→"EV series"→"New Tang EV
2021"→"New Tang EV 2021 General"→"ECU module"→"Interior Rearview Mirror (BYD)".

![](images/d3b5245b76a503979cde2d9a2051caefd5a97f7f26a7427d6b2c5a4468c1c000.webp)

### 6. Action test

a. Select "Auto anti-glare test".

![](images/6cb06876fecfb55e0b2b56cad23ca6145ca814658e7356e03effe5fbc3dfad13.webp)

a. Perform the following action test items:

Click "severe anti-glitz" to activate the severe automatic anti-glare function, and check whether the rear view mirror functions properly under different levels of light intensity. Click "moderate anti-glitz" to activate the moderate automatic anti-glare function, and check whether the rear view mirror functions properly under different levels of light intensity. Click "slight anti-glitz" to activate the slight automatic anti-glare function, and check whether the rear view mirror functions properly under different levels of light intensity. Click "Close" to deactivate the automatic antiglare function, and check whether the rear view mirror functions properly under different levels of light intensity.

7. If the automatic anti-glare function of the rear view mirror is abnormal after the action test, check the related circuits and the rear view mirror assembly according to the circuit diagram.

### Removal procedures

The rear view mirror is too close to the front windscreen, special attention is required during removal and installation of this mirror to avoid damaging the windscreen.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear view mirror assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.

### 5.10.2.1 Recommended tools and equipment

![](images/ccbd1b632672531186736b8985b571907f82a7f88e0b0435e29ffaf5225f41eb.webp)

![](images/5003f7400455d67cb7662a4df43ed0c88b9f92d7fcd5c169413d3ee180aec4ff.webp)

### 5.10.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Do not work in an enclosed place or near a fire source. Do not weld any components filled with refrigerant.

2. Always wear goggles when checking the cooling pipe. Do not let liquid refrigerant enter into eyes or come in contact with the skin.

3. If liquid refrigerant enters the eyes or comes in contact with the skin, rinse the contact area with plenty of cold water. In severe cases, seek medical assistance immediately.

4. Be careful when moving the system components and do not let any system components fall off or bump against other objects.

5. Do not turn on the A/C for cooling when there is insufficient refrigerant in the cooling system.

6. Do not fill the system with too much refrigerant; otherwise, such problems as insufficient heat dissipation and compressor overheat will be caused.

7. Be sure to use special refrigeration oil. Do not use any other brand of refrigeration oil instead or use mixed oil (different specifications).

8. After the cooling pipe is disconnected, the O-ring must be replaced and the new O-ring should be coated with refrigeration oil before installation and then connected with a required torque.

9. As refrigeration oil is highly absorbent, after removing the cooling pipeline, immediately block the nozzle using a plug or cover to prevent moisture or dust from entering the refrigeration system.

10.When recovering excessive refrigerant in the system, do not drain the refrigerant too quickly, in order to avoid discharging the refrigeration oil in the cooling system together.

11.Clean the A/C filter element regularly and maintain good air conditioning quality.

12.Check if the condenser fin surface is dirty. If it is dirty, clean the surface using a soft hairbrush; do not flush the surface using steam or a high pressure water jet to avoid damage to the condenser fin.

### 2. Composition

a. This system mainly consists of electric compressor assembly, condenser assembly, front HVAC assembly, cooling pipe, front PTC driver assembly, air duct, and PM2.5 quick tester assembly.

### 5.10.4.1 Schematic diagram

Schematic diagram of cooling system

![](images/a5cf269f664ac50bb0fe1db05094c61c8b7f64bd5ab1f6191e721d6c7c9f3f9e.webp)

### 1. Principle of the refrigeration system

a. The gaseous refrigerant is pumped out of the evaporator by an electric compressor and then compressed in the compressor, so that high-temperature and high-pressure gas can be discharged to the condenser. The high-pressure gaseous refrigerant is liquefied by the condenser where heat exchange occurs (heat is released) and the heat is taken away by outside air. Next, the liquefied refrigerant goes through the reservoir dryer for moisture absorption. The high-pressure liquid refrigerant is routed through an expansion valve where it undergoes reduction in pressure. The low-pressure liquid refrigerant is vaporized in the evaporator where heat exchange occurs (heat is absorbed). The cooled air near the evaporator is blown by the blower into the compartment. The gaseous refrigerant is drawn by the electric compressor. In this way, the refrigerant circulates in a closed area and the heat in the compartment is steadily rejected to the outside, bringing the temperature in the compartment down to a suitable degree.

### 2. Principle of heating system

a. A PTC air heater is used for heating. The heating system mainly consists of front PTC driver assembly, PTC air heater assembly, blower, air duct and control mechanism. The air from the blower can bring the heat emitted by the PTC air heater assembly into the vehicle or onto the windscreen to increase the interior temperature or perform defrosting, so that heating with hot air is achieved.
