### Fault Diagnosis

The A/C-related faults of this vehicle include electrical appliance failure, mechanical faults of functional components and faults caused by refrigerant and refrigeration oil, and the fault symptoms are no refrigeration, insufficient refrigeration or abnormal sound of the system.

1. Basic judgment The basic method is to intuitively feel the faulty part by observing, listening, touching, etc. a. Observing Observe whether there is any oil stain on the condenser, evaporator or pipe joint. f any, it means that there is leakage of refrigerant and refrigeration oil. Observe whether frosting or icing exists on system components and at pipe joints. b. Listening Listen to the compressor, blower and cooling fan for abnormal sound. c. Touching: Turn on the cooling system for running 15 \~ 20 min, touch the system components with hands and feel their temperature. There should be obvious temperature difference between intake and exhaust pipes of the compressor. There should be obvious temperature difference between inlet and outlet pipes of the condenser, and the outlet temperature should be lower than the inlet temperature. There should be obvious temperature difference between inlet and outlet of the expansion valve. There should be obvious temperature difference between intake and exhaust pipes of the compressor. i Caution: Avoid scalding when touching high-pressure components with hands.

d. Measure the high and low pressure with an A/C pressure gauge, and judge whether the system is normal in different pressure states.

### Fault diagnosis of compressor

1. Startup conditions for compressor (all the following are indispensable):

a. A discharge permission signal is received from the high voltage battery BMC; b. No power-off signal is received from the integrated vehicle body controller; c. A duty cycle control signal is received from the A/C controller (integrated vehicle body controller) and the duty cycle is within 1%\~100%; d. There is no shutdown protection failure of the compressor body (the compressor can work in case of a speed limit protection failure, but it fails to reach the target speed required).

2. Self-check speed limit or shutdown fault of compressor:

![](images/dead1583f1bb5eaa1987915ad879738b72c355e4a8ceff28fb4b0678f2d0dd7b.webp)

### 3. Self-check shutdown fault of compressor:

![](images/9c6cd9563394cb40528e5c1d44bc662b17aa778c354cb944025a87ed0f36aa63.webp)

### Fault diagnosis of front PTC driver assembly

1. Startup conditions for front PTC driver assembly (all the following are indispensable):

a. A discharge permission signal is received from the high voltage battery BMC;
b. No power-off signal is received from the integrated vehicle body controller;
c. A duty cycle control signal is received from the A/C controller (integrated vehicle body controller) and the duty cycle is within 1%\~100%;
d. There is no shutdown protection failure of the front PTC driver assembly body.

2. Abnormal operation of front PTC driver assembly:

### Inspection of A/C compressor

1. Remove the front left compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Disable the high voltage power. Refer to: High voltage power disable and enable
4. Disconnect the connector of the HV distribution wiring harness sub-assembly of the charging and distribution assembly. Refer to: Charging and distribution assembly
5. Disconnect the connector of the A/C compressor wiring harness sub-assembly of the charging and distribution assembly. Refer to: Charging and distribution assembly Measure the

6. resistance of A/C compressor.

![](images/b02e714586b9008360bf9f666274cd9228657d845807e2ca13d67b80491dadd9.webp)

a. Measure the resistance between connector anode and cathode of the A/C compressor wiring harness sub-assembly with a digital multimeter in resistance mode.

### 0 Tip:

Because there is a capacitor on the internal circuit board of the product, charging and discharging will occur during the test and the resistance value will always jump, so that no single resistance measured could be used as the judgment basis.
As long as a measured resistance is at the kΩ level, it is in the normal range. This measured value is only for reference and used for preliminary judgment.

### 7. Measure the pipe pressure drop of A/C compressor.

![](images/c0d0a4cd5596234e0148a55d74477b2566b177c8831f57593043fcf7b9e4cc3a.webp)

a. Measure the pipe pressure drop of A/C compressor with a digital multimeter in diode mode.

As long as a measured resistance is at the kΩ level, it is in the normal range. This measured value is only for reference and used for preliminary judgment.

7. Measure the pipe pressure drop of front PTC driver assembly.

### Diagnostic steps

![](images/f43a55e07fce92cc52eb935645b55dde553bffe1b09f9f2b15b5cdabfeb58284.webp)

a. Read and clear the DTC. Refer to: DTC reading and clearing
b. Check if the fault code exists.

Diagnose it as an occasional fault, and check whether the corresponding connector is loose or damaged, and whether the wiring harness terminal is corroded.

Yes

![](images/57e51bdf0d0828b56eb545524ec24dc5e768256376da59ba476b377c86fb7561.webp)

a. When the vehicle is OFF, disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).
b. Disconnect the wiring harness connector G05 of interior temperature sensor.
c. Disconnect the wiring harness connector G64K of integrated vehicle body controller.
d. Check the wiring harness or connector for corrosion, damage, or pin withdrawal.
e. Check whether the result is normal?

Replace the faulty wiring harness or connector.

![](images/4b8cacc40c2cb2fbe757b3d56a1017616a011db90d1d6ee2083f050ee5f48afa.webp)

![](images/104a459bdf09b13c78c89107783567eafd6e96c28897f96cfd9252bb3a6e65ea.webp)

a. Measure the resistance between the terminal 2 of G05 and terminal 1 of G64K with a digital multimeter.

Resistance:
![](images/ce493cd12877078195ebbbb57044cc06c9e378401db869137a7b4f09dd26c3c3.webp)

![](images/bb29a4dddc5514450a07e862f769c7d4e839096bca8b72abe128dd96858a8430.webp)

b. Measure the resistance between the terminals 1/ 2 of G05 and GND with a digital multimeter.

Resistance:
![](images/c3184307b536db9a3fc00cddcf35317befbde312c0b6a617493c082af9fd15c2.webp)

c. Check whether the result is normal?

Replace the faulty wiring harness.

Yes

![](images/d8a2658d1a2356c1b3599dc87dc03d48ec4f8d0eac070fff3d94d9300c7145f1.webp)

a. Remove the interior temperature sensor. b. Measure the resistance as per the following table. Standard value:

![](images/c4431c32cb0ff983c81d56dd9cb8e898f988a6256aac71ea5da8ba69a150e799.webp)

c. Check whether the result is normal?

Replace the interior temperature sensor.

Yes

![](images/96139272dae9d9bf3b97dc867447b4cb123bfe830ede3612779f93637dff2454.webp)

a. Replace the integrated vehicle body controller with a new one.

i Caution:

Perform intelligent key matching after replacing the integrated vehicle body controller. Refer to: Intelligent key matching b. Restore the vehicle, clear all module fault codes, and perform the test drive for functional inspection. c. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

Follow the above diagnostic steps and check again.

### Check refrigerant leakage

1. Leakage detection by visual inspection

a. Visually inspect the pipeline and check whether there is any oil trace somewhere in the system. If any, this location may be the leaking point.

2. Leakage detection by soapy water

a. Fill the system with nitrogen with the pressure of 1\~2 MPa, and then coat all parts of the system with soapy water. The bubbling location is the leaking point.

### 3. Leakage detection by halogen lamp

a. Light up the halogen lamp for leakage detection and hold the air pipe on the halogen light with hand. When the pipe opening is moved close to a possibly leaking part of the system, the flame color will change to purple-blue, indicating a large amount of leakage here.

### 4. Leakage detection by fluorescent agent

a. Add fluorescent agent to the system according to a certain proportion. After 20 min of system running, wear special glasses and illuminate the outside of the system with a leakage detection lamp. The part with yellow fluorescence is a leaking point.

### Inspect condenser

1. After the condenser has been used for a period of time, it is easy to accumulate flocs on the surface, which affects the heat dissipation of the condenser.

a. If the radiator fin of condenser assembly is dirty, clean it with water and blow it dry with compressed air.
b. Avoid touching the condenser surface as far as possible. If the radiator fin of the condenser assembly is bent, straighten it with a screwdriver or tweezers.

### Refrigerant recovery

1. Remove the front left compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly

2. Refrigerant recovery

a. Start the vehicle, turn on the A/C and run the A/C compressor.
b. Operate the A/C under the following conditions: A/C switch: ON Temperature setting: Lo Blower speed: maximum (7 levels) Operation time: longer than 3 min

### 0 Tip:

This makes most of the compressor oil in different parts of the A/C system collected in the A/C compressor.
If the A/C does not work due to compressor failure, there is no need to operate as per the steps above.

c. A/C is turned off.

![](images/a53db85f9262f9e647be0807547fde56ec95172086a06f3bdf8d6befdff97b24.webp)

d. Use a refrigerant recovery and filling machine to recover refrigerant from the A/C system.

### i Caution:

Do not turn on the A/C switch after finishing refrigerant recovery and before filling refrigerant into the A/C system; otherwise, because the compressor may be damaged when it works without refrigerant.

### 0 Tip:

Please use the refrigerant recovery and filling machine according to the manufacturer's instructions.

### 1. Add refrigerant

a. Use a refrigerant recovery and filling machine to vacuum the A/C system.

0 Tip: Please use the refrigerant recovery and filling machine according to the manufacturer's instructions.
b. Hold the pressure for 5min to confirm whether there is any change in pressure.
c. After there is no change in pressure, use a refrigerant recovery and filling machine to add refrigerant to the A/C system. Refrigerant specification: R-1234yf Refrigerant capacity: 720±20g

### 0 Tip:

Please use the refrigerant recovery and filling machine according to the manufacturer's instructions.
The refrigerant recovery and filling machine cannot recover 100% of the refrigerant in the A/C system. When filling the refrigerant, make sure that there is enough refrigerant in the filling machine.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Remove the front left compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
3. Recover refrigerant. Refer to: Refrigerant recovery and filling
4. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
5. Disable the high voltage power. Refer to: High voltage power disable and enable
6. Remove the front motor lower mudguard assembly. Refer to: Front motor lower mudguard assembly

7. Remove the electric compressor assembly a. Disconnect the low voltage connector of the electric compressor.

### i Caution:

The normal reception of satellite signals will be affected when:
the vehicle is running in rainy weather or between tall buildings.
the vehicle is running in tunnels or underground parking lots, or on overpasses, viaducts or boulevards.
there is any metal object above the vehicle.

### 3. Important tips for radio

0 Tip:

If the grounding connection of the antenna is not firm, it will cause noise when broadcast information is received. Even if the antenna is replaced with a new one, such a problem still cannot be effectively solved.

### 5.11.6.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021 → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Multimedia player_ Android(BYD)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

### 5.11.6.5 System cannot be switched on

Diagnostic steps

![](images/847aa16a8374764581f1b36a9ae2ec7c9f60f3bbe11508ffe0e8d89ce672cbe8.webp)

a. Power up the vehicle and check whether the PAD display screen is turned on normally. b. Check whether the buttons on the operation panel and the touch screen can work normally. c. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

![](images/45ca8d6cf283cde5af1f8a0eb0ac85b122ff2233ec8401fe55e8c78b81f8cdc6.webp)

![](images/9227f6879f8f87f476025f1d2fb096ac1d753c8937d8d97a8bc8f9db97fbac86.webp)

a. Check whether the fuses F2/13 in the dashboard distribution box are blown.

Standard value:

![](images/8780859b10c9dbd66f583bd65679cd342fd537869bd6093b9c0d2618bdb436c5.webp)

Troubleshoot the system circuit short circuit, and then replace it with a fuse of the same specification.

![](images/64f81dcd548e1eda79b2181aa20e5bb907391f2088ff0c51ac821170a76d4909.webp)

a. When the vehicle is OFF, disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). b. Disconnect the multimedia player connector G07A.

c. Check the wiring harness or connector for corrosion, damage, or pin withdrawal. d. Check whether the result is normal?

Replace the faulty wiring harness or connector.

![](images/4828512efaf8fc79521aa5c05458062beba5a29e37feff2fa7b37d19b8f69358.webp)

![](images/842e66844029ec7953c94965c7ace77c96066fabce2ca04314ae6fb26c892356.webp)

a. Measure the resistance between the terminals 7/ 21/28/29/30/31/32 of G07A and GND with a digital multimeter.

Resistance:
![](images/608bc205db9ffcc8997745a6519bee52f7e82181f717e18f843be78ab56d84ec.webp)

b. Connect the multimedia player connector G07A.
c. Connect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and start the vehicle.
d. Measure the voltage between the terminals 12/ 13/14/15/16 of G07A and GND with a digital multimeter. Voltage:

![](images/de1518a2b6d24cd1f6284e7052b534dc3de5254ca00827a031a3c9d1609c21c4.webp)

![](images/54deb19a118b337909beb392d45ee76d3718d5f06115eff4dbe93039a61d0ce1.webp)

e. Measure the voltage between the terminals 7/21/ 28/29/30/31/32 of G07A and GND with a digital multimeter. Voltage:

![](images/5025525bbee9118228fd94c3292a33ed2ee79cdc836bafd9f118d86e0732cedc.webp)

![](images/94176c1b4ae7ff7469e2babfc5c66bd25a37eb46bb62a7eb14d42b4637294791.webp)

f. Check whether the result is normal?

No

Replace the power supply and GND wiring harness.

Yes

![](images/38a99b4bab8a007b484746ad39e093f2aded22e9da8611cc1934fce0a12ae0d0.webp)

a. Replace the wiring harness between the PAD display screen and the multimedia player with a new one. b. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

No

![](images/939f0723daebc0fb1ad3918d1fac0f25c2b394c07208f676dae4835d26fa2661.webp)

a. Replace the multimedia player assembly or the PAD in turn.
b. Restore the vehicle, clear all module fault codes, and perform the test drive for functional inspection.
c. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

Follow the above diagnostic steps and check again.

### Diagnostic steps

Yes

![](images/5eee94c86666301b21ff442cdec23945d56ac9c960249bbda541cc6acb3994d0.webp)

![](images/5c9e334bc530ba3827480a876c48f9959be60f144b0c67b95b3b5f1b2d0c49ba.webp)

### 5.11.6.10 Black screen error

Diagnostic steps

![](images/e042c9c3d5ca9288a2d57e5d868555231ea909ffa67e31872a8b460067637098.webp)

a. Power up the vehicle and check whether the PAD display screen is turned on normally. b. Check whether the buttons on the operation panel and the touch screen can work normally. c. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshooting.

![](images/d2d46071970676ba8064a6767fc5576565d1aae688a12a4ce7c6920efe9e6f0e.webp)

a. Check whether the interior temperature and humidity change greatly. Excessively high temperature difference and humidity will easily cause a short circuit of the circuit inside the PAD display screen.

### Precautions

1. It is recommended to perform matching during routine vehicle maintenance in the following circumstances. If the panoramic view stitching effect is not affected, matching is unnecessary:

a. Replace the front bumper assembly or front grille.
b. Replace the side mirrors.
c. Replace the camera.

2. + poor panoramic view stitching effect is encountered during routine vehicle maintenance, piece of panoramic view calibration cloth must be used to calibrate the panoramic view system.

### Site and scene requirements

1. The calibration site should be open, with an area of 8m×11m at least.

2. The calibration site should be level.
3. The calibration site should be free of accumulated water or stones, to avoid soiling and breaking the matching cloth.
4. The light should be sufficient and uniform.
5. The calibration cloth must be spread level.
6. The middle area of the calibration cloth should be at equal distances away from and be parallel to the front and rear of the vehicle and the left and right sides of the vehicle body respectively.

### i Caution:

No power-off of the vehicle is allowed during calibration.

a. Park the vehicle in the middle of the central box on the matching cloth and make the wheels face the front, without deflection or tilt.
b. Make sure that the light i s uniform and there is no stain on the white calibration cloth.
c. Turn on the panoramic view system and switch to the front/rear/left/right view by pressing the corresponding button on the steering wheel, and confirm that the panoramic view can be displayed normally before matching.
d. Exit the panoramic view system by pressing the corresponding button on the steering wheel.
e. With the vehicle in P or N mode, click "Time Zone" in "Settings-DiLink-Time-Time zone" for 10 times in the centre console touchscreen.
f. Calibration interface: The system enters the calibration interface for automatic calibration, image call-out and identification of calibration points.
g. The centre console touchscreen displays "Calibration succeeded".
h. The system automatically exits the calibration interface and enters the panoramic view interface to confirm the calibration effect.
i. Calibration completed

### Panoramic camera calibration acceptance

1. After successful panoramic camera calibration, open the panoramic view interface in situ to observe whether the calibration area is spliced normally.
2. After matching, drive the vehicle slowly out of the calibration site. During this period, pay attention to whether the ground reference frame on the screen is obviously misplaced or ghosted.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the PAD display screen assembly a. Power off the vehicle.

![](images/3e48d97fda0e0f5f41a8b70eaa4513615d25a6301c99b415de2e719d1332379f.webp)

b. Pry out the 4 clip tongues and remove the PAD maintenance hatch cover assembly.

![](images/4fadd5ccb1c06871616849cbee683ef86cbd9011f9cafdf97e4f9f8790b93119.webp)

c. Remove the 2 fixing screws and rotate the PAD display screen assembly to move it out.

### 0 Tip:

Rotate the PAD display screen assembly clockwise a little to move it out.

![](images/378607ee1fce617d36cbd5c16d422feceb0c4fda535dabdbaebeea878d4f3abc.webp)

d. Disconnect the connector and remove the PAD display screen assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the PAD display screen assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following: a. The connector should be installed in place.

b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the PAD display screen assembly can work properly.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the PAD display screen assembly. Refer to: PAD display screen assembly
2. Remove the display screen bracket assembly

![](images/8892dea40f136c7a0263bf5076850a0b7cea1b0f0f2752ece232c17a0936bddb.webp)

![](images/3467e6e6d9f46c7c44bdc9fdf37b6e9a4ba8a074d2872246c36741ac435ba6be.webp)

c. Disconnect the connector and remove the display screen bracket assembly.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the display screen bracket assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the display screen bracket assembly can work properly.

### 5.12.2.1 System descriptions

1. The instrument cluster is of liquid crystal type and located in front of the driver seat. It provides the driver with the required information such as vehicle running parameters, faults and mileage. 2. Please refer to the vehicle manual for details of the instrument cluster.

### 5.12.5.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021 “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Combination Meter (Desay)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/f8f7202b4f7f40a29975cc62125da396421c81ab097db6a0b5fce205739c6238.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

### Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of instrument cluster without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021 “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” → “Combination Meter (Desay)”

6. Read data flow

a. Select “Data flow” to read the data flow.

### 5.13.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Important warnings for airbags

A Warning: Unstandardized or incorrect operation during maintenance or replacement of an airbag may cause unexpected airbag deployment, leading to personal injuries/deaths or vehicle damage; furthermore, improper maintenance may also cause airbag failure. Therefore, the supplemental restraint system (SRS) can be repaired or replaced only by technicians that have received professional training. Never use any electrical equipment to operate any circuit of the SRS except for operations described in this manual. When checking and repairing the multi-function steering wheel, neither use a multimeter to check the resistance of the airbag, nor hit/strike the airbag, to prevent unexpected airbag deployment.

### 2. Important tips for airbags

0 Tip:

The backup power supply inside the airbag controller is set to keep the airbag function effective after the power output of the vehicle's 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and alternator is cut off. It consists of a power control circuit and several capacitors.
The airbag and its connectors all employ the short-circuiting bar (copper leaf spring) mechanism to prevent unexpected airbag deployment. The function of this mechanism is that when the connector is unplugged, the short-circuiting bar will automatically get close to the plug or socket on one side of the airbag igniter and short the two lead terminals. This mechanism can prevent unexpected airbag deployment caused by connecting the ignition circuit due to static electricity or unintended electrification.
The SRS circuit can be identified by the wiring harness or connector wrapped with yellow bellows.

3. Important precautions for airbags

### i Caution:

It is difficult to identify an SRS fault, and the DTC of self-diagnosis system in the memory is an important information source for troubleshooting of the SRS. For this reason, before checking and elimination of an airbag fault, the DTC must be read before the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) is removed.
It is necessary to carry out inspection after powering off the vehicle and disconnecting the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) for 90s or longer. As there is a backup power supply inside the airbag controller, if inspection is carried out within 90s after the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) is removed, unexpected airbag deployment may be caused.
The requirements are high for SRS components, all of which are disposable. Damaged SRSrelated components can never be repaired and reused. SRS-related components include collision sensors, driver SRS module, front passenger SRS module, seat belt pretensioners, side curtain SRS modules, airbag controllers, and front passenger detector.
If an airbag has been deployed or the driver/front passenger airbag cover has been scratched, cracked or damaged after a vehicle collision, the airbag or collision sensor should be replaced immediately.
Airbag is a precision component, so the airbag connector must be removed or connected after the airbag is fixed; otherwise, an airbag function failure may be caused.
It is not allowed to change, remove, hit or open any component during maintenance, such as steering wheel, driver airbag cover, front passenger airbag or airbag controller and sensor component; otherwise, the airbag will suddenly inflate or the system will lose its function. During handling or transportation of SRS-related components, the side with the airbag trimming cover should face upwards and SRS-related components should not be overlapped and stacked, in order to prevent serious accidents caused by unexpected airbag deployment.

### i Caution:

All collision sensors are disposable and are not allowed to be repaired.
If any airbag deploys after collision, the corresponding collision sensor should also be replaced.
For replacement of collision sensors, new parts should be used and those parts from other vehicles of different models should not be used.
During installation of collision sensors, they must be installed in the directions pointed by the arrows on sensor housings.

### 5.13.3.2 System descriptions

1. Automobile safety systems are divided into two classes: active safety systems and passive safety systems. Active safety means to enable the driver to identify dangers in advance (e.g., windscreen vision, lighting system, mirrors, etc.) and to avoid dangers in advance (e. g., steering system, brake system, driving antiskid system, and smooth driving control system). Passive safety means to avoid or reduce the harm to the occupants, such as seat belts and airbags. The supplemental restraint system (SRS) in this section is a passive and deployable supplemental protective system. A vehicle equipped with this system can be quickly identified by the "AIRBAG" mark.

2. The driver airbag mark is cast on the trim cover in the middle of the steering wheel, while the front passenger airbag mark is cast on the dashboard above the glovebox. A vehicle equipped with SRS can also be identified by the SRS fault warning light on the instrument cluster. Each time the power is turned to "OK" for system self-check, the SRS fault warning light on the instrument cluster will go on and then go out after self-check.

3. The SRS mainly consists of the following components:

a. Collision sensor.
b. SRS ECU.
c. Clock spring.
d. Driver SRS module.
e. Front passenger SRS module.
f. Side curtain SRS module.
g. Front seat side SRS module.

4. The SRS ECU is installed on the central axis of the vehicle, below the auxiliary dashboard. If the voltage of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) is too low or the power supply is cut off due to collision, the SRS ECU can still continue to work for more than 100ms.

5. The driver SRS module is installed in the steering wheel central trim cover and cannot be disassembled. This module includes gas generator, airbag, trim cover, bracket and other auxiliaries. The function of the driver SRS module is to receive ignition signal from the SRS ECU and ignite the gas generator to generate a large amount of gas to inflate the airbag and form an air cushion for protecting the driver.

6. The clock spring is installed on the multi-function switch and composed of spiral cable, rotor, shell, wiring harness and auxiliary structural parts. When the steering wheel is turned, the rotor and steering wheel rotate as a whole and the cable with sufficient length is coiled in the shell spirally so that it will not affect the reliable connection of the wire when the rotor rotates by 2.0 turns clockwise or counterclockwise from middle position.

7. The front passenger SRS module is installed above the dashboard glovebox, and its composition and function are the same as those of the driver SRS module.

8. The front seat side SRS modules are fitted on the sides of the driver seat and the front passenger seat near the doors. The seats fitted with such SRS modules have "AIRBAG" marks sewn on the edge of the backrest skin. The front seat side airbags have the same function as the driver SRS module.

9. The side curtain SRS modules are fitted on the side wall sheet metal at the boundary on both sides of the ceiling, with inflators fitted on the sheet metal in the C-pillar shields and the entire airbags fitted in the ceiling boundary, extending from the D-pillar to the A-pillar. The vehicle model with side curtain airbags has "AIRBAG" marks on the interior trimming surfaces of the C-pillar shield and A-pillar shield. The side curtain SRS modules have the same function as the driver SRS module.

### 5.13.3.2 System descriptions

10.The function of a collision sensor is to transmit collision signal to the SRS ECU as the basis for the SRS ECU to determine whether it is necessary to send the ignition signal or collision unlocking signal.

11.SRS wiring harnesses are used to connect SRS ECU, driver SRS module, front passenger SRS module, side curtain SRS modules, front seat side SRS modules, clock spring and dashboard wiring harness. The SRS wiring harness consists of SRS module drive circuit, warning light circuit, collision unlocking circuit and vehicle communication bus, etc. Its function is to communicate signals between the SRS ECU and the SRS module as well as the vehicle and to ensure reliable communication. The SRS circuit wiring harness can be identified by its yellow cable or plug.

12.The SRS fault warning light is located on the instrument cluster and will go on for informing the driver of a fault in the SRS in case of any fault identified by the SRS ECU self-diagnosis circuit.

13.The working of SRS depends on the angle and severity of vehicle collision. The deployment of an airbag does not depend on the vehicle speed but on the deceleration ratio measured by gravity (G) and this force is measured by the collision sensor. When frontal collision is serious enough, the microprocessor in the SRS ECU will send a working signal to the deployment device of 6 SRS modules to make the airbags deploy. When the vehicle suffers frontal collision and the airbags are deployed, the knee pads work together with the seat belts to restrain the driver and front seat passenger in place; the knee pads can also absorb and disperse the impact energy of the driver and front seat passenger acting on the dashboard structure. When the SRS ECU detects a fault in any SRS component or SRS circuit, it stores a corresponding DTC in its memory and sends information to the instrument cluster to turn on the SRS fault indicator. A fault diagnostics device is needed to properly test the SRS components, read or clear DTCs, and perform maintenance.

### 5.13.5.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New
Tang EV 2021 ” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → ECU module” →Airbag(New)(BYD)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/363cdb461175bed7d737e449a690cfd523a77cd559352aefc76c560920c54228.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

### 5.13.5.3 Action execution

As for the action execution of the SRS, unlock the SRS ECU and test the warning light.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New
Tang EV 2021 → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → ECU module” →Airbag(New)(BYD)”

6. Action execution

![](images/a75b43aa94f46ffb4a846c1937695136cab567dcf7dfe09c174ecde66d700258.webp)

a. Select "Action execution" → "ECU unlocking" to unlock the ECU.
b. Select "Action execution" → "Test of warning light" to test the warning light.

Diagnose it as an occasional fault, and check whether the corresponding connector is loose or damaged, and whether the wiring harness terminal is corroded.

### Yes

### 1. Visually check the airbags.

a. Check the mounting positions of driver SRS module, front passenger SRS module and side curtain SRS module, and make sure that their surfaces are clean and free of foreign objects, bonded decorations and other accessories, cracks or other damages.

2. Visually check the SRS fault warning light on the instrument cluster.

a. The vehicle is powered on.
b. Check the SRS fault warning light on the instrument cluster.
c. If this light stays on or flashes after the self-check, it means that the SRS is faulty. In this case, please use a diagnostics device for troubleshooting.

### i Caution:

Make sure that the clock spring is in the centring position before installing the steering wheel; otherwise, the clock spring will be damaged.

### 1. Centre the clock spring.

a. Check that the steering wheel has been removed. b. Check that the steering system has been assembled. c. Check and make sure that the front wheels are straight ahead. d. Gently turn the clock spring clockwise by hand until it cannot rotate i Caution: When turning the clock spring, operate gently and slowly, and do not apply excessive force to avoid causing damage to it.

e. Next, turn the clock spring counterclockwise for 2.2 turns to align the "△" and "▽" marks. At this moment, the white flat cable that can be seen from the viewing window represents the centring position.

f. Install the steering wheel.

### OVERVIEW

1. To scrap an SRS module, remove it first. To scrap a vehicle equipped with the SRS or scrap an SRS module, always deploy the SRS module according to the following operating procedure.

2. When an airbag is deployed, very loud noise will be generated. Therefore, the airbag should be deployed in an open outdoor area where it will not cause public harm to others.

3. When deploying an airbag, be sure to always use the specified special maintenance tools (airbag initiator, deployment wire, etc.). Carry out the work in a place free from electrical noise disturbance.

4. Deploy an airbag in a place at least 10m away from the SRS module.

5. The SRS module becomes very hot after deployment of the airbag. Therefore, do not touch it at least 30 min after deployment.

6. When handling an SRS module that has deployed, wear goggles and rubber gloves for maintenance. After operation is completed, wash your hands with clean water.

7. Do not water an SRS module that has deployed.

### Functional verification of airbag initiator

1. Connecting the airbag initiator to the 12V battery (starter Fe battery): connect the red clip of the airbag initiator to the anode post of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and connect the black clip to the cathode post.

i Caution: Do not connect the yellow connector, which is connected to the airbag module.

2. Verifying the function of the airbag initiator: press the airbag initiator execution switch and check whether the LED indicator for this switch lights up.

### i Caution:

If the LED indicator lights up without pressing the execution switch, it means that the airbag initiator may be faulty. In this case, do not use the airbag initiator concerned.

### Scrapping of vehicle equipped with airbags

1. When scrapping a vehicle, deploy its airbags in turn, and then scrap the vehicle equipped with airbags. The operation procedure is as follows:

a. Park the vehicle in a flat and safe place.
b. Prepare a 12V battery (starter Fe battery) as the power supply for airbag deployment. To verify the function of the airbag initiator, disconnect the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and make the red clip and black clip of the airbag initiator short-circuited to each other to prevent accidental airbag deployment due to static electricity.
c. Remove the lower shield assembly of multi-function switch, unplug the connector between the clock spring and the SRS ECU, and connect the airbag initiator connector to the unplugged clock spring connector (if the two connectors do not match, cut off the wiring harness on the SRS side between the SRS ECU and the clock spring, connect it to the deployment wire of the airbag initiator, and plug in the connectors).
d. Move away the airbag initiator and keep it at least 10m away from the front of the vehicle.
e. Close all windows and doors, and be careful not to damage the airbag initiator wiring harness.

f. Connect the red clip of the airbag initiator to the anode post of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and connect the black clip to the cathode post. g. Confirm that there is no one inside the vehicle or within 10m of the vehicle. h. Press the airbag initiator execution switch to deploy the airbag. When the LED indicator for the airbag initiator execution switch lights up, the airbags will deploy.

### Scrapping of SRS module

1. To scrap the SRS module only, do not deploy the airbag on the vehicle; instead, remove the SRS module from the vehicle and follow the procedure given below to deploy the airbag.

a. Remove the SRS module.
b. Fix the SRS module onto an old tyre with rim.
c. Attach a thick wire or wiring harness (with insulation sheath stripped) to the rim for fixing the rim and SRS module.

### i Caution:

It is required to use conductor with bare cross-sectional area of 1.25mm² or larger.

d. Fix the SRS module onto a tyre with rim firmly (for the driver SRS module, the trim cover is required to face up).

e. Prepare a 12V battery (starter Fe battery) as the power supply for airbag deployment. To verify the function of the airbag initiator, disconnect the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and make the red clip and black clip of the airbag initiator short-circuited to each other to prevent accidental airbag deployment due to static electricity.

f. Connect the airbag initiator connector to the SRS module with the deployment wire.

i Caution: The airbag initiator wiring harness should be pulled under the tyre.

g. Move away the airbag initiator and keep it at least 10m from the SRS module.

h. Cover the SRS module with tyres, which should have the minimum width of 185 mm and the minimum inner diameter of 360 mm. At least 3 tyres should be used for this purpose.

i. Bundle the tyres together using two wiring harnesses.

j. Connect the red clip of the airbag initiator to the anode post of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), and connect the black clip to the cathode post. Confirm that nobody is within 10m of the SRS module.

k. Press the airbag initiator execution switch to deploy the airbag. When the LED indicator for the airbag initiator execution switch lights up, the airbags will deploy.

### Disposal of SRS module after deployment:

1. After deployment of the SRS module, the gas generator is hot; let it stand for more than 30min until it cools down before disposal.
2. Remove the SRS module that has deployed. Wear goggles and rubber gloves during operation.
3. Put the SRS module into a plastic bag and tie up the plastic bag opening for disposal.

4. After the operation, wash your hands.

### 5.13.7.1 Driver seat SRS module

0 Tip:

When operating a deployed airbag module, be sure to wear goggles and rubber gloves.
When operating an undeployed airbag module, stand beside it as far as possible.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly 2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and wait for 90s. Refer to: Disconnect cathode of 12V battery (starter Fe battery)

3. Remove the driver SRS module a. Insert a straight screwdriver or equivalent into reserved holes on both sides and below the steering wheel, and push the circlips on both sides and the clip tongues at the lower end to disengage the three fixing points of the driver SRS module.

![](images/088c9d2bcb0fcf46d60df7cef05ceef9e402be1e0ac4c1f53019e1db839f33b0.webp)

### 0 Tip:

The figure on the left is only a schematic diagram, showing the internal structure and tool insertion positions. The three reserved holes are in a sealed state during the first removal, but there are obvious depressions visible to naked eyes.

![](images/bb7b151d1e9f2d76bd14b2ad44ec9b03871d8db055c3654834db9eef51aa2923.webp)

b. Disconnect the driver SRS module connector A and the horn wiring harness connector B, and remove the driver SRS module.

### i Caution:

Be careful not to pull the airbag wiring harness when removing the driver SRS module.
Do not disassemble the driver SRS module. When storing the driver SRS module, make its trimming cover face up.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the driver SRS module in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, read and clear the DTC.

### 5.14.4.5 The backup power supply does not work

Diagnostic steps

![](images/3d4ca4f2bc2c86da48ea4d15afc8db082778414fe3161afba224b1cd9370c263.webp)

a. With the vehicle powered on, use a digital multimeter to measure whether the voltage between backup power supply interfaces is 11\~14 V. b. Check whether the result is normal?

Diagnose it as an occasional fault, and check whether the corresponding connector is loose or damaged, and whether the wiring harness terminal is corroded.

![](images/3e8ed6a3ae4f07a33ce06d1f89f8f88fbc2e80b92fd5594f27854f53d7686f41.webp)

![](images/9bf1582d27ca611fd21caea964d85674ed71e3858fbb7de0b62e9fa4803a0759.webp)

a. Check whether the fuse F2/46 in the dashboard distribution box and the fuse F8/22 in the rear compartment distribution box are blown. Standard value:

![](images/322e8f1605e01c8c624c5364329010e8d9560a4a16252cde569a14073e794336.webp)

![](images/c883087db7b5bfa0d339a58f8907411509d7cf223952835d1c95d620bc8fb2cb.webp)

### Standard value:

![](images/bd3022ab396f35ec4360db34bed740b0b137c75dc15dafa47df120f59a9e62bd.webp)

b. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshoot the system circuit short circuit, and then replace it with a fuse of the same specification.

Yes

![](images/91cd5a81ebd840a95c4b0376bacaeba563d4b54be9507b7ba2952e8f8b0aebeb.webp)

a. When the vehicle is OFF, disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). b. Disconnect backup power supply 1 (front row) connector G43 and the backup power supply 2 connector K35. c. Check the wiring harness or connector for corrosion, damage, or pin withdrawal. d. Check whether the result is normal?

Troubleshoot the system circuit short circuit, and then replace it with a fuse of the same specification.

![](images/e11e95822a1268998170528d6e8cf4b3ea9be95070b0951b75c7c5f361a582ae.webp)

a. Measure the resistance between terminal 1 of G43 and terminal 1 of K35 with a digital multimeter.

![](images/725bcd23c86a21405fe99a48aa3a22fa12aaf7fdb406367a4586dff1111ba765.webp)

Resistance:
![](images/d9e368c39ab72a72e959d46701ae6524cf368a406d83e37ce957d8cfb552a019.webp)

![](images/56052f0cf4e0dfcd02dadd815b309ceb2e7d0fd40cec1c3aaff9149cc22af436.webp)

c. Measure the voltage between terminal 2 of G43 / terminal 2 of K35 and GND respectively with a digital multimeter. Voltage:

![](images/19bb0594a043ea0dff6fa3081f3819956ad416ea3861328ab8d5a3e09e618965.webp)

Voltage:

d. Check whether the result is normal?

### 5.14.4.6 Charging port hatch actuator motor does not work

Diagnostic steps

![](images/208dde4694c077d91609ce5edcbc1125f5161ab221816294942247c196850b55.webp)

![](images/8230372f8bcada96339155c6b1a890c18fe0203c72e7fb8798a2a6ce984416b2.webp)

d. Check whether the result is normal?

![](images/49aa0a78c6f7e392247fe9a1b4cf2769660546344c9df738ca322a430730d455.webp)

![](images/853426cebc00e3cbcb2d39235aa0ad5e3d9c6402d584c0784579a36961eee1c6.webp)

b. Disconnect the rear compartment distribution box connector K8B.
c. Measure the resistance between the terminals 1/ 2 of K106 and terminals 9/11 of K8B with a digital multimeter.

![](images/7823aba8e68427b723e900f6d17fd7a77daa956e8b6f46f69c1441b72b685538.webp)

Yes

![](images/a70a912804feac2046edf84ba26097d4c45df24dab2bb5c079ffe4f2774840f1.webp)

Yes

Replace the charging port hatch actuator motor to eliminate the fault.

Follow the above diagnostic steps and check again.

### 5.14.5.1 Snail horn

0 Tip:

A high-pitched snail horn is arranged on the left side of the vehicle, while a low-pitched snail horn is arranged on the right side.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left/right compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
2. Remove the grille upper cover assembly. Refer to: Grille upper cover assembly
3. Remove the front left/right wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly
4. Remove the front bumper assembly. Refer to: Front bumper assembly
5. Remove the snail horn
a. Remove the fixing bolt A, disconnect the connector B and remove the high-pitched snail horn ①.
b. Remove the low-pitched snail horn ② using the same method.

![](images/adfd4ed54079cdef46c51a6aa97f16eee2fff7e70984e026056b43341fd35535.webp)

### Installation procedures

1. Install the snail horn in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, check that both high-pitched and low-pitcthed snail horns can work properly.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear trimming panel assembly of auxiliary dashboard. Refer to: Rear trimming panel assembly of auxiliary dashboard
2. Remove the gearshift control mechanism cover assembly. Refer to: Gearshift control mechanism cover assembly

3. remove the backup power supply a. Disconnect the backup power supply connector.

![](images/6f3e83c629fc0b2a3c3c2023dc1730bd535493eb2381341566329dc9fcfba3ca.webp)

b. Push the backup power supply core ① upward from the inside, and then push out the backup power supply base.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the backup power supply in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following: a. The connector should be installed in place.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear-row backup power supply.

![](images/9e90dec9bbbe568705574eb59f7c5b5e6be946e11ce7ae5552cf55efac698a8f.webp)

a. Pry out the deep low-pitched speaker cover.

![](images/b81ce660d6637854479a496855b53b9e8922400fbbb89e766298879c06411912.webp)

b. Disconnect the backup power supply connector and remove the deep low-pitched speaker cover assembly.

![](images/f2849917c2cf4e6295a03bf0b9576b311dd4fb610ced06a78de531f6a6594439.webp)

c. Push the rear-row backup power supply outward to remove it.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the rear-row backup power supply in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the rear-row backup power supply can work properly.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left door shield assembly. Refer to: Front door shield assembly
2. Remove the switch set #6.

![](images/bd2d12fd945d4abad33c7f5d1b48511bc9fd5d2106df29cc27507f08fcdd1611.webp)

a. Press the clip tongue and remove the switch set #6.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the switch set #6 in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following: a. After installation, check that switch set #6 can normally open the boot lid.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and wait for 90s. Refer to: Disconnect cathode of 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Remove the driver SRS module. Refer to: Driver SRS module
4. Remove the steering wheel assembly. Refer to: Steering wheel assembly.
5. Remove the lower shield assembly of multi-function switch. Refer to: Lower shield assembly of multi-function switch
6. Remove the clock spring. Refer to: Clock Spring
7. Remove the multi-function switch

![](images/9440e89936edcffd3494d5a3fcbadfe877f9f6dbc2d84a1e849ba287d240d61c.webp)

a. Loosen the clamp bolt of the multi-function switch.

![](images/69d7a9c4bcc8f038ea2a7102fa211bd2980b4bab483162ef8bbafd263e9906cd.webp)

b. Gently pry out one clip tongue (arrow A) at the position of the clamp bolt, and remove the multifunction switch. c. Disconnect the multi-function switch connector B and remove the multi-function switch.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the multi-function switch in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following: a. The connector should be installed in place. b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the multi-function switch can properly control the lights and wipers.

### 5.14.5.6 USB Charger Connector

0 Tip:

Refer to the rear trimming panel assembly of auxiliary dashboard for removal and installation of the USB charging connector. Refer to: Rear trimming panel assembly of auxiliary dashboard

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear left/right combination light assembly. Refer to: Rear combination light assembly

2. Remove the rear left/right wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Rear wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly

3. Remove the rear bumper assembly. Refer to: Rear bumper assembly
4. Remove the boot lid button

![](images/77d313e64999af5691a9b7b984fac9e892fd8168b580f7151950e907d8953ece.webp)

a. Disconnect connector A, remove the 2 fixing screws B and remove the boot lid button.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the boot lid button in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, check that the boot lid button can work properly.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the power trunk lid closing button assembly a. Open the boot lid, pry up the bolt trimming covers and remove one fixing bolt.

![](images/ff0825f8d655aca529ced1e9dd33256862c23a006a0d8555bebc16a13f691787.webp)

![](images/92f78de8be8d559ec64113282c4cdb8ae437b6f1e670cea38427c63725cd96d9.webp)

b. Pry out the boot lid handle box assembly and disconnect the connector of power boot lid closing switch assembly.
c. Push out the power trunk lid closing button assembly ①.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the power boot lid closing switch assembly in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, check that the power boot lid closing switch assembly can work properly.

### 5.14.5.9 Charging port hatch actuator

0 Tip:

Refer to AC/DC charging port hatch assembly for removal and installation of the charging port hatch actuator. Refer to: AC/DC charging port hatch assembly

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left sound insulation board assembly of dashboard

2. Remove the brake light switch.

![](images/3336750a98a983532048d05bd0e7e898a3001abb3ca745f1e3faa0855fdc4985.webp)

a. Disconnect the brake light switch connector A. b. Turn the brake light switch ① counterclockwise to remove it.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the brake light switch in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Install the brake light switch and adjust the brake light switch clearance. Refer to: Adjustment of brake light switch clearance
b. The connector should be installed in place.

### 5.14.5.11 Position Adjustment Switch for Steering Wheel

0 Tip:

Refer to the lower shield assembly of multi-function switch for removal and installation of the steering wheel position adjustment switch. Refer to: Lower shield assembly of multi-function switch

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left door shield assembly. Refer to: Front door shield assembly
2. Remove the front left position memory switch.

![](images/25f114e203a560b7aa978ea766306add8bbda979ed908a662345b9c2cfa716f1.webp)

a. Remove the 2 fixing screws and the front left memory switch.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the front left memory switch in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the front left memory switch can work properly.

### 5.14.5.13 Rear door window regulator switch set

0 Tip:

This manual takes the removal and installation of the rear left door window regulator switch set as an example. For the removal and installation of the rear right door window regulator switch set, please refer to the left side.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the rear left door shield assembly. Refer to: Rear door shield assembly
2. Remove the rear left door window regulator switch set a. Remove the sound insulation cotton.

![](images/baa6a5a83b2027956edfdcf8d138ae193702bab2f79ecfd6c00ab6f51c927344.webp)

b. Remove the 24 fixing screws shown in the figure.

### 5.15.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Be careful not to damage the engine sound simulator due to falling during removal.
2. After installation, check the engine sound simulator system and ensure that it works well.

### 5.15.3.2 System descriptions

1. The engine sound simulator is an audio warning device. When the vehicle speed is less than 30km/h, the engine sound is simulated to remind pedestrians to pay attention to the approaching vehicle and safety.

2. The engine sound simulator should emit continuous and even sound, without disturbing sound. After 25,000 sounding cycles, its appearance and function should be normal, and the change in sound pressure level before and after the test should not exceed 2 dB.

3. The engine sound simulator should fulfill the following functions:

a. When the vehicle speed changes from 0 to 30km/h, the engine sound simulator will automatically produce the simulated engine sound;
b. When the vehicle accelerates, the engine sound simulator has a change in acceleration tone; when the vehicle decelerates, the engine sound simulator has a change in deceleration tone. When the vehicle speed is above 30 km/h, the alarm sound of the engine sound simulator is 0 decibel, and the engine sound simulator stops working after receiving a multimedia system shutdown signal.
c. During reversing, reversing alarm will sound at a certain sound pressure level.
d. When the CAN communication of the vehicle is abnormal, the power amplifier will record the DTC and the engine sound simulator will not work.

### i Caution:

Maintenance should be carried out according to standard diagnostic procedures.
It is forbidden to disassemble the integrated vehicle body controller.
Parts can be replaced with those from the specified manufacturers only; otherwise, the normal operation of the system will not be guaranteed.
Do not remove any parts or components or connectors of the system from their installation positions to avoid damage or prevent foreign matters such as water, oil or dirt from entering the connectors, affecting normal operation of the system.
Before the disconnection or connection of connectors, the vehicle must be powered off; otherwise, the corresponding electrical components may be damaged.
If it is necessary to remove the cathode cable or GND wire of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), the vehicle must be powered off and all electrical loads must be turned off. Repair of other electrical appliances can be conducted 90s after the cathode cable or ground wire is removed.
Faults of the body control system mainly include wiring harness faults and connector faults, which are generally broken wiring harness, poor contact of connector, connector terminal being pulled out or not plugged into the bottom, and parts grounded.
It is rare for the wiring harnesses to be broken in the middle, and most of them are broken at the connector, so it is especially important to carefully check the wiring harnesses at the sensor and connector.
Poor contact may be caused by corrosion of connector terminals, external dirt entering terminals, or reduced contact pressure between connector plug and socket. Disconnecting and connecting a connector again can change its connection status and restore its normal contact.
During fault diagnosis, if there is no abnormality when checking the wiring harness and connector, and the fault disappears after reconnection, it can be considered that the wiring or connector is faulty.
Do not prick the wiring harness with fine needle for checking the electrical signals of the system;
Tighten the fixing bolt or nut to the specified torque.
In case of a system fault, if the system fault is not eliminated after the diagnostics device clears the DTC, the DTC will remain when the DTC reading step is performed again until the fault is eliminated. In addition, historical DTCs should also be cleared after the maintenance is completed.

### Description of integrated vehicle body controller

1. Integrated vehicle body controller has the function of traditional vehicle body control module and other functions. Such as i-key (intelligent key) controller, high frequency receiver, A/C controller, park assist controller and gateway, which contribute to compact controller capacity, lower cost and lower weight.

a. Gateway: 4 CAN and 2 Lin connections; available for CAN FD connection.

b. Traditional BCM: lights control, motor drive, lock and unlock, vehicle low voltage power distribution control, vehicle anti-theft system, vehicle locating, and high voltage battery charging/discharging control process, smart charging, OTA, windows/sun-roof control and it s anti-pinch functions.
c. PEPS(Passive Entry and Passive Start): remote lock/unlock, keyless entry and keyless start, remote power ON, reminder of key forgotten, A/C remote start, etc.
d. Park assist: receives 8 radars both front and rear, information communication with other controllers.
e. A/C controller: auto A/C, high voltage battery thermal management system.
f. High frequency receiver: receive the signal from remote control key.
g. Diagnostics: available for VDS functions.

### Description of body anti-theft system

1. When the vehicle is in anti-theft mode, if anyone forcedly enters the vehicle, opens any door, bonnet or boot lid without key, or connects the disconnected cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), the anti-theft system will be triggered, sound an alarm by the horn and make anti-theft alarm indicator flash, which acts as a deterrent to such behaviour.

2. The anti-theft system has four states: not in anti-theft mode, anti-theft setting mode, antitheft mode and alarm mode. a. Anti-theft OFF mode: Both the alarm system and the anti-theft system do not work. b. Anti-theft setting mode: It is the mode before entering the anti-theft mode and the anti-theft system does not work. c. Anti-theft ON mode: The anti-theft system works normally. d. Alarm mode: The alarm system works normally.

3. Alarm form and duration:

![](images/344d39bedad32ea3f2d87d5f4eac67417d672ed6c241540e7a4c84d6cc53a39b.webp)

### Description of four-in-one sensor

1. The four-in-one sensor includes rain sensor, humidity sensor, light intensity sensor and sunlight intensity sensor. The four-in-one sensor is mainly used to assist the vehicle in realizing such functions as automatic wiping, automatic defrosting of front windscreen, automatic lighting and automatic air conditioning, to effectively improve the convenience and comfort of the vehicle.

2. The four-in-one sensor transmits the light, rain, humidity, temperature and other information outside the vehicle to the integrated vehicle body controller through LIN signals, which are subject to relevant control to realise such functions as automatic wiping, automatic lighting, automatic air conditioning and automatic defrosting

### Description of smartphone wireless charging

1. Smartphone wireless charging is based on the principle of electromagnetic induction. There is a coil at the sending end and a coil at the receiving end. The coil at the sending end is connected with a wired power supply to generate electromagnetic signals, and the receiving end senses the electromagnetic signals, thus generating current to charge the smartphone.

### 5.16.6.2 DTC reading and clearing

Use VDS to read and clear the vehicle fault codes, and determine the current DTC to help maintenance personnel to test quickly.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. d. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” “ECU module” →Integrated vehicle body controller B2(BYD)”

6. Read and clear the DTC.

![](images/d9c837e324c67292b92dc14848ca4477449dc2cec4fd49251c5bf360b52b5791.webp)

a. Select “Fault detection” to read DTC.
b. Select “Clear fault” to clear DTC.

### 5.16.6.3 Read data flow

According to the display on VDS, read the data flow of the current system, and read the working state information of the integrated vehicle body controller without disassembling any parts. Reading the data flow first when troubleshooting can improve work efficiency.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. d. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” →Integrated vehicle body controller B2(BYD)”

6. Read data flow

a. Select “BCM related data flow” to read the data flow.

### 5.16.6.4 Action test

Without disassembling any parts, use VDS to conduct action test on the suspected parts, and then judge whether the suspected parts function normally. Active test when troubleshooting can avoid unnecessary disassembly and improve diagnosis efficiency and accuracy.

1. The vehicle is powered off.
2. Connect VDS to the diagnostic interface.
3. Start the vehicle.
4. Turn on VDS and establish communication with the vehicle.
5. d. Select “VDS2000 vehicle diagnosis system” → “Passenger car” → “EV series” → “New Tang EV 2021” → “New Tang EV 2021 General” → “ECU module” →Integrated vehicle body controller B2(BYD)”

6. Action test

### 1. All-door window initialisation

a. With the vehicle powered on, pull up and hold the window switch, wait until the glass rises to the top, keep the window switch pulled up until the window motor is stalled, then release the window switch to complete window initialisation.

### 5.16.8.1 Smartphone wireless charging module

0 Tip:

Refer to the gearshift control mechanism cover assembly for removal and installation of the smartphone wireless charging module. Refer to: Gearshift control mechanism cover assembly

### Removal procedures

1. Remove four-in-one sensor

![](images/d10a06a44e54f2b08d28babb9ad7e07f26a05819410ee841426614b544c63e8b.webp)

a. Pry up the lane departure warning system protection cover II ② from the left side, then move it leftward to remove it.

### i Caution:

The right sides of the protection cover II and the protection cover are of latch structure, so they must be pried from the left side to avoid damage.
b. Pry out the lane departure warning system protection cover ①.
c. Press and hold the middle part of the elastic sheet of four-in-one sensor to disconnect the connector.
d. Press and hold the middle part of the four-in-one sensor and pry open the elastic sheets on both sides.
e. Wait for 5\~10 min, and if the silicone of the fourin-one sensor is still strongly adhered to the glass, forcibly remove the four-in-one sensor.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the four-in-one sensor in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. Clean the mounting position on the glass, and remove residual silicone or other stains.

![](images/8514c18ce768f353d47784cfea6d454ff43f61e0676b969fd23df1e0a96cf6d9.webp)

b. When replacing the four-in-one sensor with a new one, do not touch the silicone part of the sensor with hands or other objects to ensure that the silicone is clean.
c. When replacing the four-in-one sensor with a new one, do not touch the humidity sensing area of the sensor with hands or other objects to avoid causing damage.

d. When installing the four-in-one sensor, align the sensor with its mounting position, move the sensor close to the glass, and press and hold the middle part of the sensor with fingers to ensure that the silicone of the sensor is completely attached to the glass.

e. Press down the elastic sheets of the sensor, lock the elastic sheet on one side and then press that on the other side for locking. After installation, check that the sensor is installed in place.
f. Observe the sensor from the outside of the front windscreen to ensure that the sensor is completely attached to the glass without bubbles. If there are any bubbles, remove and install the sensor again according to the steps mentioned above.
g. The connector should be installed in place.
h. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the automatic wiping, automatic defrosting of front windscreen, automatic lighting and automatic air conditioning functions are normal.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the engine trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Engine trimming panel assembly
2. Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Refer to: Disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery)
3. Remove the lower left shield assembly of dashboard. Refer to: Lower left shield assembly of dashboard

4. Remove integrated vehicle body controller

![](images/b8deb603f971fd5b2ff7c39eadb45b100218d76a8a9fb908e243e9ef29063180.webp)

a. Remove one fixing nut A and disconnect the anode wire in the dashboard distribution box. Torque: 9 N•m
b. Remove one fixing bolt B and one fixing nut C, and move away the dashboard distribution box. Torque: 9 N•m

c. Disconnect the 11 connectors, remove the 3 fixing nuts and remove the integrated vehicle body controller. Torque: 9 N•m

### Installation procedures

1. Install the integrated vehicle body controller in an order reverse to its removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, disconnect the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and reconnect.
c. Perform intelligent key matching. Refer to: Intelligent key matching
d. Perform NFC key card matching. Refer to: NFC card matching
e. Read and clear the DTC.

### 5.17.1.1 Warnings and precautions

1. The detection function of a sensor may not work properly in any of the following conditions:

a. Mud or snow clings to the sensor (the sensor function returns to normal after the foreign matter is removed by directly using water jet)
b. The sensor is blocked by other objects.
c. When the exterior temperature is low, a fault of the sensor is caused by sensor icing, etc.

2. The detection range of the sensor may change in the following conditions:

a. Mud or snow clings to the sensor (the sensor function returns to normal after the foreign matter is removed by directly using water jet) b. The vehicle is exposed to sunshine or ultra-low temperature environment.

3. A sensor may produce false detection results in any of the following conditions:

a. The vehicle is on a bumpy road, gravelly road or on grassland.
b. There is ultrasonic noise in the same frequency, such as metal noise, high-pressure gas emission noise, vehicle horn sounding against the sensor, etc.
c. The vehicle is in a heavy rain or splashed with water.
d. The vehicle tilts at a large angle.
e. Mud or snow clings to the sensor.
f. The vehicle is provided with a towing hook.
gh. TAhneotvhehricvlehisc lreunwnitihn sensors is approaching. g on a high or right-angle curb.

4. A sensor may not detect the following obstacles due to their shapes, characteristics or materials: a. Thread-like objects such as wiring or ropes. b. Objects liable to absorb sound such as cotton or snow. c. Objects with sharp edges. d. Objects at too low positions. e. Objects at too high positions or with upper projections. f. Objects when the sensor suffers a strong impact or collision; g. When the vehicle is too close to steps, its system cannot correctly measure the distance from the bottom step.

5. No disposal of sensors a. Neither touch-up paint nor overall painting is allowed.

### 6. Sensor cleaning

a. Do not have high-pressure water or steam come into direct contact with the sensors when washing the vehicle, as doing so may damage them.

7. As sensors are precision wearing parts, bumping and scratching of them should be avoided during maintenance.

### 5.17.1.2 System descriptions

1. The parking assistant system of vehicle is a vehicular monitoring system developed by applying the detection principle used by bats in flight. Several sensors are installed at the rear and front of a vehicle to transmit and receive signals and provide feedback information to a controller; the controller calculates the distance from the vehicle to an obstacle based on the turn-back time and triggers different sounds and indicator alarms based on the distance to alert a driver of the distance between the obstacle and the vehicle. This increases the reversing and parking convenience and safety;

2. Sensor position and detection range

![](images/9adc85d7abb370dfaecff1204d2e8af63b9bb5293886baed390b69ec7d9e1b46.webp)

### 3. Sensor alarm working state

![](images/8ca6920c76e7f45bed0f074bfc744b0db9165b370432d4baa7c1d7297618557c.webp)

4. When driving at speeds below 10 km/h with the Park Assist System on, a beep will be heard if the sensor detects an obstacle within its range.

5. Beeping becomes faster as the vehicle moves closer to the obstacle. When the distance is within about 0.3m, the beeper sounds at a constant tone. At this point, stop the vehicle to avoid collision.

### Removal procedures

1. Remove the front left/right compartment trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front compartment trimming panel assembly
2. Remove the grille upper cover assembly. Refer to: Grille upper cover assembly
3. Remove the front left/right wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Front wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly
4. Remove the front bumper assembly. Refer to: Front bumper assembly
5. Remove the sensor (front bumper).

![](images/7e1bd88e6b15f02b178f4b3fe8103b878ef245d5255c9dfc1252492b981d1b77.webp)

a. Disconnect the connector, release the clip tongue and remove the sensor (front bumper).

### 0 Tip:

A total of 4 sensors are installed on the front bumper. The two sensors in the middle are under the energy-absorbing foam of the front bumper, and they can be removed by lifting the energy-absorbing foam a little. The sensor connector has a secondary lock structure.

### Installation procedures

1. Install the sensors (front bumper) in an order reverse to their removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the sensors (front bumper) can work properly.

### 0 Tip:

A total of 4 sensors are installed on the rear bumper. The 2 sensors on the left and right sides can be directly removed after the vehicle is lifted up, while the 2 sensors in the middle can be removed only after removal of the rear bumper.
Remove the rear bumper assembly based on actual needs.

1. Remove the rear left/right combination light assembly. Refer to: Rear combination light assembly

2. Remove the rear left/right wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly. Refer to: Rear wheel eyebrow trimming panel assembly

3. Remove the rear bumper assembly. Refer to: Rear bumper assembly
4. Remove the sensor (rear bumper).

![](images/b7683840072166ae7947f2ee5388bb19bb0b47c6a42408d7ef5d2a7b84a5344b.webp)

a. Disconnect the connector, release the clip tongues, and remove the sensors (rear bumper) (on both sides).

### 0 Tip:

The sensor connector has a secondary lock structure.

![](images/0db7bc5e3f5df7ead85a893d80468539025599100aad94ecffc15e0e8780f72a.webp)

b. Remove the rear bumper and then remove the sensor (rear bumper) (in the middle).

### Installation procedures

1. Install the sensors (rear bumper) in an order reverse to their removal and pay attention to the following:

a. The connector should be installed in place.
b. After installation, start the vehicle and check that the sensors (rear bumper) can work properly.

### 5.18.3.1 Warnings and precautions

1. Important warnings for 12V battery (starter Fe battery)

A Warning: When removing the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) terminals, make sure to remove the negative terminal first. If the positive terminal makes contact with any metal in the surrounding area during removal, there may be sparks and even fire, as well as a high risk of electric shock, resulting in serious or even life threatening injury. Turn off all electrical equipment on the vehicle before turning on the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) again. First connect the positive terminal and then the negative. Do not install the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) in the wrong order, as this may cause fire. The 12V battery (starter Fe battery) should be kept away from heat sources and open flames, and it should be well-ventilated when charged and used. Failure to do so may result in fire or personal injury. The 12V battery (starter Fe battery) has a built-in power manager. Do not disassemble or repair the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) without authorisation, so as to avoid damage or personal injury.

2. Important precautions for 12V battery (starter Fe battery)

### i Caution:

Regularly check the surface of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) and the positive and negative terminals to ensure they are not loose or rusted.
Scrapped 12V battery (starter Fe battery) should be subject to centralised treatment. Please recycle the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) according to local laws and regulations to prevent causing harm to the environment.
The 12V battery (starter Fe battery) must be replaced with another of the same model and specification.
Avoid Fe battery overcharging or long-term power loss .
Avoid long-term heavy-current discharge of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).
The 12V battery (starter Fe battery) should be firmly installed on the vehicle to avoid vibration.
Oxides and sulfates generated by fixing clips of 12V battery (starter Fe battery) terminals must be cleaned quickly, and grease should be applied to avoid corrosion reincidence. Do not charge the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) separately with a charger.
12V battery (starter Fe battery) can be used normally only after communicating with the vehicle. Make sure to connect and harness it correctly.
When cleaning the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), make sure to prevent any liquid from entering.
The 12V battery (starter Fe battery) has a built-in relay, and it is normal for the relay to pull in when starting the vehicle.
Avoid bumping against the 12V battery (starter Fe battery). Once the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) cracks, it needs to be stopped from being used and properly recycled.
Turn off all electrical appliances and power off the vehicle before disconnecting the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery).
When repairing the SRS, do not proceed with the next operation until the cathode of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) has been disconnected for at least 90s.

### 5.18.3.2 System descriptions

1. The Tang EV equipped with a starter Fe battery as its 12V battery， there are four pouch cells integrated and equipped with separate Battery management system which is connected with vehicle CAN-BUS communication.

2. It mainly provides power for low-voltage electrical appliances.

3. Intelligent charging function: In order to avoid power loss of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery), the battery thermal management system will activate to charge the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) when the following conditions are all met simultaneously:

a. The hood is closed.
b. The vehicle is powered off.
c. Battery is allowed to discharge (SOC＞10%).
d. The voltage of the 12V battery (starter Fe battery) is below 12.8V.
