### 1. Warnings for paint preparation and painting operation

a. The diffuse solvent will cause serious respiratory diseases during paint preparation and painting operation. It must be operated in strict accordance with the instructions of paint, equipment and safety device manufacturers. b. Be sure to wear special personal protective equipment, such as gas masks, anti-static clothing, goggles and gloves, to prevent injury when performing this procedure.

### 2. Precautions for paint preparation and painting operation

a. Do not mix paint systems or substitute products from different manufacturers. Mixing incompatible products will cause the following phenomena: Delamination of primer Poor adhesion between coatings . Poor curing Lower luster Poor color accuracy Coating damage (pits, bubbles, orange peel, loss of luster).
b. The color masterbatch must be stored and mixed in plastic containers that do not contain release agents.
c. The prepared color masterbatch should be thoroughly stirred before use.
d. Pigments must be judged by spraying test plates for color comparison.
e. The test plate for spraying must be aluminum plate or iron plate sprayed with primer and completely wrapped.
f. Pay attention to keeping the electronic scale clean and avoid placing it in a place prone to vibration or interference by airflow.

### 3. Precautions for maintenance and repair of finish varnish

a. Avoid washing the vehicle in direct sunlight.
b. Avoid using strong soaps and chemical detergents.
c. Use brushless automatic car cleaning equipment.
d. Avoid using products containing acid and alkali.
e. Do not use brushes or brooms to remove snow or ice.
f. Be sure to wipe off the remaining rinse water immediately after thorough cleaning, and do not dry it on the surface. It is recommended to wipe off with soft oil-tanned leather.
g. The vehicle should be polished only when the defects on the surface can be eliminated by polishing.
h. Avoid removing too much transparent paint, otherwise it will cause premature damage to the paint.
i. Use the electric polishing equipment in strict accordance with the requirements recommended by the polishing manufacturer. Never use wax or silicone products to cover vortex marks (the marks will reappear soon and make users dissatisfied).

### 4. Precautions for anti-corrosion treatment

a. When spraying sound insulation or anti-corrosion materials, precautions must be taken to avoid spraying them into component openings (such as door locks, window lifting slots,

window regulators and seat belt retractors) and any moving or rotating parts. After spraying the material, make sure that all the relief holes of the vehicle body are open.
b. The foamed sound insulation materials at the maintenance parts must be removed when repairing the vehicle body with open flame. Avoid inhaling harmful dust when reinstalling the sound insulation materials.
c. Be sure to wear special goggles and gloves when performing this procedure.
d. When the vehicle leaves the factory, all metal plates of the vehicle body have been subjected to electrophoretic coating primer treatment. After overhaul and replacement of parts, all exposed metal surfaces must be treated with anti-rust primer.
e. If the original coating or anti-corrosion material is burned during welding or heating operation, cleaning and re-anticorrosion treatment are required.
f. During maintenance after collision, the metal will be exposed. These surfaces must be repainted with special anti-corrosion materials.
g. The sealant can prevent water and dust from entering the vehicle, and also has an anticorrosion effect. Original sealed joints are obvious. If these seals are damaged, they should be corrected by resealing. The joint of the newly replaced plate should be resealed. Sealant used must remain flexible after curing and painting. Open joints sealed with sealant should be filled with high consistency filler. Follow the instructions for the selected material.
h. Sound insulation materials can control the general noise level inside the car. When the sound insulation layer is damaged due to maintenance operation or replacement of new panels, it muse be replaced with the same material.

### 1. Paint

a. Paint is a kind of mixed liquid that can be coated on various substrates. After the paint dries, a solid paint film is formed to protect the substrates and beautify the appearance. b. The vehicle has been sprayed with paint when leaving the factory to make it have good corrosion resistance and luster. c. The requirement of spraying paint is to restore the repaired parts to their original appearance. During maintenance, the painting process specified by the manufacturer must be strictly observed. Refer to: Paint spraying process for rigid surfaces

2. Main functions of electrophoretic primer

a. Rust prevention.
b. Improve adhesion.
c. Improve the limited fillibility.

3. Main functions of intermediate coat

a. Fillibility.
b. Insulation/tightness.
c. Foil colored paint.

4. Main functions of colored paint a. Add color. b. Give luster.

5. Main functions of transparent paint

a. Contain anti-ultraviolet materials, which can resist ultraviolet rays in sunlight.
b. Resist the corrosion of environmental dust (acid rain) on the top coat.
c. Make the top coat have friction resistance.
d. Give the top coat a better luster.

### 1. Please observe the following principles during daily maintenance of automobile top coat:

a. During maintenance of the vehicle, do not touch the top coat of vehicle body with greasy hand, or wipe the top coat with a piece of greasy wiping cloth at will. Do not place a greasy tool or wiping cloth containing organic solvent on the vehicle body. If found, wipe it clean in time to avoid any chemical reaction.
b. If there are scratches, indentations or peels on the top coat, timely repair is required.
c. To prevent causing color nonconformity or poor bonding, do not conduct secondary paint spraying if the top coat has no obvious scratches.
d. For long-time parking, the vehicle should be parked in the garage or at a well-ventilated place. In addition, the vehicle should be parked with special cover in winter. For temporary parking, the vehicle should be parked at a shady and cool place.
e. Prevent causing strong impact, bumping and scratches on paint film of the vehicle body.
f. Use high-quality detergent to clean trimmings on vehicle body. Do not apply wax forcefully.
g. Some special traces (of asphalt, bird droppings, insects, etc.) which are highly corrosive should be removed in time. Be sure to use special detergent to remove these traces. To prevent causing damage to the top coat, do not scrape these traces with a knife blade or remove them with gasoline.
h. Before, during or after using the vehicle, clear the dust on the vehicle body without delay to reduce dust adsorption due to static electricity of the vehicle body.
i. Wash the vehicle immediately after rainfall. As rain stains on the vehicle body shrink little by little after rainfall, the concentration of acid substances in rain stains will increase gradually. If these rain stains are not washed off by clean water, the top coat will be damaged after a long period of time.
j. Wash the vehicle after the drive motor gets cool down. Do not wash the vehicle under the burning sun or in a high-temperature environment, so as to prevent leaving any trace of detergent because of drying. Usually, when washing the vehicle by yourself, use special detergent instead of washing powder, soapy water or dishwashing liquid with high alkalinity, so as to prevent the removal of grease in the top coat and the premature aging of the top coat. When taking the vehicle to a washing station, make sure the staff will not use de-waxing detergent. It is recommended that vehicles travelling in coastal or heavily polluted areas are washed once a day.
k. Use a clean and soft cloth or sponge to clean the vehicle, and make sure there are no abrasive grains on them. To avoid scratches, do not use a dry cloth, dry towel or dry sponge to clean the vehicle. Wipe the vehicle along with the water flow direction and from top to bottom. Do not wipe the vehicle in a circular or transverse way.
l. Irregularly wax the top coat for protection and regularly maintain it (once a quarter) to recover the brightness and glossiness of the top coat of vehicle body. In addition, the protective film of automobile top coat can be pasted for protecting the top coat of body bumper, front cover, door and mirror. The top coat should be protected from being scratched by slight collision.

### 8.3.2.1 Examples and treatment methods for common defects of automobile top coat

![](images/d17fbdbf41fd8f4f58054c312fb79c600be32bfebe6143170f08377016dfdc02.webp)

![](images/0e0b0368ac8c70df63ad68e3eee0020bb193e5cab73cbb0348a336c9e91a839d.webp)

### 8.3.2.2 Examples of treatment process of common paint film defects

1. Examples of treatment process of common paint film defects:

a. Clean the surface to be polished with degreasing materials before polishing. b. First, fully wet the sponge polishing disc, squeeze out excess water, apply a small amount of wax polish on the top coat to be polished, and adjust the rotating speed of the polishing machine. c. Put the sponge polishing disc on the top coat, and then start the polishing machine at a speed of 2,500\~3,000 r/min, and then lightly press it for 3\~5s for polishing treatment.

i Caution: During operation, keep the machine moving smoothly and gently, and avoid taking too long, so as not to generate too much heat and damage the top coat.

d. Wipe off the excess wax polish with a piece of car cleaning cloth.

### 8.3.2.3 Examples of treatment process of common grinding and polishing treatment

1. Examples of treatment process of common grinding and polishing treatment:

a. Clean the surface to be polished with degreasing materials before polishing.
b. Apply a proper amount of polishing agent on the top coat to be polished, and adjust the rotating speed of the polishing machine.
c. Put the wool polishing disc on the top coat, and then start the polishing machine at a speed of 2,500\~3,000 r/min.

### A Caution:

During operation, keep the machine moving smoothly and gently, avoid excessive grinding, and ensure that the grinding time is as short as possible and the grinding area is as small as possible.

d. First, fully wet the sponge polishing disc, and squeeze out excess water; apply a small amount of wax polish on the top coat to be polished, put the sponge polishing disc on the top coat, and then start the polishing machine at a speed of 2,500\~3,000 r/min, and then lightly press it for 3\~5s for polishing treatment.

### i Caution:

During operation, keep the machine moving smoothly and gently, and avoid taking too long, so as not to generate too much heat and damage the top coat.

e. Wipe off the excess wax polish with a piece of car cleaning cloth.

### 8.3.2.4 Examples of treatment process of deep grinding and polishing treatment

1. Examples of treatment process of deep grinding and polishing treatment:

a. Grind the damaged top coat with #2000 waterproof sand paper, parallel and close to the top coat to be ground, and perform round grinding.
b. Remove grinding dust on the surface.
c. Apply a proper amount of polishing agent on the top coat to be polished, and adjust the rotating speed of the polishing machine.
d. Put the wool polishing disc on the top coat, and then start the polishing machine at a speed of 2,500\~3,000 r/min.

### i Caution:

Keep the machine moving smoothly and gently, avoid excessive grinding. Ensure that the grinding time is as short as possible (3\~5s) and the grinding area is as small as possible.

e. First, fully wet the sponge polishing disc, and squeeze out excess water; apply a small amount of wax polish on the top coat to be polished, put the sponge polishing disc on the top coat, and then start the polishing machine at a speed of 2,500\~3,000 r/min, and then lightly press it for 3\~5s for polishing treatment.

### i Caution:

During operation, keep the machine moving smoothly and gently, and avoid taking too long, so as not to generate too much heat and damage the top coat.

### 8.3.2.5 Paint spraying process for rigid surfaces

1. Paint spraying process for rigid surfaces:

0 Tip:

Take the fender as an example to explain the process of local painting (touch-up).

### i Caution:

All paint repairs on rigid surfaces must conform to factory standards.

Confirm the repair area and select the repair range, such as local repair, block repair and vehicle repair; In case of collision damage, perform the corresponding repair after the sheet metal repair according to the damage or spray paint after replacing the parts.

a. Fender scratches are serious, so local spraying (touch-up) process is adopted.

b. Grind the damaged top coat with ＃P500 wet (waterproof) sandpaper (round grinding).

c. Degrease and clean it with degreasing agent after grinding.

d. Apply primer during spraying, try to control the scope of primer spraying. The coating at the edge should be gradual and not stepped.

e. Perform flash drying for 4\~5min, and then drying for 20\~30min (temperature: 70℃\~80℃).

f. After drying, perform wet grinding with #P800\~1000 sandpaper.

g. Perform grinding with #P2000 fine (waterproof) sandpaper and expand the grinding range.

h. After grinding, use sticky gauze for dust removal before painting.

i. Spray primer.

Air pressure: 150\~200kPa Spraying distance: 200\~300mm

j. After flash drying for 2\~3min, spray the second primer until the joint position is no longer obvious.

k. Perform flash drying for 4\~5min, and then drying for 20\~30min.

l. After drying, use sticky gauze for dust removal before painting varnish.

m. Spray transparent paint, with a spraying range completely covering the primer range.

n. Perform flash drying for 2\~3min, and spray the second transparent paint, with a spraying range completely covering the range of the first transparent paint.

o. After spraying the transparent paint, immediately add the lapel water to the original transparent paint.

p. Spray diluted lapel water for 2\~3 times at the joint position.

q. Dry it in spray booth for 20\~30min (temperature: 70℃\~80℃).

### 0 Tip:

The paint spraying process for rigid surfaces after sheet metal repair is similar to that of the rigid surfaces, except that the following steps are added after the primer is ground and before the primer is sprayed:

a. Spray epoxy primer.
b. Scrap and coat the poly-putty.
c. Grind the poly-putty.
d. Blow dust, degrease and clean.
e. Scrap and coat fillers.
f. Sand the surface of old paint film.
g. Clean, degrease, and shield areas that are not painted.

### 8.3.2.7 Paint repair procedure of plastic parts

1. There are three basic requirements for paint repair on the surface of plastic parts:

a. Paint has a certain adhesion with plastic, without losing mechanical properties.
b. The paint film should be flexible enough to deform with the plastic without breaking.
c. The original particles and rough texture on the surface of some plastic parts can be reflected.

2. Top coat repair procedure of plastic parts surface:

a. The top coat repair of plastic parts surface can refer to the above-mentioned paint spraying process for rigid surfaces. Pay attention to the temperature of spray booth. Baking conditions: 70℃\~80℃, 20\~30min
